classes.name: Core\Arr
classes.summary:
`array<T>` is an insertion-ordered hash with copy-on-write value semantics
([ADR 0007 § 5](../decisions/0007.md)). Every member is pure (R3); an implementation
mutates in place whenever the argument's refcount is 1, so purity costs nothing. `T` is a type variable —
the stdlib is parametric where user code is not.

Every key is a `string`, so every key-valued **return** below is typed `string`; a key **parameter** is
`int|string`, matching the subscript normalisation of that same section. How arrays combine, and why no
member is named `merge`, is `rule:types/array-combination`.

doc.shortHtml: The direction Core\Arr::sort and sortByKey put elements in — spec § 2's {order: …} option, which is Asc when omitted.

cases.name: Asc
cases.descHtml: Smallest first — what an omitted {order: …} means.

cases.name: Desc
cases.descHtml: Largest first — rsort, arsort and krsort as one option rather than three names.

doc.shortHtml: Which part of an entry Core\Arr::diff and intersect compare — spec § 2's {on: …} option, which is Values when omitted; by and comparator apply to the part it selects.

cases.name: Values
cases.descHtml: The value alone — array_diff, array_intersect and their u forms.

cases.name: Keys
cases.descHtml: The key alone — array_diff_key, array_intersect_key and their u forms; a by here maps the key.

cases.name: Both
cases.descHtml: The key and the value together — array_diff_assoc, array_intersect_assoc and their u forms.

doc.shortHtml: Counts the entries in $a, as count and sizeof do.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to count.

doc.returnHtml: The number of entries; 0 for the empty array.

doc.shortHtml: Whether $a holds no entries — empty($a) and count($a) === 0 as one member.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to test.

doc.returnHtml: true for the empty array, false otherwise.

doc.shortHtml: Whether the keys are exactly "0", "1", … in that order, as array_is_list does.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to test.

doc.returnHtml: true for a list and for the empty array; false once any key is out of sequence or is not its index's exact decimal spelling.

doc.shortHtml: Whether $a holds an entry under $key, as array_key_exists does — and as isset($a[$k]) does, since a stored null still counts.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to look in.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key, an int or a string; 1 and "1" name one entry.

doc.returnHtml: true when the key is present, whatever value it holds.

doc.shortHtml: Whether some entry is $needle under strict identity, as in_array with strict: true does — there is no loose form.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The array to search.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The value to look for, compared by identity; int, uint, float and decimal are one numeric domain, so 1 finds 1.0.

doc.returnHtml: true at the first identical entry; false over the empty array.

doc.shortHtml: The key of the first entry that is $needle under strict identity, as array_search with strict: true does.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The array to search.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The value to look for, compared as contains compares.

doc.returnHtml: The key as a string, or null when no entry is identical — never false.

doc.shortHtml: Every key in insertion order, as array_keys does without its search argument.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array whose keys are wanted.

doc.returnHtml: A list of the keys as strings — "10" stays "10", never an int; the empty array for an empty subject.

doc.shortHtml: Every value in insertion order under fresh keys, as array_values does.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array whose values are wanted.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0".

doc.shortHtml: The first entry's value, as reset, current and $a[array_key_first($a)] answer it — with no internal pointer to move.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to read.

doc.returnHtml: The value, or null for the empty array — which a stored null in an array<?T> cannot be told from.

doc.shortHtml: The last entry's value, as end and $a[array_key_last($a)] answer it.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to read.

doc.returnHtml: The value, or null for the empty array — which a stored null in an array<?T> cannot be told from.

doc.shortHtml: The first entry's key, as array_key_first and key answer it.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to read.

doc.returnHtml: The key as a string, or null for the empty array.

doc.shortHtml: The last entry's key, as array_key_last answers it.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to read.

doc.returnHtml: The key as a string, or null for the empty array.

doc.shortHtml: The entries in one window of positions, as array_slice does; a position is ordinal, whatever the keys are.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to take from.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: Where the window opens; a negative offset counts back from the last entry, and one reaching past the first clamps to it.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many entries the window holds; a negative length stops that many short of the end, and null runs to the end.

params.name: preserveKeys
params.descHtml: Keep every entry's own key; the default discards every key, string keys included, and renumbers from "0".

doc.returnHtml: The window's entries; the empty array when the window closes before it opens.

doc.shortHtml: The array with one window of positions replaced by $replacement's values — what array_splice returns, never what it does by reference.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to edit.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: Where the window opens, on slice's sign rule; an offset at the end appends.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many entries the window holds, on slice's sign rule; 0 inserts at the position and null reaches the end.

params.name: replacement
params.descHtml: The values to put in the window's place; omitted, the window is simply removed.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0", kept entries and replacement alike.

doc.shortHtml: The entries in consecutive runs of $size, as array_chunk does; the last run is short when the count does not divide.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to split.

params.name: size
params.descHtml: How many entries each run holds; at least 1.

params.name: preserveKeys
params.descHtml: Keep each entry's own key inside its run; the default renumbers every run from "0".

doc.returnHtml: A list of runs; no runs at all for the empty array.

errors.descHtml: $size is 0.

doc.shortHtml: The array with every trailing value added after its last entry, as array_push does — $a[] = $v in expression position.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to extend.

params.name: values
params.descHtml: The values to add, in written order.

doc.returnHtml: The subject's entries under their own keys, then each value under the next free integer key — one past the largest present; the subject itself when no values are given.

doc.shortHtml: The trailing values, then the array's values, as array_unshift does.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to put them in front of.

params.name: values
params.descHtml: The values to put in front, in written order.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0" — every key is discarded, since a value put in front has no key of its own to take.

doc.shortHtml: Every entry but the first — what array_shift leaves behind, with first answering the element it removes.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to shorten.

doc.returnHtml: The remaining entries under their own keys, never renumbered; the empty array for a subject of one entry or none.

doc.shortHtml: Every entry but the last — what array_pop leaves behind, with last answering the element it removes.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to shorten.

doc.returnHtml: The remaining entries under their own keys, never renumbered; the empty array for a subject of one entry or none.

doc.shortHtml: Copies of $value in front until the array holds $size entries, as array_pad with a negative length does.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to pad.

params.name: size
params.descHtml: The length to reach; a subject already that long is not padded.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value every added entry holds.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0" — every key is discarded, padded or not.

errors.descHtml: The padded result is larger than any array this process could hold.

doc.shortHtml: Copies of $value after the last entry until the array holds $size entries, as array_pad with a positive length does.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to pad.

params.name: size
params.descHtml: The length to reach; a subject already that long is not padded.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value every added entry holds.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0" — every key is discarded, padded or not.

errors.descHtml: The padded result is larger than any array this process could hold.

doc.shortHtml: The entries in the opposite order, as array_reverse does.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to reverse.

params.name: preserveKeys
params.descHtml: Keep every entry's own key; the default discards every key, string keys included, and renumbers from "0".

doc.returnHtml: The same entries, last first.

doc.shortHtml: Every value made a key and every key made its value, as array_flip does.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to flip; every value is an int or a string, and 1 and "1" flip to one key.

doc.returnHtml: The old keys as string values under the old values as keys, in first-occurrence order; a repeated value keeps its first position and takes its last key.

members.name: flatten
members.replaces: one level of a hand-written recursive walk

doc.shortHtml: One level of nesting removed — every inner array's values in order, as a hand-written walk does.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: An array of arrays.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0"; the inner keys are discarded, since two inner arrays can share one.

members.name: flattenDeep
members.replaces: `iterator_to_array` on a recursive iterator, a hand-written recursive walk

doc.shortHtml: Every level of nesting removed, as a recursive walk or iterator_to_array over a RecursiveIteratorIterator does; there is no depth count, since flatten is the other real case.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: An array nested to any depth.

doc.returnHtml: A list of every non-array leaf in walk order, renumbered from "0"; mixed because the depth is the caller's data, not the type's.

doc.shortHtml: $count copies of $value under "0", "1", …, as array_fill does from index zero; there is no start index, since fillKeys takes the keys a caller wants.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: How many entries; 0 yields the empty array.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value every entry holds.

doc.returnHtml: A list of $count entries.

errors.descHtml: $count names a result larger than any array this process could hold.

doc.shortHtml: $value stored under every key in $keys, as array_fill_keys does.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The keys to store under, as the array's values — each an int or a string; its own keys are ignored.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value every entry holds.

doc.returnHtml: One entry per distinct key, in first-occurrence order; 1 and "1" are one key.

doc.shortHtml: The integers from $start to $end inclusive, as range does; the direction is the bounds', so $start > $end counts down.

params.name: start
params.descHtml: The first value.

params.name: end
params.descHtml: The last value that may appear; a step that overshoots stops at the last in-range value.

params.name: step
params.descHtml: The distance between neighbours, 1 by default; always positive, since the direction comes from the bounds.

doc.returnHtml: A list from $start towards $end; one entry when the two are equal.

errors.descHtml: step is 0 or negative.

doc.shortHtml: $values' entries stored under $keys' entries, paired in order, as array_combine does.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The keys, as the array's values — each an int or a string; its own keys are ignored.

params.name: values
params.descHtml: The values, in the same order; its own keys are ignored.

doc.returnHtml: One entry per pair, in $keys' order; a repeated key keeps its first position and takes its last value, and 1 and "1" are one key.

errors.descHtml: The two arrays hold different numbers of entries.

doc.shortHtml: A sequence materialised as an array, as iterator_to_array does with preserve_keys: false — an Iterable<T>, an Iterator<T> or an array, whatever foreach would take.

params.name: items
params.descHtml: The sequence to drain, once.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: Stop the drive after this many elements — the only guard against an unbounded generator; the default takes everything, and 0 takes nothing.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0" — a cursor has no keys, and an array's are discarded.

doc.shortHtml: One named cell out of every row, as array_column does.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The rows, each an array.

params.name: column
params.descHtml: The key of the cell to take; 0 and "0" name one cell, as $row[0] and $row["0"] do.

params.name: indexBy
params.descHtml: The key of the cell to key the result by; the default gives the result fresh integer keys.

doc.returnHtml: The cells in row order: a row without the column is skipped, a row without the indexBy cell lands under the next free integer key, and two rows with one indexBy value collapse to the last.

doc.shortHtml: $base with every layer's entries written over it, the right-hand value winning, as array_replace does — and as array_merge over maps does, with every key treated alike.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The array underneath.

params.name: layers
params.descHtml: The arrays laid over it, in order; a later layer wins over an earlier one.

doc.returnHtml: Every key of every argument: an existing key keeps its position and takes the last value written under it, a new one is appended.

doc.shortHtml: overlay recursing wherever both sides of a key hold an array and neither is a list, as array_replace_recursive does; a list is replaced wholesale.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The array underneath.

params.name: layers
params.descHtml: The arrays laid over it, in order; a later layer wins over an earlier one.

doc.returnHtml: Every key of every argument, as overlay answers it, with two maps under one key combined the same way rather than the right one winning.

doc.shortHtml: $base with every layer's entries written underneath it, the left-hand value winning — PHP's array + array, which does not compile here.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The array on top.

params.name: layers
params.descHtml: The arrays laid under it, in order; an earlier one wins over a later one.

doc.returnHtml: $base's entries in their own positions, then each layer's keys not yet present, appended in order.

doc.shortHtml: Every value of $a, then of each of $others, under fresh keys — array_merge over lists, and the array_merge(...$arrays) idiom.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first array.

params.name: others
params.descHtml: The arrays whose values follow, in order.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0"; every key is discarded.

members.name: diff
members.signature: diff(array<T> $a, array<T> $b, {on?: SetOn, by?: callable, comparator?: callable}): array<T>

doc.shortHtml: The entries of $a that $b does not have, under strict identity — array_diff, array_diff_key, array_diff_assoc and their three u variants as one member.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array whose entries are kept.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The array whose entries exclude.

params.name: on
params.descHtml: Which part of an entry is compared: SetOn::Values (the default), SetOn::Keys or SetOn::Both.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: Called once per entry as ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters; what it answers stands in for the part on selected — the key, under SetOn::Keys.

params.name: comparator
params.descHtml: Called as ($a, $b) on two selected parts and answering a negative, zero or positive number, as array_udiff's callback does; it replaces identity, and makes the walk pairwise.

doc.returnHtml: The kept entries of $a under their own keys, in $a's order.

errors.descHtml: The comparator answered NaN.

members.name: intersect
members.signature: intersect(array<T> $a, array<T> $b, {on?: SetOn, by?: callable, comparator?: callable}): array<T>

doc.shortHtml: The entries of $a that $b also has, under strict identity — array_intersect and its five variants as one member.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array whose entries are kept.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The array an entry must also be in.

params.name: on
params.descHtml: Which part of an entry is compared: SetOn::Values (the default), SetOn::Keys or SetOn::Both.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: Called once per entry as ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters; what it answers stands in for the part on selected — the key, under SetOn::Keys.

params.name: comparator
params.descHtml: Called as ($a, $b) on two selected parts and answering a negative, zero or positive number, as array_uintersect's callback does; it replaces identity, and makes the walk pairwise.

doc.returnHtml: The kept entries of $a under their own keys, in $a's order.

errors.descHtml: The comparator answered NaN.

doc.shortHtml: The entries whose value has not been seen before, as array_unique does — by strict identity, so 1 and "1" are two entries, never SORT_STRING's cast.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to deduplicate.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: Called once per entry as ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters; identity is asked of what it answers, while the entry kept is still the entry.

doc.returnHtml: The first occurrence of each value, under its own key and in its own position.

doc.shortHtml: How many entries fall under each distinct value, as array_count_values does — or under each answer of by, the group-and-count loop PHP has no function for.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to count over.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: Called once per entry as ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters; it answers the bucket's name, an int or a string. Without it the value itself is the bucket.

doc.returnHtml: One uint per distinct bucket, keyed by it in first-occurrence order; 1 and "1" are one bucket.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces every value with what $fn answers for it, as array_map does over one array; keys are preserved.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to map.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters; its return type is the result's U.

doc.returnHtml: One entry per entry of $a, under the same key, holding the callback's answer.

doc.shortHtml: Stores every value under the key $fn answers for it — the keyBy idiom, and array_combine(array_map(…), …) as one member.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to re-key.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters; it answers the entry's new key, an int or a string.

doc.returnHtml: The values under their new keys, in first-occurrence order; two entries given one key collapse to the last, and 1 and "1" are one key.

doc.shortHtml: Keeps the entries $predicate answers truthily for, as array_filter does — with both of its flags folded in, since the callback receives ($value, $key) and may declare fewer parameters.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to filter.

params.name: predicate
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry; a truthy answer keeps the entry, on the same truthiness table if reads.

doc.returnHtml: The kept entries under their own keys, never renumbered; an empty array when nothing passes.

members.name: reduce
members.signature: reduce(array<T> $a, callable(U, T, string): U $fn, U $initial): U

doc.shortHtml: Folds the entries into one value from $initial, as array_reduce does; the callback receives ($carry, $value, $key) and may declare fewer parameters.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to fold.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: Called as ($carry, $value, $key) per entry, answering the next carry.

params.name: initial
params.descHtml: The seed, whose type is the fold's U and therefore the result's.

doc.returnHtml: The last carry; $initial itself over an empty array, with no call made.

doc.shortHtml: The first value $predicate answers truthily for, as array_find does; the walk stops at the match.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to search.

params.name: predicate
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters.

doc.returnHtml: The matching value, or null when nothing matches — which a stored null in an array<?T> cannot be told from.

doc.shortHtml: The key of the first entry $predicate answers truthily for, as array_find_key does; the walk stops at the match.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to search.

params.name: predicate
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters.

doc.returnHtml: The key as a string, whatever it was written as; null when nothing matches.

doc.shortHtml: Whether at least one entry satisfies $predicate, as array_any does; the walk stops at the first match.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to test.

params.name: predicate
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters.

doc.returnHtml: true at the first truthy answer; false over the empty array.

doc.shortHtml: Whether every entry satisfies $predicate, as array_all does; the walk stops at the first failure.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to test.

params.name: predicate
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters.

doc.returnHtml: false at the first falsy answer; true over the empty array.

members.name: groupBy
members.replaces: nothing — the most-written PHP userland helper

doc.shortHtml: Partitions the entries into buckets named by what $key answers for each — the group-by loop PHP has no function for.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to partition.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters; it answers the bucket's name, an int or a string.

doc.returnHtml: One inner array per distinct answer, in first-occurrence order, each keeping its entries under their own keys; 1 and "1" name one bucket.

doc.shortHtml: The entries added up, as array_sum does, promoting entry by entry: int with int stays int, a float anywhere makes the total float, a decimal anywhere makes it decimal.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The numbers to add.

doc.returnHtml: The total, of the widest type met; 0 as an int for the empty array.

errors.descHtml: The running int or decimal total leaves its type's range — there is no silent promotion to float — or a float and a decimal meet in one array, which have no common type.

doc.shortHtml: The entries multiplied together, as array_product does, promoting entry by entry exactly as sum does.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The numbers to multiply.

doc.returnHtml: The product, of the widest type met; 1 as an int for the empty array.

errors.descHtml: The running int or decimal product leaves its type's range — there is no silent promotion to float — or a float and a decimal meet in one array, which have no common type.

doc.shortHtml: The entries' mean — array_sum($a) / count($a) with the empty case answered.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The numbers to average.

doc.returnHtml: A decimal when the total is one — exact, rounded half to even at the widest scale the quotient admits — and a float otherwise; null for the empty array.

errors.descHtml: The running total leaves its type's range or meets a float and a decimal in one array, as sum throws; or a decimal quotient falls outside what a decimal can hold.

doc.shortHtml: The smallest entry under the natural order, as min with an array argument does — the order sort uses without a comparator, never PHP's loose comparison.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to search.

doc.returnHtml: The smallest value, the first of equals; null for the empty array. Two strings compare bytewise, so min(["1e2", "50"]) is "1e2".

errors.descHtml: Two entries have no natural order between them — an int against a string, or any object.

doc.shortHtml: The largest entry under the natural order, as max with an array argument does — the order sort uses without a comparator, never PHP's loose comparison.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to search.

doc.returnHtml: The largest value, the first of equals; null for the empty array. Two strings compare bytewise, so max(["1e2", "50"]) is "50".

errors.descHtml: Two entries have no natural order between them — an int against a string, or any object.

members.name: sort
members.signature: sort(array<T> $a, {by?: callable, order?: Order, comparator?: callable, preserveKeys?: bool}): array<T>

doc.shortHtml: The entries in order, stably — sort, rsort, asort, arsort, usort, uasort, natsort, natcasesort and array_multisort as one member and four options.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to sort.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: Called once per entry as ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters; what it answers is compared in the entry's place.

params.name: order
params.descHtml: Order::Asc (the default) or Order::Desc, which reverses the comparison rather than the result, so equal entries keep their relative order either way.

params.name: comparator
params.descHtml: Called as ($a, $b) on two values — or on two by answers — and answering a negative, zero or positive number, as usort's callback does; it replaces the natural order.

params.name: preserveKeys
params.descHtml: Keep each entry's own key, as asort does; the default renumbers from "0", as sort does.

doc.returnHtml: The sorted entries. The natural order is between two numbers, two strings bytewise, two bools or two nulls — "10" sorts before "9" — and nothing else.

errors.descHtml: Two entries have no natural order between them — an int against a string, or any object — and no comparator was given; or the comparator answered NaN.

doc.shortHtml: The entries in key order, stably, every key kept — ksort, krsort and uksort as one member.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to sort.

params.name: order
params.descHtml: Order::Asc (the default) or Order::Desc, which reverses the comparison rather than the result, so equal keys keep their insertion order either way.

params.name: comparator
params.descHtml: Called as ($a, $b) on two keys, both strings, and answering a negative, zero or positive number, as uksort's callback does; it replaces the natural order.

doc.returnHtml: The same entries under the same keys, ordered by key; the natural order is bytewise, so "10" precedes "9".

errors.descHtml: The comparator answered NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Reads $a as the type T written at the call site — an inline shape, {name: T}, or a class carrying #[Json\Derive] — converting each named field with as and leaving every key the type does not name behind; write array<T> to read a list of them instead.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The loose values to read: a form, a query string, a decoded document, or an array a program built.

doc.returnHtml: A new T whose every field is the declared type, or — for an array<T> — one per entry, in the array's own order.

errors.descHtml: A field T requires is absent, or holds a value as refuses for its declared type. Every field that failed is one issue on the error, at its own dotted path, so a form shows the whole list rather than the first item of it.
T is a class that carries no #[Json\Derive], so there is no field list to read $a against.

classes.summaryHtml:
array<T> is an insertion-ordered hash with copy-on-write value semantics (ADR 0007 § 5). Every member is pure (R3); an implementation mutates in place whenever the argument's refcount is 1, so purity costs nothing. T is a type variable — the stdlib is parametric where user code is not.

Every key is a string, so every key-valued return below is typed string; a key parameter is int|string, matching the subscript normalisation of that same section. How arrays combine, and why no member is named merge, is rule:types/array-combination.

classes.name: Core\Ast
classes.surface: `parse(string): Node` returning inert typed data

doc.shortHtml: Parses $source with the compiler's own parser and answers the file's node tree. Replaces token_get_all and every userland parser over it.

params.name: source
params.descHtml: Novis source, starting outside <?nvs the way a file does.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the one attribute on $target, or on its member $member, whose payload object matches the shape T written at the call site. nvs check finds it and replaces the call with the result, so nothing runs.

params.name: target
params.descHtml: The declaration whose attributes are read — a class or function reference.

params.name: member
params.descHtml: The name of a member of $target to read instead of $target itself; the empty string, which is the default, means the target.

doc.returnHtml: The payload object of the matching attribute, as T. The result is null when no attribute matches T. When more than one matches, the code does not compile, and the error names all<T> as the fix. A payload matches when it has at least the fields of T. So the empty shape {} matches every attribute, and a marker type with no fields gives that compile error when the target has a second attribute.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every attribute on $target, or on its member $member, whose payload object matches the shape T written at the call site. nvs check finds them and replaces the call with the result, so nothing runs.

params.name: target

params.name: member
params.descHtml: The name of a member of $target to read instead of $target itself; the empty string, which is the default, means the target.

doc.returnHtml: An array<T> of the matching payload objects, in the order they are declared. It is empty when no attribute matches T. A payload matches when it has at least the fields of T, so the empty shape {} matches every attribute.

classes.name: Core\Budget
classes.surface: `memoryHeld(): int`, `memoryPeak(): int`, `memoryLimit(): int` — this request's held bytes, its high-water mark and the ceiling both are measured against. Three members and no `$real_usage` boolean; an uncapped request answers `0` from `memoryLimit`. Replaces `memory_get_usage` and `memory_get_peak_usage`

doc.shortHtml: The bytes this request holds right now — what memory_get_usage was reaching for, with no $real_usage boolean. It falls as values die, because Novis releases on the last reference rather than at the end of the script, so a request that has finished with a large payload reads small again.
doc.returnHtml: This request's held bytes. Never the process's — that is Core\Os::residentBytes, and it is a different question.

doc.shortHtml: The highest memoryHeld() has been during this request — memory_get_peak_usage. The runtime records the mark as it allocates rather than deriving it from a reading, so a spike that has already been released is still reported.
doc.returnHtml: This request's high-water mark in bytes, never below what memoryHeld() answers. It cannot be reset: the number the request-level notices exist to surface is not one an application may put back.

doc.shortHtml: The ceiling memoryHeld() and memoryPeak() are measured against — [limits] memory as a byte count, less whatever is reserved for the limit handler. It is here so that a peak has a scale without every call site parsing Core\Config::get('limits.memory') and its suffix.
doc.returnHtml: The ceiling in bytes, or 0 for a request under no cap at all — the same reading of zero the runtime's own limit check uses, not a second spelling for it.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $values as the octets $format describes, as pack does, over a closed code table: a/A/Z a buffer NUL-padded, space-padded, or NUL-padded and NUL-terminated; c/C one octet; n/v, N/V and J/P 16, 32 and 64 bits most or least significant octet first; G/g binary32 and E/e binary64 the same way; x one NUL octet. A bare code takes the whole argument, never one octet, and an integer field takes the union of its width's signed and unsigned ranges in two's complement.

params.name: format
params.descHtml: The format string. It must be written directly in the code. Each code may be followed by a count or *: how many arguments a numeric field takes, and how many octets wide a buffer field is.

params.name: values
params.descHtml: The values written, one per numeric field and one buffer per buffer field; an integer field takes an int or a uint, a float field a float, and nothing is converted.

doc.returnHtml: The packed buffer.

errors.descHtml: $format holds a code outside the table — the machine-width codes s, S, i, I, l, L, q, Q, f and d, the hex codes h and H, and the cursor codes X and @ are refused naming the replacement — or x*, or a count larger than any buffer; a field's value is missing, of the wrong type, outside its width's range, a float outside binary32's range, or a buffer wider than its field; or the format writes fewer values than the call passed.

doc.shortHtml: Reads $b back through $format, as unpack does, over pack's code table in reverse — so unpack(pack($f, ...$v), $f) is $v, field for field. Octets the format does not describe throw rather than being ignored.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The buffer read.

params.name: format
params.descHtml: The same format string pack takes, an intrinsic and a sink; there is no second grammar for field names.

doc.returnHtml: The fields as a positional list, never PHP's name-keyed map: an int for c, a uint for every other integer code, a float for G/g/E/e, and a bytes for a buffer code with A's and Z's padding taken back off.

errors.descHtml: $format holds a code outside the table or a count larger than any buffer, a field reads past the end of $b, or octets are left over after the last field.

classes.name: Core\Cache
classes.surface: `local(): Cache\Store`, `process(): Cache\Store`, `shared(): Cache\Store` — a member per tier, none of them taking an argument. `process()` is one store per serving process, coherent across its cores, in memory only and bounded by `[cache.process] max_size`. On the store: `put(string $key, mixed $value, {ttl?: Duration}): void` / `get(string $key): mixed` — copy-in/copy-out, and a miss answers `null` rather than throwing — plus `forget(string $key): void`, all three tiers gaining a lifetime and a `forget` together. A secret meets a cache only through `putSecret(string $key, secret string $value, Duration $ttl, array<secret bytes> $keys): void` and `getSecret(string $key, array<secret bytes> $keys, {fill?: callable(): Cache\SecretEntry, wait?: Duration}): ?secret string`, which store XChaCha20-Poly1305 **ciphertext** bound to the app, the entry's name and its expiry — so no `secret` crosses the boundary, `put` still refuses one and `get` answers `null` for a sealed entry. A sealed entry that does not open, under any key of the ring or past its sealed expiry, is a **miss**; on a miss `fill` runs in exactly one caller per process while every other waits for at most its `wait` (`[cache.process] fill_wait`) and then throws `TimeoutError`, a throwing `fill` releases the waiters with nothing, and an entry inside the last fifth of its lifetime is answered to everyone while one caller replaces it. `Cache\SecretEntry::of(secret string $value, Duration $ttl)` is what a `fill` answers. Sealing hides a secret from code that knows an entry's name but not the ring and keeps it out of the shared store in the clear; it does not protect it from a compromised process. Replaces `apcu_*`, `memcached` for the local case

doc.shortHtml: The per-core, in-process tier: a map in this core's own memory, with no lock, no network and no coherence between cores. A value one request writes may or may not be there when the next request asks, because the next request usually runs on another core with an empty map of its own.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Cache\Store over this core's own entries. Any entry may be absent at any time, for any reason, and a write on one core is not visible on another. The only read this tier promises is your own write back in the same request; a value every core should find wants process, and a program that would be incorrect on a null wants shared.

doc.shortHtml: The per-process tier: one store every core of this serving process shares, in memory only, and gone when the process ends. A follow-up request on the same machine finds what an earlier one wrote, whichever core it lands on, which is what local cannot promise; this is the tier for ordinary application caching.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Cache\Store over this process's own entries, which every core of it reads and writes behind a lock. Any entry may be absent at any time — for the cap, or because this is a different process than the one that wrote it — so a program that would be incorrect on a null wants shared instead.

doc.shortHtml: The coherent tier: a real store over the network, shared by every core and every machine that names it.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Cache\Store over the configured shared store, whose entries every core sees.

errors.descHtml: The capability cache.shared is not granted; or no [cache.shared] url is configured, or it is not a URL this client reads. Each is a deployment that was not configured rather than a store that failed.
The configured store cannot be reached — it throws rather than answering as though the entry were absent, since the two mean opposite things to whatever asked.

A secret meets a cache only through putSecret(string $key, secret string $value, Duration $ttl, array<secret bytes> $keys): void and getSecret(string $key, array<secret bytes> $keys, {fill?: callable(): Cache\SecretEntry, wait?: Duration}): ?secret string, which store XChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext bound to the app, the entry's name and its expiry — so no secret crosses the boundary, put still refuses one and get answers null for a sealed entry. A sealed entry that does not open, under any key of the ring or past its sealed expiry, is a miss; on a miss fill runs in exactly one caller per process while every other waits for at most its wait ([cache.process] fill_wait) and then throws TimeoutError, a throwing fill releases the waiters with nothing, and an entry inside the last fifth of its lifetime is answered to everyone while one caller replaces it. Cache\SecretEntry::of(secret string $value, Duration $ttl) is what a fill answers. Sealing hides a secret from code that knows an entry's name but not the ring and keeps it out of the shared store in the clear; it does not protect it from a compromised process. classes.name: Core\Cache\SecretEntry
classes.summary: A secret and how long it stays valid, such as a token and the time until it expires. The `fill` function of `getSecret` returns one.

doc.shortHtml: Builds the entry a getSecret fill answers with: the secret the fill fetched, and how long that secret stays good.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The secret to store. A plain string reaches this parameter too, and nothing is laundered either way — what makes the value confidential is its own type.

params.name: ttl
params.descHtml: How long the entry stays readable, counted from the write that stores it — what the fetch itself said, rather than a lifetime the caller guessed at.

doc.returnHtml: The entry. It answers nothing about either half: a program builds one for a fill to hand back, and reads a secret out of getSecret instead.

classes.summaryHtml: A secret and how long it stays valid, such as a token and the time until it expires. The fill function of getSecret returns one.

classes.name: Core\Cache\Store
classes.summary: One cache, from `Core\Cache`. It saves a copy of a value under a key and returns a copy when you read it. A change to the value after you save it does not change the cache.

doc.shortHtml: Copies $value into the store under $key, replacing whatever was there — a recursive graph copy, so the entry shares nothing with the request that wrote it.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name to store under; tainted is admitted, since no byte of it reaches any answer.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to copy in. It cannot be a callable or a secret, the same as for a value sent to an isolate.

params.name: ttl
params.descHtml: How long the entry stays readable, counted from this call. Omitted, it stays until the tier's cap forgets it or another put replaces it. A lifetime that has already run out forgets whatever was under the key and stores nothing.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A successful put is still no promise that a later get answers — see Core\Cache::local.

errors.descHtml: The value cannot cross: it is or contains a callable, or an object with a secret property that was not revealed.
On the shared tier only: the store cannot be reached or refused the write. The local tier has nothing to be unreachable.

doc.shortHtml: Copies the entry stored under $key back into this request, or answers null when there is none.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name to read; tainted is admitted, as it is on put.

doc.returnHtml: The value as it was copied in, or null — an entry may be absent at any time, for any reason, and on the local tier that is the contract rather than a failure.

errors.descHtml: The entry names a class this program cannot resolve — the same refusal Core\Serialize::decode makes, and the ordinary consequence of a deployment whose classes changed under a store that outlives them.
On the shared tier only: the store cannot be reached. An entry that is simply not there is null on either tier, which is the difference between a miss and a failure.

doc.shortHtml: Takes the entry under $key out of this store, whether or not there was one there.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name to forget; tainted is admitted, as it is on put.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A key nothing was stored under is already forgotten, so there is no second answer here for whether there had been an entry — the same reading get gives a miss, and for the same reason: on these tiers an entry may be absent at any time.

errors.descHtml: On the shared tier only: the store cannot be reached or refused the command. The in-process tiers have nothing to be unreachable.

members.name: putSecret
members.signature: putSecret(string $key, secret string $value, Core\Time\Duration $ttl, array<secret bytes> $keys): void

doc.shortHtml: Seals $value under the newest key of $keys and stores the ciphertext under $key — the only way a secret reaches a cache, and no secret value ever enters a tier.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name to store under; tainted is admitted, as it is on put. It is bound into the ciphertext, so the same entry moved to another name does not open.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The secret to store. A plain string reaches this parameter too, and nothing is laundered either way — what makes the value confidential is its own type.

params.name: ttl
params.descHtml: How long the secret stays readable, counted from this call. Required, where put's is optional: the lifetime is sealed into the entry as well as given to the tier, so an entry written back under a longer store lifetime is still past its own expiry.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The key ring, newest first, as Core\SignedCookie takes one. The newest key seals; every key opens, so a rotated ring reads what the retired one wrote.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. What sealing buys is that code which knows an entry's name but not the ring cannot read it, and that a tampered, moved or replayed entry is a miss — it does not protect a secret from a compromised process, which holds the ring in the same memory.

errors.descHtml: $keys is empty, or an entry of it is not a key of the construction's length. A ring that cannot key anything is the program's bug rather than a miss.
On the shared tier only: the store cannot be reached or refused the write, as on put.

members.name: getSecret
members.signature: getSecret(string $key, array<secret bytes> $keys, {fill?: callable(): Core\Cache\SecretEntry, wait?: Core\Time\Duration}): ?secret string

doc.shortHtml: Opens the secret stored under $key against every key of $keys, or answers null when there is none that opens.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name to read; the one putSecret wrote under, since the name is sealed in.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The key ring, newest first. Every key is tried, so an entry sealed under a key still in the ring opens after a rotation.

params.name: fill
params.descHtml: What supplies a miss: a callable answering a Core\Cache\SecretEntry, which carries both the secret it fetched and how long that secret stays good. Exactly one caller in this process runs it, in that caller's own request and under its own capabilities, while every other waits; a fill that throws releases the waiters with nothing and the next caller runs it again, so no failure crosses from one request into another.

params.name: wait
params.descHtml: How long this caller waits for another's fill, defaulting to [cache.process] fill_wait. There is no spelling for waiting forever.

doc.returnHtml: The secret, or null. A sealed entry that opens under no key of this ring, or whose own expiry has passed, is a miss like any other — never an error, so a rotated ring re-fetches rather than failing. A plain get on the same name is a miss too: the sealed door is the only door.

errors.descHtml: $keys is empty, or an entry of it is not a key of the construction's length — putSecret's refusal, unchanged. Also a fill that asks for the key it is filling, which would be a wait on itself.
Another caller in this process was still running fill when this call's wait was up, which defaults to [cache.process] fill_wait.
On the shared tier only: the store cannot be reached. An entry that is simply not there is null, as it is on get.

classes.summaryHtml: One cache, from Core\Cache. It saves a copy of a value under a key and returns a copy when you read it. A change to the value after you save it does not change the cache.

classes.name: Core\Cap
classes.surface: `has(string $capability): bool`, and nothing else. Reports whether the **calling namespace** holds a capability at this point in the request — the grant table narrowed by anything the request or an enclosing isolate already dropped. It is how a package that declared a capability *optional* degrades instead of failing a build, so the argument is a roster name and an unknown one is a compile error (`rule:security/optional-capability-degrades` and `rule:security/capability-roster-is-closed`). It grants nothing and needs no capability of its own; there is no `Core\Cap::drop`, because dropping a capability is `Core\Config::set` and stays there.

doc.shortHtml: Reports whether the code running here holds $capability at this point in the request — the deployment's grant table, narrowed by anything the request or an enclosing isolate already dropped. It grants nothing: the door the guarded branch reaches asks again for itself.

params.name: capability
params.descHtml: A capability name as nvs.toml grants it under — fs.read, net.connect. A written name outside that roster is a compile error, and a computed one that is not a capability answers false.

doc.returnHtml: true where the capability is granted for something, false otherwise. A true is not a promise about a particular path or host: a scoped grant still refuses an argument outside it, at the door.

classes.surfaceHtml: has(string $capability): bool, and nothing else. Reports whether the calling namespace holds a capability at this point in the request — the grant table narrowed by anything the request or an enclosing isolate already dropped. It is how a package that declared a capability optional degrades instead of failing a build, so the argument is a roster name and an unknown one is a compile error (rule:security/optional-capability-degrades and rule:security/capability-roster-is-closed). It grants nothing and needs no capability of its own; there is no Core\Cap::drop, because dropping a capability is Core\Config::set and stays there.

classes.name: Core\Cldr
classes.summary: Plural rules for many languages. They pick the word form for a count, such as "1 file" or "2 files", and for a position, such as "1st" or "2nd".

doc.shortHtml: Answers which of CLDR's plural forms $count selects in $locale, so a message catalog keys its variants on the locale's own rule rather than on == 1.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: The number the message is about. A decimal carries its scale, so 1.0 and 1 can select different forms where a locale reads the fraction; an int has none, and a float is read at the digits it prints.

params.name: locale
params.descHtml: A BCP 47 tag. Only the language subtag is read and case is ignored, so en-GB, en_US and EN all answer as en.

doc.returnHtml: The category the language's rules put $count in — Other for every count in a language that makes no plural distinction.

errors.descHtml: The tag carries no language subtag, or names a language whose rules are not among those compiled in — a locale is never given another language's rules.
$count is a float that is not finite, or one that prints more digits than the rules can be evaluated over.

doc.shortHtml: Answers which form $count takes as a place rather than as an amount — English's 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th — so a template writes the suffix its locale marks.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: The place the message is about. CLDR states its ordinal rules over whole numbers, so a count showing a fraction is outside all of them and answers Other — except in the two languages whose rules read the integer part alone, Macedonian and Georgian.

params.name: locale
params.descHtml: A BCP 47 tag, read exactly as pluralCategory reads it: only the language subtag, and case is ignored.

doc.returnHtml: The category the language's ordinal rules put $count in — Other for every count in a language that marks no ordinal form, which is most of them.

errors.descHtml: The tag carries no language subtag, or names a language neither table carries rules for. A language carried for cardinals but marking no ordinal form is not this case: it answers Other.
$count is a float that is not finite, or one that prints more digits than the rules can be evaluated over.

classes.summaryHtml: Plural rules for many languages. They pick the word form for a count, such as "1 file" or "2 files", and for a position, such as "1st" or "2nd".

classes.name: Core\Cli
classes.surface: the terminal surface, owned by `rule:tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink` — `arguments(): array<tainted string>`, `write`, `escape`, `isTty(Cli\Stream)`, `width`, `height`, `colorDepth`, `displayWidth`; the prompts `ask`, `confirm`, `select<T>`, `multiSelect<T>` and `secret(): secret tainted string`; and the scoped regions `live<T>` and `progress<T>`. Its value types are `Cli\Text` — built by `plain`/`styled`, composed with `+`, and read back by `text(): string` — `Cli\Style` and `Cli\Color`, its enums `Cli\Stream`, `Cli\ColorDepth` and `Cli\Shell`. Replaces `$argv`, `$argc`, `readline`, `mb_strwidth`, `posix_isatty`. **Terminal output is a `tainted` sink** that substitutes every control byte with a visible glyph; `Cli\Text` is the only thing that writes raw. The byte-and-line side of standard input is `Core\IO` (§ 14), not here; process exit is the `exit` keyword (`rule:statements/nvs-is-the-only-open-tag`).

doc.shortHtml: The words this program was started with, past the program itself — PHP's $argv and $argc in one place. A program that declares a #[Command] reads its arguments off the table Core\Command::run matched them against instead; this is the raw list, for a program that parses its own.
doc.returnHtml: An array<tainted string> in the order the shell wrote them, empty for a program started with none. Every element is tainted: the words came from outside the program's own text, so a path, a URL or a query built from one passes its own launderer first. The program's own name is not an element — nothing indexes it away, and $argv[0] has no spelling here.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $value to a standard stream, replacing fwrite(STDOUT, …) and print. A string has every control byte replaced by the visible glyph Core\Cli::escape gives it; a Core\Cli\Text is written through unchanged, because it is the sink's own carrier and its bytes have already been neutralized.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The text to write. A tainted one is written like any other — the substitution is what makes the terminal safe, so nothing has to be laundered first — while a secret one is refused at compile time.

params.name: stream
params.descHtml: Which standard stream to write to. Out when omitted; Err writes to this request's diagnostic channel, which a Core\Out::capture does not take. In throws.

params.name: newline
params.descHtml: Whether to append one LF after the value. false when omitted, so the member writes exactly what it was handed.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The bytes are on the stream, or the write failed and the request is over.

errors.descHtml: $stream is Core\Cli\Stream::In, which a program reads and never writes. The case exists for Core\Cli::isTty, which asks its question about all three.

doc.shortHtml: Answers $text with every control byte replaced by a visible, inert glyph — ESC as ␛, a bare CR as ␍, DEL as ␡, a C1 code point or an unterminated bidirectional control as � — while LF and TAB pass through. This is the terminal sink's own table as a value; echo already performs it, so a program needs this only to hold the neutralized form.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The text to neutralize. Its tainted qualifier is removed, because the terminal is the sink this launders for and nothing is left in the answer for it to act on.

doc.returnHtml: The same text with the substitutions applied, and no other change — this is not an HTML escaper, so <, & and " are returned as themselves.

doc.shortHtml: Reports whether one standard stream is attached to a terminal — posix_isatty and stream_isatty, which PHP splits between two extensions. Resolved once for the process, so two calls in one run cannot disagree.

params.name: stream
params.descHtml: Which stream to ask about. It is a parameter rather than a single process-wide answer because colour on standard output while standard input is a pipe is the common case, and one isTty() cannot express it.

doc.returnHtml: true when that stream is a terminal, false when it is a pipe, a file or closed.

doc.shortHtml: The controlling terminal's width in columns — tput cols, without a child process. Resolved once for the process.
doc.returnHtml: The column count, or 80 when no standard stream is a terminal. Never 0, so a caller may subtract a margin from it without checking.

doc.shortHtml: The controlling terminal's height in rows — tput lines. Resolved once for the process, alongside the width it was read with.
doc.returnHtml: The row count, or 24 when no standard stream is a terminal. Never 0, for width's reason.

doc.shortHtml: How much colour standard output can show, honouring NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE, FORCE_COLOR, COLORTERM and TERM. A program does not normally ask: it writes Cli\Text and the sink degrades to what the terminal has. Resolved once for the process.
doc.returnHtml: The depth as a Core\Cli\ColorDepth case — None whenever standard output is not a terminal and nothing forced colour on, which is what makes myprog | grep and a CI log plain.

doc.shortHtml: How many terminal columns $value will occupy when it is written — UAX #11 widths over grapheme clusters, replacing mb_strwidth. A CJK ideograph and a fullwidth Latin letter are two columns, a combining mark is none, and a control byte is the one its Control Picture costs, because that is what the terminal sink shows.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The text to measure. A tainted one is accepted: a column count carries nothing back out of it.

doc.returnHtml: The column count. A tab advances to the next multiple of eight, and a newline ends the row — so a value spanning several rows answers the width of its widest one, which is what a box is padded to.

members.name: ask
members.signature: ask(string $question, {default?: string, validate?: callable}): tainted string

doc.shortHtml: Asks $question at the controlling terminal and answers the line typed back — readline, without the GNU library and without reading standard input, so a program reading piped data can still ask. With no terminal it answers default if one was given and throws otherwise; it never blocks waiting for an answer nobody can give.

params.name: question
params.descHtml: What to write at the terminal. It goes through the same substitution echo performs, so a question built from untrusted text cannot move the cursor or repaint the screen around its own answer.

params.name: default
params.descHtml: What to answer when the terminal is not there, and what an empty line means when it is. Absent makes both of those a Core\Cli\NotInteractive.

params.name: validate
params.descHtml: Called with each answer; a falsy verdict asks again. It runs only where there is a terminal to ask again at, so it never sees a default.

doc.returnHtml: The line typed, without its ending, and tainted whatever it says — it came from outside the program, exactly as a request body did.

errors.descHtml: There is no controlling terminal to ask, its input ended, or nobody answered within the prompt deadline — and the call named no default.

doc.shortHtml: Asks $question as a yes/no question, showing which way the Enter key goes, and answers what was typed. An answer that is neither is asked again rather than read as false.

params.name: question
params.descHtml: What to write at the terminal, substituted as ask substitutes it.

params.name: default
params.descHtml: What an empty line means, and what an unattended run answers. Absent makes an unattended run throw, and makes an empty line ask again.

doc.returnHtml: true for yes and false for no — a plain bool and never a tainted one, because nothing of what was typed survives into a closed two-case answer.

errors.descHtml: There is no controlling terminal to ask, its input ended, or nobody answered within the prompt deadline — and the call named no default.

members.name: select
members.signature: select(string $question, array<T> $choices, {labels?: callable, default?: T}): T

doc.shortHtml: Offers $choices as a numbered list and answers the one chosen — the value itself, never its position, so nothing at the call site indexes back into the array.

params.name: question
params.descHtml: What to write above the list, substituted as ask substitutes it.

params.name: choices
params.descHtml: The values to choose between, listed in their own order. An empty array is a LogicError: there is no answer to hand back.

params.name: labels
params.descHtml: Called with each option to produce the line shown for it. Absent renders each option as text the way echo would.

params.name: default
params.descHtml: What an empty line chooses, and what an unattended run answers. Typed as the choices' own element type, so it cannot be a value that is not on offer.

doc.returnHtml: The chosen element of $choices, with that array's element type.

errors.descHtml: There is no controlling terminal to ask, its input ended, or nobody answered within the prompt deadline — and the call named no default.
$choices is empty, so there is nothing that could be chosen.

doc.shortHtml: Offers $choices as a numbered list and answers every one chosen, as the values themselves — select where the answer is a set, so the numbers are typed together on one line and an empty line names none of them.

params.name: question
params.descHtml: What to write above the list, substituted as ask substitutes it. The accepted range and separator are appended to it, the way confirm appends [y/n].

params.name: choices
params.descHtml: The values to choose between, listed in their own order. An empty array is a LogicError: there is nothing that could be chosen.

params.name: labels
params.descHtml: Called with each option to produce the line shown for it. Absent renders each option as text the way echo would.

doc.returnHtml: The chosen elements of $choices, in that array's own order and each at most once, whatever order they were typed in. An empty line answers an empty array; there is no default, so a run with no terminal throws instead.

errors.descHtml: There is no controlling terminal to ask, its input ended, or nobody answered within the prompt deadline. Unlike the other prompts this one has no default to fall back on.
$choices is empty, so there is nothing that could be chosen.

doc.shortHtml: Asks $question with the terminal's echo turned off, so a password is not left on the screen or in a scrollback buffer — PHP's readline has no spelling for this at all and every program shells out to stty -echo for it.

params.name: question
params.descHtml: What to write at the terminal, substituted as ask substitutes it.

doc.returnHtml: The line typed, secret and tainted at once: output, logs, dumps, Throwable messages and serialization all refuse it, and it still has to be laundered for any sink it reaches.

errors.descHtml: There is no controlling terminal to ask, its input ended, or nobody answered within the prompt deadline. secret takes no default, because a password nobody typed is not a password.

doc.shortHtml: Runs $body with a live region open on the terminal, and answers whatever $body answered. $body receives a Core\Cli\Live whose set replaces the region's rows in place — the scoped replacement for moveUp/clearLine cursor primitives, which break the moment output is piped and leave a shell unusable when a program dies holding them.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The work to do while the region is open. Its own return value is this member's, so a region costs a call site nothing in what it can compute.

doc.returnHtml: Exactly what $body answered, at $body's own type. The terminal is restored on every path out — a return, a throw, a fatal, an internal panic — and a run whose output is not a terminal renders nothing at all rather than a smear of escape sequences.

doc.shortHtml: Runs $body with a progress bar open on the terminal, and answers whatever $body answered. A closed, named behaviour over live's general one: the region is a bar the runtime draws, so counting toward $total is all a program says.

params.name: total
params.descHtml: How many units of work the bar is scaled to. A total of 0 is work already done, and draws a full bar rather than refusing.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The work to do while the bar is open. Its own return value is this member's.

doc.returnHtml: Exactly what $body answered, at $body's own type — live's contract, since this is that member with a frame the runtime writes.

classes.surfaceHtml: the terminal surface, owned by rule:tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink — arguments(): array<tainted string>, write, escape, isTty(Cli\Stream), width, height, colorDepth, displayWidth; the prompts ask, confirm, select<T>, multiSelect<T> and secret(): secret tainted string; and the scoped regions live<T> and progress<T>. Its value types are Cli\Text — built by plain/styled, composed with +, and read back by text(): string — Cli\Style and Cli\Color, its enums Cli\Stream, Cli\ColorDepth and Cli\Shell. Replaces $argv, $argc, readline, mb_strwidth, posix_isatty. Terminal output is a tainted sink that substitutes every control byte with a visible glyph; Cli\Text is the only thing that writes raw. The byte-and-line side of standard input is Core\IO (§ 14), not here; process exit is the exit keyword (rule:statements/nvs-is-the-only-open-tag).

classes.name: Core\Cli\Color
classes.summary: A terminal colour: one of the sixteen named colours, or any RGB colour. A terminal that shows fewer colours gets the nearest colour it can show.

doc.shortHtml: A colour from the terminal's 256-entry palette, whose first sixteen entries are the named constants on this class.

params.name: index
params.descHtml: The palette entry, 0 to 255.

doc.returnHtml: The colour that entry names, which a terminal with a smaller palette renders as the nearest of the sixteen it has.

errors.descHtml: $index is above 255, which no palette has an entry for.

doc.shortHtml: A 24-bit colour, for the terminals that have one — the sixteen million members that are why this class is a value type and not an enum.

params.name: red
params.descHtml: The red channel, 0 to 255.

params.name: green
params.descHtml: The green channel, 0 to 255.

params.name: blue
params.descHtml: The blue channel, 0 to 255.

doc.returnHtml: The colour, which is written as itself on a true-colour terminal and as the nearest palette entry on one without.

errors.descHtml: A channel is above 255.

classes.summaryHtml: A terminal colour: one of the sixteen named colours, or any RGB colour. A terminal that shows fewer colours gets the nearest colour it can show.

classes.name: Core\Cli\Live
classes.summary: An area of the terminal that your program redraws while it works. `Core\Cli::live` gives one to your function. Each update replaces what the area showed before.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces the region's rows with $lines. The runtime owns the cursor: it coalesces frames on a timer rather than repainting per call, diffs against what is on screen, and writes nothing at all where the run has no terminal.

params.name: lines
params.descHtml: The region's rows, one Core\Cli\Text each, replacing whatever it held. A row wider than the terminal is clamped rather than wrapped, because a wrapped row is a region that can no longer be repainted.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. What was drawn is on screen, or was coalesced into the next frame — a program cannot observe which, and the last frame handed in is always painted before the region closes.

errors.descHtml: The handle's own region is not the one holding the terminal — it has closed, or an inner Core\Cli::live is open inside it. A Cli\Live is scoped to the call that made it and escaping one is a program bug.

classes.summaryHtml: An area of the terminal that your program redraws while it works. Core\Cli::live gives one to your function. Each update replaces what the area showed before.

classes.name: Core\Cli\Progress
classes.summary: A progress bar that `Core\Cli::progress` gives to your function. Each step moves the counter forward and draws the bar again.

doc.shortHtml: Counts by units of work as done and redraws the bar, optionally changing the caption beside it.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: How many units this step finished; omitted, one.

params.name: label
params.descHtml: The caption beside the bar, substituted as every other terminal write is; omitted, the caption is left as it was.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A bar past its total reads as complete rather than as more than complete, so a loop that miscounts draws a finished bar instead of a wrong one.

errors.descHtml: The handle's own region is not the one holding the terminal — it has closed, or an inner region is open inside it, exactly as Core\Cli\Live::set refuses.

classes.summaryHtml: A progress bar that Core\Cli::progress gives to your function. Each step moves the counter forward and draws the bar again.

classes.name: Core\Cli\Style
classes.summary: How a piece of terminal text looks: its colours, and whether it is bold, underlined or struck through. A style does not change after you create it.

members.name: of
members.signature: of({color?: Core\Cli\Color, background?: Core\Cli\Color, bold?: bool, dim?: bool, italic?: bool, underline?: bool, strikethrough?: bool}): Core\Cli\Style

doc.shortHtml: A style, as a value — the replacement for the "\e[1;31m" string and the "<bold><red>" markup, neither of which Novis has a grammar for.

params.name: color
params.descHtml: The foreground colour. Absent leaves the terminal's own.

params.name: background
params.descHtml: The background colour. Absent leaves the terminal's own.

params.name: bold
params.descHtml: Whether the text is bold.

params.name: dim
params.descHtml: Whether the text is dimmed.

params.name: italic
params.descHtml: Whether the text is italic, which a minority of terminals render.

params.name: underline
params.descHtml: Whether the text is underlined.

params.name: strikethrough
params.descHtml: Whether the text is struck through.

doc.returnHtml: The style, which Core\Cli\Text::styled renders for the terminal this process actually has.

classes.summaryHtml: How a piece of terminal text looks: its colours, and whether it is bold, underlined or struck through. A style does not change after you create it.

classes.name: Core\Cli\Text
classes.summary: Text for the terminal, which can have colours and styles. You join two pieces with `+`. Outside an HTTP request, `Core\Out::capture` returns the captured output as one.

doc.shortHtml: Answers $text as a Core\Cli\Text, with every control byte already replaced by the visible glyph Core\Cli::escape gives it. This is the terminal sink's own carrier: echo writes a Text through unchanged, which is why the substitution happens here instead.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The text to carry. Its tainted qualifier is removed, for the same reason Core\Cli::escape removes it: the terminal is the sink this neutralizes for, and nothing is left in the answer for it to act on.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Cli\Text carrying the neutralized form. It composes with another Text and is written by echo; it carries no styling, which is styled's.

doc.shortHtml: Answers $text as a Core\Cli\Text wearing $style, with the text itself neutralized exactly as plain neutralizes it — so the only control bytes in the answer are the ones the style put there. Replaces the "\e[31m…" string every PHP CLI program builds by hand.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The text to carry. Its tainted qualifier is removed for plain's reason, and an escape sequence inside it is substituted rather than obeyed.

params.name: style
params.descHtml: The style to wear, as a value — Novis has no markup or escape grammar to write one in.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Cli\Text carrying the neutralized text between the style's own escape sequence and a reset. The styling is rendered for the terminal this process actually has, so it is absent entirely when standard output is not one.

doc.shortHtml: Answers what this Core\Cli\Text says, as a string, leaving its styling out: the text of every run joined, already control-byte-substituted. This is what a Core\Out::capture filter reads before it writes a new carrier.
doc.returnHtml: The runs' own text, with no escape sequence in it that a Cli\Style put there. It is safe to hand straight back to plain or styled, the terminal sink's substitution being idempotent.

classes.summaryHtml: Text for the terminal, which can have colours and styles. You join two pieces with +. Outside an HTTP request, Core\Out::capture returns the captured output as one.

classes.name: Core\Command
classes.surface: `run(): uint`, `help(?string): Cli\Text` and `completions(Cli\Shell): string`, over a table built while compiling from `#[Command]`/`#[Option]`/`#[Argument]`. A duplicate command name, two options sharing a spelling and an `#[Option]` on a parameter with no conversion from `string` are compile errors. Unlike `Core\Router` it dispatches, because a CLI has one entry point and no middleware question

doc.shortHtml: The usage page, generated from the table #[Command] built while compiling — one command's arguments, or the program's own list of commands. Nobody writes usage text and nobody lets it rot.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The command to describe, or null for the program's own page listing every command it declares.

doc.returnHtml: The rendered page as a Core\Cli\Text, ending with a newline.

errors.descHtml: The program declares no #[Command] under $name — a page for a command that does not exist is a mistake in the program rather than in its input, since the table is fixed at compile time.

doc.shortHtml: Matches this process's own command line against the table #[Command] built while compiling, calls the handler the first word names, and answers the status the process should exit with.
doc.returnHtml: The handler's own uint, or 0 where it is declared void. A command line this program's table does not answer is a usage error: the page goes to standard error and the status is 2, which is the status a command line nobody can act on has meant since getopt.

errors.descHtml: The named command's handler is not a method this program declares, or one of its parameters is declared at a type no argument's text is converted into yet — both are mistakes in the program rather than in the command line it was given.

doc.shortHtml: A completion script for this program, in the named shell's own syntax, generated from the same table help reads: every command it declares, and every option each one takes.

params.name: shell
params.descHtml: Which shell to write the script for.

doc.returnHtml: The script as plain text, ending with a newline — something to redirect into the shell's completion directory rather than something to print at a terminal.

errors.descHtml: This program has no name for the script to register against, which is every context but a command-line run: a served request is not something a shell completes.

classes.surfaceHtml: run(): uint, help(?string): Cli\Text and completions(Cli\Shell): string, over a table built while compiling from #[Command]/#[Option]/#[Argument]. A duplicate command name, two options sharing a spelling and an #[Option] on a parameter with no conversion from string are compile errors. Unlike Core\Router it dispatches, because a CLI has one entry point and no middleware question

classes.name: Core\Compress
classes.surface: `compress(bytes|string $data, Codec $codec): bytes` and `decompress(bytes $data, Codec $codec, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): bytes` — one API replacing `gzopen` handles, `deflate_init` contexts and `zlib.*` stream filters. `Core\Codec` is five cases, not four: `Gzip`, `Zlib` and `Deflate` are one stream under three headers, which is what PHP spelled as three function names, plus `Brotli` and `Zstd`. The incremental half is `compressor(Codec $codec): Compress\Compressor` and `decompressor(Codec $codec, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): Compress\Decompressor`, each an object with `add` and `finish`, replacing `deflate_init`/`deflate_add` and `inflate_init`/`inflate_add` — two classes because a `Compress\Decompressor`'s `finish` answers `tainted bytes` and a `Compress\Compressor`'s answers `bytes`

doc.shortHtml: Compresses $data under $codec, replacing gzencode, gzcompress, gzdeflate and zlib_encode at once — the format is a case of Core\Codec rather than a third of a function's name.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The octets to compress; a string is read as its UTF-8 bytes.

params.name: codec
params.descHtml: The format to write. Core\Codec::Gzip is the one to reach for when the result crosses a wire.

doc.returnHtml: The compressed frame, as octets. Compressing is never refused for size: the output of a compressor is bounded by its input.

doc.shortHtml: Decompresses $data under $codec, under a bound that cannot be switched off — replacing gzdecode, gzuncompress, gzinflate and zlib_decode, whose $max_length was optional and defaulted to unlimited.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The compressed frame. Tainted in, tainted out: decompressing tells you nothing about what the octets are safe for.

params.name: codec
params.descHtml: The format $data is in. Nothing is sniffed — a frame that is not this format is refused rather than guessed at.

params.name: maxBytes
params.descHtml: The most output this call will produce, in octets. A call may ask for less than [limits] max_decompressed and never for more; 0 is a bound of zero and not a spelling for unbounded.

params.name: maxRatio
params.descHtml: The most output per octet of input. The second half of the same bound: a bomb is small on the wire, so a byte ceiling alone is a ceiling a small request can still reach.

doc.returnHtml: The decompressed octets, never a truncation — a decompression that would pass either bound throws instead of answering the prefix it had reached.

errors.descHtml: $data is not a well-formed frame of $codec, or the output would pass either half of the bound. Never an IOError: a hostile archive and a full disk are different questions.

doc.shortHtml: Opens an incremental compression under $codec, as deflate_init does — a Core\Compress\Compressor fed by add and closed by finish.

params.name: codec
params.descHtml: The format to write, any Core\Codec case. Fixed for the stream's whole life: a frame is one format.

doc.returnHtml: A fresh, open stream that has been fed nothing yet.

doc.shortHtml: Opens an incremental decompression under $codec, as inflate_init does — a Core\Compress\Decompressor fed by add and closed by finish, under the same bound that cannot be switched off.

params.name: codec
params.descHtml: The format the chunks are in. Nothing is sniffed — a frame that is not this format is refused rather than guessed at.

params.name: maxBytes
params.descHtml: The most output this whole stream will produce, in octets — resolved against [limits] max_decompressed here, at the opening, and charged once across every chunk rather than once per add.

params.name: maxRatio
params.descHtml: The most output per octet fed to the stream. The second half of the same bound, measured against everything add was handed.

doc.returnHtml: A fresh, open stream that has been fed nothing yet, carrying the bound it will be measured against.

classes.surfaceHtml: compress(bytes|string $data, Codec $codec): bytes and decompress(bytes $data, Codec $codec, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): bytes — one API replacing gzopen handles, deflate_init contexts and zlib.* stream filters. Core\Codec is five cases, not four: Gzip, Zlib and Deflate are one stream under three headers, which is what PHP spelled as three function names, plus Brotli and Zstd. The incremental half is compressor(Codec $codec): Compress\Compressor and decompressor(Codec $codec, uint $maxBytes = 67108864, uint $maxRatio = 1000): Compress\Decompressor, each an object with add and finish, replacing deflate_init/deflate_add and inflate_init/inflate_add — two classes because a Compress\Decompressor's finish answers tainted bytes and a Compress\Compressor's answers bytes

classes.name: Core\Compress\Compressor
classes.summary: Compresses data that arrives in pieces. You add each piece, and `finish` returns the compressed data.

doc.shortHtml: Feeds $data to the stream, as deflate_add does; the chunks are compressed in order at finish.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The next octets; a string is read as its UTF-8 bytes.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. PHP's deflate_add answers whatever its flush mode let the coder emit, and there is no such answer here: the frame is written whole at finish.
