members.name: sign
members.signature: sign(array<string> $claims, Core\Time\Duration $lifetime, secret bytes|Core\Crypto\KeyPair $key, {kid?: string, typ?: string, embedKey?: bool}): string

doc.shortHtml: Signs $claims into a JWT that expires $lifetime from now, under $key and the one algorithm that key has. The expiry is written here rather than passed in, so a token this member produces always carries one.

params.name: claims
params.descHtml: The application's own claims, by name. exp and iat are written by this member and are refused here; every other name is carried through unchanged.

params.name: lifetime
params.descHtml: How long the token stays valid — 15m, 1h, 7d. It must be positive: a token that has already expired is a program bug, not a token.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: A shared secret of at least 32 octets, which signs HS256 — Core\Crypto::generateKey() answers one, and a longer secret agreed with another service is accepted as it stands. Or a Core\Crypto\KeyPair, which signs ES256, EdDSA, RS256 or PS256 by its kind. There is no algorithm argument: the key is the choice.

params.name: kid
params.descHtml: The key's name in the header, for a recipient holding several. Omitted by default, and written verbatim — it names a key and selects nothing.

params.name: typ
params.descHtml: The header's typ, JWT when omitted. RFC 9068's access tokens spell it at+jwt.

params.name: embedKey
params.descHtml: Writes the pair's public half into the header as RFC 7638's minimal JWK, which is what a DPoP proof carries. Off by default, and a bug under a shared secret, which has no public half.

doc.returnHtml: The three base64url parts and their two dots, as a header, a payload and a signature — a value a header, a query string and a JSON body all carry unescaped.

errors.descHtml: $key is a secret shorter than 32 octets, or an X25519 pair, which signs nothing; {embedKey: true} was written under a shared secret; $lifetime is zero or negative; or $claims names exp or iat, which this member writes, or carries a positional entry, since a claim has a name.
This process cannot spare a buffer the size of the token.

members.name: signObject
members.signature: signObject(object $claims, Core\Time\Duration $lifetime, Core\Crypto\KeyPair $key, {kid?: string, typ?: string, embedKey?: bool}): string

doc.shortHtml: Signs a structured $claims into a JWT that expires $lifetime from now, under a key pair and the one algorithm that pair has. The claims are written as Core\Json::encode writes them, with iat and exp appended.

params.name: claims
params.descHtml: A shape or a class carrying #[Core\Json\Derive], encoded as the JSON object it is. exp and iat are written by this member and are refused among its fields; a value with no JSON encoding is a bug in the program.

params.name: lifetime
params.descHtml: How long the token stays valid — 15m, 1h, 7d. It must be positive: a token that has already expired is a program bug, not a token.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: A Core\Crypto\KeyPair, which signs ES256, EdDSA, RS256 or PS256 by its kind. A shared secret is not accepted here: a structured payload is a token issued to another party, and Core\Jwt::verify reads only the text claims sign writes.

params.name: kid
params.descHtml: The key's name in the header, for a recipient holding several. Omitted by default, and written verbatim — it names a key and selects nothing.

params.name: typ
params.descHtml: The header's typ, JWT when omitted. RFC 9068's access tokens spell it at+jwt.

params.name: embedKey
params.descHtml: Writes the pair's public half into the header as RFC 7638's minimal JWK, which is what a DPoP proof carries. Off by default.

doc.returnHtml: The three base64url parts and their two dots, exactly as sign answers — the payload is the claims object with iat and exp as its last two members.

errors.descHtml: $claims carries a field named exp or iat, which this member writes; or it has no JSON encoding at all — a class that carries no #[Core\Json\Derive], a secret value, a bytes, or a cycle. $key is an X25519 pair, which signs nothing, or $lifetime is zero or negative.
This process cannot spare a buffer the size of the token.

doc.shortHtml: Answers the claims $token carries, having checked that this key signed it and that it has not expired. It throws rather than answering an empty value, so there is no falsy result a comparison could mistake for a verified token.

params.name: token
params.descHtml: The token as the request carried it, in its three-part form.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The shared secret sign was given, or the issuer's. The token's own alg is compared against this key's algorithm and never used to pick one.

doc.returnHtml: Every claim in the payload, by name, each one tainted: a signature proves who wrote a value, not that it is safe for any sink. exp and iat are present in it, in their own decimal spelling.

errors.descHtml: $key is shorter than 32 octets — a value that was never a signing key.
The token is not one this key signed, which is one sentence for every way of not being one; or it is, and has expired, carries no exp, or carries a claim that is not text.

members.name: verifyIssued
members.signature: verifyIssued<T>(string $token, Core\Jwt\KeySet|Core\Crypto\PublicKey $keys, string $issuer, string $audience, {leeway?: Core\Time\Duration, typ?: string, nonce?: string, maxAge?: Core\Time\Duration}): T

doc.shortHtml: Verifies a token another party issued and answers its claims as the written type, having checked the header's policy, found the one key that may have signed it, checked the signature, and then the clock and the registered claims in that order. It throws rather than answering an empty value.

params.name: token
params.descHtml: The token as the request carried it, in its three-part form. It is refused unread past 8 KiB.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The issuer's key set, in which the header's kid names exactly one key, or one public key on its own. There is no try-every-key: a token naming no kid verifies only against a set holding exactly one. The token's alg is compared against the key's algorithm and never used to pick one.

params.name: issuer
params.descHtml: What the token's iss must equal, exactly.

params.name: audience
params.descHtml: What the token's aud must be, or must hold. A token listing more than one audience must also carry an azp equal to this.

params.name: leeway
params.descHtml: How far the clock may disagree, at both ends of the window: 60 seconds when omitted, and refused when negative or wider than 5 minutes. It widens the expiry check and never removes it.

params.name: typ
params.descHtml: The typ the header must carry, compared case-insensitively with any application/ prefix removed — at+jwt for RFC 9068's access tokens. Any typ is accepted when this is omitted.

params.name: nonce
params.descHtml: The value the token's nonce claim must equal, compared in constant time. A token carrying none is refused when this is named.

params.name: maxAge
params.descHtml: How old the token's auth_time may be. A token carrying none is refused when this is named.

doc.returnHtml: An instance of the written type, decoded from the payload as Core\Json::decodeAs decodes a document. Its text fields must be declared tainted, which the call site is held to: a signature proves who wrote a claim, not that it is safe for any sink.

errors.descHtml: leeway is negative or wider than 5 minutes; the written type is a list, which no token's payload is; or the key is an X25519 one, which verifies nothing.

The token is not one this issuer's key signed, its header carries a parameter a verifier may not honour, or no key was found for it — one sentence for every way of not being verifiable; or it is authentic, and is outside its validity window or carries a registered claim that is not what was asked for, which names the claim.

classes.name: Core\Jwt\KeySet
classes.summary: The public keys another service uses to sign its tokens. `read` reads them from the JWKS document that service publishes. `Core\Jwt::verifyIssued` then checks a token with the one key its `kid` names.

doc.shortHtml: Admits the signing keys a JWKS document publishes, so a token can be checked against the one key its kid names. A key this roster has no use for is skipped and a document that is wrong is refused whole, which are different answers to different questions.

params.name: jwks
params.descHtml: The document as the issuer served it. It is read here and nowhere else: fetching it, caching it and rotating it are a package's job, and this member is stateless over the text it is handed.

params.name: rsaScheme
params.descHtml: Which scheme an RSA key carrying no alg is read under — RsaPkcs1 for RS256 or RsaPss for PS256. A key's own alg always wins, and an RSA key with neither is refused rather than guessed. Every other kind names its own algorithm, so this reaches nothing else.

doc.returnHtml: A set of at most 16 public keys, each under the name the document gave it, ready for a lookup by kid and never for a try of every key.

errors.descHtml: {rsaScheme: …} names a kind that is not one of the two RSA ones, and no other kind has two schemes to choose between.

$jwks is not a document to read keys from: it is not JSON, it carries no keys array, one of its keys carries a private member or a kid that is not text, a key is not a key of the kind it claims — an RSA modulus outside 2048–8192 bits included — an alg is one its key's kind cannot carry, two keys share a kid, or more than 16 keys are admitted.

classes.summaryHtml: The public keys another service uses to sign its tokens. read reads them from the JWKS document that service publishes. Core\Jwt::verifyIssued then checks a token with the one key its kid names.

classes.name: Core\Log
classes.surface: structured logging. `write(Log\Level, string $message, array<string, mixed> $fields = [])`, where `Log\Level` is `Debug`, `Info`, `Warn`, `Error`, `Critical`. Both refuse a `secret` argument at the call site — a sink on the [0033](../decisions/0033.md) axis; on the `tainted` axis neither is a sink, because a field is *data* ([0088](../decisions/0088.md) § 7) and logging tainted input is the point

doc.shortHtml: Writes one log record — the same record, through the same writer, the engine itself uses when it reports for a program that has stopped, so a log pipeline never sees two shapes for one event. The rendering at a log target is JSON Lines: one object per line.

params.name: level
params.descHtml: How loud the record is. Core\Log\Level's five cases carry their own syslog severities.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: What happened, as one plain sentence. A tainted value is accepted here — a log record is data and recording untrusted input is the point — while a secret one is refused, which is the rule for every message a human reads.

params.name: fields
params.descHtml: Structured context, written as a fields object beside the message rather than pasted into it. Omitted from the record entirely when it is empty, so an ordinary call costs no key. Nothing in fields makes a write fail. A value the format cannot write, such as bytes, a callable or a cycle, is written as text that says what it is.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A record that cannot be written is dropped rather than retried: the log is not the program's storage.

classes.surfaceHtml: structured logging. write(Log\Level, string $message, array<string, mixed> $fields = []), where Log\Level is Debug, Info, Warn, Error, Critical. Both refuse a secret argument at the call site — a sink on the 0033 axis; on the tainted axis neither is a sink, because a field is data (0088 § 7) and logging tainted input is the point

classes.name: Core\Mail
classes.surface: an SMTP client with structured headers. Replaces `mail()`

members.name: send
members.signature: send(string $endpoint, array<string> $to, string $subject, string $text, {cc?: array<string>, bcc?: array<string>, replyTo?: string, html?: string}): void

doc.shortHtml: Hands one message to the SMTP endpoint [mail.$endpoint] names, and returns once that endpoint has accepted it.

params.name: endpoint
params.descHtml: Which [mail.<name>] block in nvs.toml to send through. Refuses a tainted argument: it selects a deployment, so it is written at the call site and never read from input.

params.name: to
params.descHtml: The recipients, one address per entry. A list rather than a comma-separated string, which has no unambiguous reading.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The subject. RFC 2047 encoded where it holds anything a header line cannot carry, so no value of it can add a header.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The plain-text body, which every message has.

params.name: cc
params.descHtml: Further recipients, named in the message.

params.name: bcc
params.descHtml: Further recipients, not named in the message — they reach the envelope and no header.

params.name: replyTo
params.descHtml: Where a reply should go, when that is not the configured sender.

params.name: html
params.descHtml: An HTML alternative to $text. Given one, the message is multipart/alternative and both parts are sent.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The endpoint accepted the message; delivery past it is the endpoint's.

errors.descHtml: The capability mail.send does not grant $endpoint; or no [mail.<name>] block of that name sets host or from; or that block sets one of user and password without the other; or an address is not one. Each is a deployment or a call that was written wrong, not a send that failed.

The configured endpoint could not be reached, closed the connection, or refused a command — the last carrying the SMTP reply that said so. Also where a block configures a credential and its endpoint cannot carry one: no STARTTLS, no AUTH PLAIN over it, or a certificate that does not verify. Nothing is sent in the clear on any of those paths.

classes.surfaceHtml: an SMTP client with structured headers. Replaces mail()

classes.name: Core\Math
classes.summary:
`**` is exponentiation and `%` is integer modulo, so neither has a member (R17). Division by zero throws
`ArithmeticError` (R4) — in `intDiv`, in `mod`, and in the `/` operator whatever the operand types, which
is exactly why `fdiv` *is* a member here: it is the one spelling left for IEEE's `INF`, and PHP has it for
the same reason. Overflow throws rather than becoming a `float`
(`rule:types/arithmetic`).

enums.name: RoundMode
enums.raw: RoundMode { HalfUp, HalfDown, HalfEven, HalfOdd, Up, Down }

doc.shortHtml: How Core\Math::round settles a value between two neighbours — PHP's four PHP_ROUND_HALF_* constants plus the two whole-direction rules ceil and floor only cover at a precision of zero.

cases.name: HalfUp
cases.descHtml: A tie goes away from zero — PHP_ROUND_HALF_UP, and round's default there and here.

cases.name: HalfDown
cases.descHtml: A tie goes toward zero — PHP_ROUND_HALF_DOWN.

cases.name: HalfEven
cases.descHtml: A tie goes to the even neighbour — banker's rounding, PHP_ROUND_HALF_EVEN, the rule that does not accumulate a bias over many values.

cases.name: HalfOdd
cases.descHtml: A tie goes to the odd neighbour — PHP_ROUND_HALF_ODD.

cases.name: Up
cases.descHtml: Every value goes away from zero, tie or not — ceil for a positive number and floor for a negative one, at any precision.

cases.name: Down
cases.descHtml: Every value goes toward zero, tie or not — truncation, at any precision.

constants.name: PI
constants.descHtml: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, 3.14159… as the nearest float — PHP's M_PI.

constants.name: TAU
constants.descHtml: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its radius, 2 PI or 6.28318… as the nearest float — a full turn in radians, which PHP spells 2 M_PI.

constants.name: E
constants.descHtml: Euler's number, the base of the natural logarithm, 2.71828… as the nearest float — PHP's M_E, and log's default base.

constants.name: EPSILON
constants.descHtml: The smallest float that added to 1.0 gives a value other than 1.0, 2.220446049250313e-16 — PHP's PHP_FLOAT_EPSILON, and the tolerance to compare two floats with in place of ==.

constants.name: INT_MIN
constants.descHtml: The smallest int, -9223372036854775808 — PHP's PHP_INT_MIN, and the one value abs has no int answer for.

constants.name: UINT_MAX
constants.descHtml: The largest uint, 18446744073709551615 — a type PHP does not have, so there is no constant to replace.

constants.name: FLOAT_MAX
constants.descHtml: The largest finite float, 1.7976931348623157e308 — PHP's PHP_FLOAT_MAX; the negative extreme is -FLOAT_MAX.

constants.name: FLOAT_MIN
constants.descHtml: The smallest positive normal float, 2.2250738585072014e-308 — PHP's PHP_FLOAT_MIN, and not the negative extreme, which is -FLOAT_MAX.

constants.name: NAN
constants.descHtml: The float that is not a number — PHP's NAN — equal to nothing, itself included, so isNan is the only test for it.

constants.name: INFINITY
constants.descHtml: Positive infinity as a float, past every finite value — PHP's INF; the negative one is -INFINITY, and isFinite is false for both.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $n without its sign, as the same kind of number. -3 gives 3 and -2.5 gives 2.5.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number whose sign is removed: an int, a float or a decimal.

doc.returnHtml: $n without its sign, with the same type as $n. An int gives an int, a uint is returned unchanged, a float gives a float and a decimal gives a decimal with the same decimal places. -0.0 becomes 0.0.

errors.descHtml: When $n is INT_MIN, whose positive value is one past INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns -1 when $n is below zero, 1 when it is above zero and 0 when it is zero. This replaces PHP's $n <=> 0.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to check: an int, a float or a decimal.

doc.returnHtml: -1, 0 or 1, as an int. -0.0 is zero, so the result for it is 0.

errors.descHtml: When $n is NaN (a value that means "not a number"). NaN is not below, above or equal to zero.
When $n is a uint bigger than Core\Math::INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the smaller of two values. This replaces PHP's min with two values. For the smallest value in an array, use Core\Arr::min.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: One value: a number, a string, a bool or null.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The other value, of the same type as $a.

doc.returnHtml: The smaller value. When the two are equal, the result is $a. NaN is smaller than every other float.

errors.descHtml: When the two values cannot be compared: an object, an array, or two values of different kinds.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the larger of two values. This replaces PHP's max with two values. For the largest value in an array, use Core\Arr::max.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: One value: a number, a string, a bool or null.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The other value, of the same type as $a.

doc.returnHtml: The larger value. When the two are equal, the result is $a. NaN is smaller than every other float.

errors.descHtml: When the two values cannot be compared: an object, an array, or two values of different kinds.

doc.shortHtml: Keeps $n between $low and $high. It replaces PHP's min(max($n, $low), $high).

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The value to keep in the range. It can be a number, a string, a bool or null.

params.name: low
params.descHtml: The smallest value the result can be.

params.name: high
params.descHtml: The largest value the result can be. It must not be below $low.

doc.returnHtml: $low when $n is below it, $high when $n is above it, and $n itself otherwise. Both ends are inside the range.

errors.descHtml: When $low is above $high. Also when two of the values cannot be compared: an object without compareTo, an array, or a number and a string.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $n up to the next whole number. For a negative $n, up means toward zero.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to round up.

doc.returnHtml: A whole number, as a float. A $n between -1.0 and 0.0 gives -0.0. NaN and the infinities stay the same.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $n down to the next whole number. For a negative $n, down means away from zero.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to round down.

doc.returnHtml: A whole number, as a float. A $n between -1.0 and 0.0 gives -1.0. NaN and the infinities stay the same.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the fractional part of $n. The result moves toward zero, so 2.7 gives 2.0 and -2.7 gives -2.0.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number whose fractional part is removed.

doc.returnHtml: A whole number, as a float. A $n between -1.0 and 0.0 gives -0.0. NaN and the infinities stay the same.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $n to a number of decimal places. This replaces PHP's round. The mode option chooses the result for a value exactly halfway between two results.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to round.

params.name: precision
params.descHtml: How many decimal places to keep. The default is 0, which rounds to a whole number. -2 rounds to hundreds.

params.name: mode
params.descHtml: A Core\RoundMode case. The default is RoundMode::HalfUp, which rounds a half away from zero.

doc.returnHtml: The rounded float. NaN and the infinities are returned unchanged. $n is also returned unchanged when precision is above 22 or below -22, or when $n * 10 precision is 2 53 or more.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $a by $b and drops the remainder, so the result moves toward zero. This replaces PHP's intdiv.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The integer to divide.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The integer to divide by. It may not be zero.

doc.returnHtml: The whole part of $a / $b. intDiv(7, 2) is 3, and intDiv(-7, 2) is -3. The % operator gives the remainder.

errors.descHtml: When $b is zero. Also when $a is Core\Math::INT_MIN and $b is -1, because the result is one more than Core\Math::INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the remainder after dividing $a by $b, for float values. The result has the sign of $a. This replaces PHP's fmod. For whole numbers, use the % operator.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The number to divide.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The number to divide by. It may not be zero.

doc.returnHtml: The remainder. mod(7.5, 2.0) is 1.5, and mod(-7.5, 2.0) is -1.5. When $a is an infinity, the result is NaN. When $b is an infinity, the result is $a.

errors.descHtml: When $b is zero. PHP's fmod returns NaN here.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $a by $b. When $b is zero, it returns INFINITY, -INFINITY or NaN. The / operator throws an error there. This replaces PHP's fdiv.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The number to divide.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The number to divide by. It may be zero.

doc.returnHtml: $a / $b. When $b is zero, the result is INFINITY or -INFINITY. Its sign comes from the signs of both numbers together. When both numbers are zero, the result is NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the greatest common divisor of two integers. This is the largest integer that divides both with no remainder. This replaces PHP's gmp_gcd.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first integer. Its sign does not change the result.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The second integer. Its sign does not change the result.

doc.returnHtml: The greatest common divisor, which is never negative. When one integer is 0, the result is the other one without its sign. When both are 0, the result is 0.

errors.descHtml: When the result does not fit an int. This happens only when one integer is Core\Math::INT_MIN and the other is Core\Math::INT_MIN or 0.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the least common multiple of two integers. This is the smallest positive integer that both divide with no remainder. This replaces PHP's gmp_lcm.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first integer. Its sign does not change the result.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The second integer. Its sign does not change the result.

doc.returnHtml: The least common multiple, which is never negative. When one integer is 0, the result is 0.

errors.descHtml: When the result is bigger than Core\Math::INT_MAX. This happens quickly for two big integers that share no divisor.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the square root of $n. This replaces PHP's sqrt.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to take the square root of.

doc.returnHtml: A float that is zero or more. A negative $n gives NaN. -0.0 gives -0.0, and Core\Math::INFINITY gives Core\Math::INFINITY.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the cube root of $n. A negative $n works too. PHP code often writes pow($n, 1/3), which gives NaN for a negative number.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: The cube root, with the same sign as $n: Core\Math::cbrt(-8.0) is -2.0. An infinity gives the same infinity, and NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the length of the longest side of a right triangle. $a and $b are the other two sides. The result is sqrt($a $a + $b $b), but it stays correct when $a * $a is too big for a float. This replaces PHP's hypot.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The length of one side. Its sign does not change the result.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The length of the other side. Its sign does not change the result.

doc.returnHtml: The length. It is never negative. When $a or $b is INFINITY or -INFINITY, the result is INFINITY, even when the other one is NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns E raised to the power $n. E is about 2.718. This replaces PHP's exp.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The power to raise E to.

doc.returnHtml: E ** $n, which is never negative. Above about 709.78 the result is INFINITY. Far enough below zero, the result is 0.0. NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the logarithm of $n: the power you raise base to to get $n. The base is E unless you give one. This replaces PHP's log, log10 and log2.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to take the logarithm of.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The base. It must be greater than zero, and it is E when you leave it out. For a power of 10.0 or 2.0 in that base, the result is exact.

doc.returnHtml: The logarithm. When $n is 0.0 and base is greater than 1.0, the result is -INFINITY. When $n is negative, or base is 1.0, the result is NaN.

errors.descHtml: When base is zero or negative. PHP throws a ValueError here.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the sine of an angle. The angle is in radians.

params.name: radians
params.descHtml: The angle, in radians. Core\Math::toRadians converts degrees to radians.

doc.returnHtml: A number from -1.0 to 1.0. An infinity or NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the cosine of an angle. The angle is in radians.

params.name: radians
params.descHtml: The angle, in radians. Core\Math::toRadians converts degrees to radians.

doc.returnHtml: A number from -1.0 to 1.0. An infinity or NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the tangent of an angle. The angle is in radians. The tangent is the sine divided by the cosine.

params.name: radians
params.descHtml: The angle, in radians. Core\Math::toRadians converts degrees to radians.

doc.returnHtml: Any number. It is very large when the angle is close to 90 degrees. An infinity or NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the angle, in radians, whose sine is $n. This is the arc sine.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: A sine: a number from -1.0 to 1.0.

doc.returnHtml: An angle from -PI / 2 to PI / 2, in radians. A $n outside -1.0 to 1.0 gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the angle, in radians, whose cosine is $n. This is the arc cosine.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: A cosine: a number from -1.0 to 1.0.

doc.returnHtml: An angle from 0.0 to PI, in radians. A $n outside -1.0 to 1.0 gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the angle, in radians, whose tangent is $n. This is the arc tangent. For a point, use Core\Math::atan2, which takes both coordinates.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: A tangent: any number.

doc.returnHtml: An angle between -PI / 2 and PI / 2, in radians. An infinite $n gives exactly PI / 2 or -PI / 2.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the angle of the point ($x, $y), in radians, measured from the positive x-axis. $y comes first.

params.name: y
params.descHtml: The point's y coordinate.

params.name: x
params.descHtml: The point's x coordinate.

doc.returnHtml: An angle from -PI to PI, in radians. A point above the x-axis gives a positive angle, and a point below it gives a negative one. The point (0, 0) gives 0.0.

doc.shortHtml: Converts an angle from degrees to radians. It computes ($degrees / 180) * PI, the same way as PHP.

params.name: degrees
params.descHtml: The angle, in degrees.

doc.returnHtml: The same angle in radians. Core\Math::toRadians(180.0) is PI. An infinity gives an infinity, and NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Converts an angle from radians to degrees. It computes ($radians / PI) * 180, the same way as PHP.

params.name: radians
params.descHtml: The angle, in radians.

doc.returnHtml: The same angle in degrees. Core\Math::toDegrees(Core\Math::PI) is 180.0. A result too big for a float is an infinity, and NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns true when $n is NaN, a value that means "not a number". NaN is not equal to any value, itself included, so == cannot find it. This replaces PHP's is_nan.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The value to test.

doc.returnHtml: true when $n is NaN. false for every other float, INFINITY and -INFINITY included.

doc.shortHtml: Returns true when $n is an ordinary number. INFINITY, -INFINITY and NaN are not ordinary numbers. This replaces PHP's is_finite. PHP's is_infinite($n) is !isFinite($n) && !isNan($n).

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The value to test.

doc.returnHtml: true for every ordinary float, zero included. false for INFINITY, -INFINITY and NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Writes the number $n in base $base and returns the digits as a string. This replaces PHP's decbin, dechex, decoct and base_convert. Digits above 9 are the lower case letters a to z.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to write. It can be negative.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The base, from 2 to 36. Base 2 is binary and base 16 is hexadecimal.

doc.returnHtml: The digits, with no prefix and no leading zeros. A negative $n starts with -. 0 returns "0".

errors.descHtml: When $base is outside 2 to 36. PHP's base_convert returns 0 here.

doc.shortHtml: Reads a number written in base $base and returns it as an int. This replaces PHP's bindec, hexdec, octdec and base_convert. Every character must be a digit of the base. PHP skips a character that is not.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The digits. A leading - is allowed. A prefix such as 0x, spaces and separators are not allowed. Letters can be upper or lower case.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The base, from 2 to 36. Digits above 9 are the letters a to z.

doc.returnHtml: The number as an int. Core\Math::toBase writes it back.

errors.descHtml: When $base is outside 2 to 36, when $s has no digits, or when a character of $s is not a digit of the base.
When the number is too large for an int.

members.name: format
members.signature: format(int|float|decimal $n, {decimals?: uint, decimalSeparator?: string, groupSeparator?: string}): string

doc.shortHtml: Writes a number as text for a person to read, with a fixed number of decimals. This replaces PHP's number_format. The digits are not grouped unless you give a groupSeparator.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to write: an int, a float or a decimal.

params.name: decimals
params.descHtml: How many digits to write after the decimal separator, from 0 to 100. The default is 0, which writes no decimal separator.

params.name: decimalSeparator
params.descHtml: The text between the whole part and the decimals. The default is ..

params.name: groupSeparator
params.descHtml: The text between each group of three digits, counted from the right. The default is empty, so the digits are not grouped.

doc.returnHtml: The text. The number is rounded to decimals places, and a half is rounded away from zero. A negative number starts with -. A number that rounds to zero has no -.

errors.descHtml: When $n is INFINITY, -INFINITY or NaN, or when decimals is more than 100.
When $n is a uint larger than Core\Math::INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the hyperbolic sine of $n, which is (exp($n) - exp(-$n)) / 2.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: A number with the same sign as $n. It is INFINITY when $n is above about 710, and -INFINITY when $n is below about -710. NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of $n, which is (exp($n) + exp(-$n)) / 2.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: A number of at least 1.0. It is INFINITY when $n is above about 710 or below about -710. NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of $n. That is Core\Math::sinh divided by Core\Math::cosh.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: A number from -1.0 to 1.0, with the same sign as $n. INFINITY gives 1.0, -INFINITY gives -1.0 and NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of $n. It undoes Core\Math::sinh.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: The number whose hyperbolic sine is $n. It has the same sign as $n. NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the number whose hyperbolic cosine is $n. This is the inverse hyperbolic cosine.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: A hyperbolic cosine: a number that is 1.0 or more.

doc.returnHtml: A number that is 0.0 or more. A $n below 1.0 gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the number whose hyperbolic tangent is $n. This is the inverse hyperbolic tangent. It undoes Core\Math::tanh.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: A hyperbolic tangent: a number from -1.0 to 1.0.

doc.returnHtml: A number with the same sign as $n. 1.0 gives INF and -1.0 gives -INF. A $n outside -1.0 to 1.0 gives NaN.

classes.summaryHtml: * is exponentiation and % is integer modulo, so neither has a member (R17). Division by zero throws ArithmeticError (R4) — in intDiv, in mod, and in the / operator whatever the operand types, which is exactly why fdiv is* a member here: it is the one spelling left for IEEE's INF, and PHP has it for the same reason. Overflow throws rather than becoming a float (rule:types/arithmetic).

classes.name: Core\Metrics
classes.surface: `increment(string $name, {by?, labels?})`, `observe(string $name, float $value, {labels?})`, `gauge(…)`. A `labels` **value** is a `tainted` sink with no launderer — label by an enum, an `as`-converted scalar or a route name

doc.shortHtml: Adds to a counter, fixing $name to a counter on its first use — the replacement for every hand-rolled $GLOBALS tally and for a statsd client's increment.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The series name, [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. A name written directly in the code that does not match this pattern does not compile. A tainted name does not compile either.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: How much to add; one by default, and never negative, since a counter that went backwards would read as a process restart.

params.name: labels
params.descHtml: The label values this series is written under, keyed by label name. A tainted or secret value is refused: label by an enum case, an as-converted scalar or a route name.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. No program can read a metric back: the values are per-core aggregates a scrape merges, and the only reader is outside every request.

errors.descHtml: The name is already fixed to another kind or to another set of label names. The message gives both the call that fixed it and this one. A new series past the core's max_series is not an error: it is dropped and counted, and the call answers normally.

doc.shortHtml: Records one observation into a histogram, fixing $name to a histogram on its first use — a duration, a payload size, a queue depth at the moment it was measured.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The series name, [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. A name written directly in the code that does not match this pattern does not compile. A tainted name does not compile either.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The observation, in the series' own unit — seconds for a _seconds name, bytes for a _bytes one.

params.name: labels
params.descHtml: The label values this series is written under, keyed by label name. A tainted or secret value is refused: label by an enum case, an as-converted scalar or a route name.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing, as increment.

errors.descHtml: The name is already fixed to another kind or to another set of label names. The message gives both the call that fixed it and this one. A new series past the core's max_series is not an error: it is dropped and counted, and the call answers normally.

doc.shortHtml: Sets a gauge to $value, fixing $name to a gauge on its first use — a level that goes up and down, such as the number of items waiting or the bytes a pool holds.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The series name, [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. A name written directly in the code that does not match this pattern does not compile. A tainted name does not compile either.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: What the gauge now reads. The last write before a scrape is the one reported.

params.name: labels
params.descHtml: The label values this series is written under, keyed by label name. A tainted or secret value is refused: label by an enum case, an as-converted scalar or a route name.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing, as increment.

errors.descHtml: The name is already fixed to another kind or to another set of label names. The message gives both the call that fixed it and this one. A new series past the core's max_series is not an error: it is dropped and counted, and the call answers normally.

classes.surfaceHtml: increment(string $name, {by?, labels?}), observe(string $name, float $value, {labels?}), gauge(…). A labels value is a tainted sink with no launderer — label by an enum, an as-converted scalar or a route name

classes.name: Core\Mime
classes.surface: `detect(bytes $data): Mime\Type` and `mediaType(Mime\Type $type): string` — type detection by magic bytes, from a fixed table of literal signatures rather than libmagic's rule interpreter, and never from a file extension: a type read off a name is a type an attacker chose. `Core\Mime\Type` is closed and its zero case is `Unknown`, so a caller compares against a case rather than against a spelling that may never occur, and a format serialized as text answers `Unknown` rather than a guess

doc.shortHtml: Reports what $data is, read from the octets themselves — replacing mime_content_type, finfo_buffer and exif_imagetype. There is no parameter for a file name, because a type read off an extension is a type an attacker chose.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The octets to inspect. Only the first few are read — the widest signature in the table is sixteen — so a prefix of an upload answers what the whole of it would.

doc.returnHtml: The case naming what the octets are, or Core\Mime\Type::Unknown where no signature matched — which includes every format serialized as text. Detection is not a laundering: bytes that detect as image/png are still tainted, because a signature describes the first octets and says nothing about what the rest is safe for.

doc.shortHtml: The IANA media type $type is spelled with, for a Content-Type header or a stored record. One direction only: a case has a name, and a name never becomes a case.

params.name: type
params.descHtml: The case to spell, usually one detect just answered.

doc.returnHtml: The media type, as image/png — and application/octet-stream for Core\Mime\Type::Unknown, which is what a program that must send something should send for octets it could not name.

classes.surfaceHtml: detect(bytes $data): Mime\Type and mediaType(Mime\Type $type): string — type detection by magic bytes, from a fixed table of literal signatures rather than libmagic's rule interpreter, and never from a file extension: a type read off a name is a type an attacker chose. Core\Mime\Type is closed and its zero case is Unknown, so a caller compares against a case rather than against a spelling that may never occur, and a format serialized as text answers Unknown rather than a guess

classes.name: Core\Net
classes.surface: TCP/UDP/Unix sockets over the runtime's own reactor. Replaces `socket_*`, `stream_socket_*`, `fsockopen` — three PHP APIs for one job

doc.shortHtml: Opens a TCP connection to $host on $port, parking on the runtime's reactor while the handshake is in flight. Needs net.connect for the host, and the address it resolves to must not be one the address policy denies.

params.name: host
params.descHtml: A hostname or an IP address. It is checked against the grant before it is resolved, and the one address it resolves to is what the connection is made to.

params.name: port
params.descHtml: The port to connect to, 1 to 65535.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long the handshake may take. The bound is lifted once the connection is up, so a later read takes whatever bound its own caller names.

doc.returnHtml: An open Core\Net\Stream, closed with this request if the program does not close it first.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant net.connect for this host, the host resolves to no address, the address it resolves to is in a denied range, $port is not a port, or $within is not a positive length of time.
The handshake was still in flight when $within ran out.
The connection failed — refused, unreachable, or reset while it was being established.

doc.shortHtml: Binds a listening TCP socket to $address on $port. Needs net.listen for that exact endpoint; the address policy net.connect carries does not apply, because its terms invert under a bind.

params.name: address
params.descHtml: An IP address, such as 127.0.0.1, ::1 or 0.0.0.0. Not a hostname: the grant is matched against one endpoint, and a name resolving to two could not be the one an operator named.

params.name: port
params.descHtml: The port to bind, or 0 to let the operating system pick one — which Core\Net\Listener::port then reports.

doc.returnHtml: A bound Core\Net\Listener, closed with this request if the program does not close it first.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant net.listen for this endpoint, $address is not an IP address, or $port is not a port.
The operating system refused the bind — the port is taken, or the address is not one of this host's.

doc.shortHtml: Binds a datagram socket to $address on $port. Needs net.listen for that exact endpoint, exactly as a TCP bind does; sending to anywhere is a separate grant asked at Core\Net\Datagram::send.

params.name: address
params.descHtml: An IP address, such as 127.0.0.1, ::1 or 0.0.0.0. Not a hostname, for Core\Net::listen's reason: a grant names one endpoint.

params.name: port
params.descHtml: The port to bind, or 0 to let the operating system pick one — which Core\Net\Datagram::port then reports.

doc.returnHtml: A bound Core\Net\Datagram, closed with this request if the program does not close it first.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant net.listen for this endpoint, $address is not an IP address, or $port is not a port.
The operating system refused the bind — the port is taken, or the address is not one of this host's.

doc.shortHtml: Connects to the Unix-domain socket bound at $path, parking on the runtime's reactor while the connect is in flight. Needs net.local for that path, which is a grant of its own: net.connect never covers a path, and carries no policy that could read one.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: An absolute path to a bound socket. It is never read as a host and never as a URL — this is the member that takes a path, and no other one does.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait for the connect. It bounds this call alone, and a local connect waits at all only when the listener's backlog is full.

doc.returnHtml: A connected Core\Net\Stream, closed with this request if the program does not close it first.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant net.local for this path, this build has no Unix-domain transport, or $within is not a positive length of time.
The connect was still in flight after $within.
The operating system refused the path — nothing is bound there, no permission, or a name too long for the platform.

doc.shortHtml: Binds a listening Unix-domain socket at $path, creating it. Needs net.local for that path: the grant governs both ends, because a socket a program creates is one whatever finds it on this host may speak to.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: An absolute path the socket is created at. It must not exist yet, and it is not removed when the socket closes — the name may by then be something else's.

doc.returnHtml: A bound Core\Net\Listener, closed with this request if the program does not close it first. Its port throws: a socket bound at a path has none.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant net.local for this path, or this build has no Unix-domain transport.
The operating system refused the path — it exists already, the directory does not, or there is no permission to create it.

classes.surfaceHtml: TCP/UDP/Unix sockets over the runtime's own reactor. Replaces socket_, stream_socket_, fsockopen — three PHP APIs for one job

classes.name: Core\Net\Datagram
classes.summary: A UDP socket, returned by `Core\Net::bindDatagram`. `send` sends one message to an address, and `receive` waits for one message and returns it as a `Core\Net\Datagram\Message`.

doc.shortHtml: Sends one datagram to $host on $port and answers how many octets went. Needs net.connect for the host, and the address it resolves to must not be one the address policy denies — the same question a TCP connect is asked, asked here because this is where the address is named.

params.name: host
params.descHtml: A hostname or an IP address. It is checked against the grant before it is resolved, and the datagram goes to the one address it resolved to.

params.name: port
params.descHtml: The port to send to, 1 to 65535.

params.name: payload
params.descHtml: The octets of one message. There is no partial send: a message too large for the path is refused rather than split.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait for the socket to take the message. It bounds this call alone.

doc.returnHtml: How many octets went, which is $payload's length on every success.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant net.connect for this host, the host resolves to no address, the address it resolves to is in a denied range, $port is not a port, this handle is closed, or $within is not a positive length of time.
The socket would not take the message within $within.
The operating system refused the send — the message is over the maximum size, or the network is unreachable.

doc.shortHtml: Waits for one datagram, no longer than $within, and answers it together with who sent it. It asks no capability: the bind was granted when this socket was opened, and who sent the message was not this program's choice.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: How many octets to keep, capped at 64 KiB because no datagram is larger. A datagram arrives whole or not at all, so a message longer than this keeps what fits and the rest are gone — there is no second call that answers the tail.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait for a message. It bounds this call alone.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Net\Datagram\Message carrying the octets and the endpoint they came from.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed, or $within is not a positive length of time.
No datagram arrived within $within.
The operating system failed the receive — on Windows, this is also how an earlier send of this socket's is reported unreachable.

doc.shortHtml: The port this socket is bound to, which is how a program that asked for 0 learns the one the operating system picked.
doc.returnHtml: The bound port, 1 to 65535.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed.
The operating system would not answer for this socket.

doc.shortHtml: Closes this socket and gives its port and its reactor registration back. A request that forgets closes every socket it opened when it ends.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: This handle is already closed.

classes.summaryHtml: A UDP socket, returned by Core\Net::bindDatagram. send sends one message to an address, and receive waits for one message and returns it as a Core\Net\Datagram\Message.

classes.name: Core\Net\Datagram\Message
classes.summary: One message that `Core\Net\Datagram::receive` returned. `payload` gives its bytes, and `host` and `port` give the address it came from, which is where a reply goes.

doc.shortHtml: The octets this datagram carried, as tainted bytes. Truncated to the $max the receive named, if the message was longer than that.
doc.returnHtml: What arrived, which may be empty: a zero-length datagram is a message and not an absence.

doc.shortHtml: The address this datagram came from, written out — 127.0.0.1, ::1. A plain string, so it can be handed straight back to send, which asks the grant and the address policy about it exactly as it would about any other address.
doc.returnHtml: An IP address, never a hostname: nothing here is resolved backwards.

doc.shortHtml: The port this datagram came from, which is where a reply goes.
doc.returnHtml: The sender's port, 1 to 65535.

classes.summaryHtml: One message that Core\Net\Datagram::receive returned. payload gives its bytes, and host and port give the address it came from, which is where a reply goes.

classes.name: Core\Net\Listener
classes.summary: A TCP server socket, returned by `Core\Net::listen` and `Core\Net::listenLocal`. `accept` waits for the next client and returns a `Core\Net\Stream` for it.

doc.shortHtml: Waits for the next client to connect, for no longer than $within, and returns a Core\Net\Stream for that client. It needs no setting of its own: nvs.toml was checked when Core\Net::listen opened this socket.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait for a client. It is the limit for this call only.

doc.returnHtml: The connection to the client. The request closes it when it ends, if the program has not closed it before.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed, or $within is not a positive length of time.
No connection arrived within $within.
The operating system failed the accept.

doc.shortHtml: The port this listener is bound to, which is how a program that asked for 0 learns the one the operating system picked.
doc.returnHtml: The bound port, 1 to 65535.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed, or it is a listener Core\Net::listenLocal bound at a path, which has no port at all.
The operating system would not answer for this socket.

doc.shortHtml: Stops listening and gives the port back. Connections already accepted are unaffected: each is its own socket.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: This handle is already closed.

classes.summaryHtml: A TCP server socket, returned by Core\Net::listen and Core\Net::listenLocal. accept waits for the next client and returns a Core\Net\Stream for it.

classes.name: Core\Net\Stream
classes.summary: A connection to one client or server, returned by `Core\Net::connect`, `Core\Net::connectLocal` and `Core\Net\Listener::accept`. `read` and `write` move bytes, and each waits no longer than its `$within`.

doc.shortHtml: Reads whatever has arrived, up to $max octets, waiting no longer than $within. A short answer is ordinary and not an error: a socket reports what arrived, never what was asked for.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: The most octets to answer with. The buffer is capped below this where $max is larger than one read can usefully be.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait for the first octet. It bounds this call alone.

doc.returnHtml: The octets that arrived, as tainted bytes, or an empty bytes once the peer has closed its half — which is how the end of a stream is spelled.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed, or $within is not a positive length of time.
Nothing arrived within $within.
The connection failed — reset by the peer, or dropped by the network.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $payload to the peer, waiting no longer than $within, and answers how many octets the socket took. A write that took only some of them is ordinary: the caller sends the rest.

params.name: payload
params.descHtml: The octets to send.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait for the socket to take octets. It bounds this call alone.

doc.returnHtml: How many octets of $payload were written, which is between 0 and its length.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed, or $within is not a positive length of time.
The socket took nothing within $within.
The connection failed — reset by the peer, or its reading half closed.

doc.shortHtml: Closes this connection and gives its reactor registration back. A request that forgets closes every socket it opened when it ends.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: This handle is already closed.

classes.summaryHtml: A connection to one client or server, returned by Core\Net::connect, Core\Net::connectLocal and Core\Net\Listener::accept. read and write move bytes, and each waits no longer than its $within.

classes.name: Core\ObjectMap
classes.summary:
`array<T>` is list, stack, queue and dictionary, so `SplStack`, `SplQueue`, `SplDoublyLinkedList`,
`SplFixedArray`, `ArrayObject` and `ArrayIterator` are dropped as restatements of it. These three survive
because an insertion-ordered `string`-keyed hash cannot express them
(`rule:types/arrays`).
classes.surface: `set`, `get`, `has`, `remove`, `count`, `isEmpty`, `keys`, `values`, `clear`; `Iterable`

doc.shortHtml: Associates $value with $key, replacing whatever $key held; a key is matched by identity, never by equality.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key, matched by identity against the keys the map holds.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to store under $key.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; a key set again keeps its place in the insertion order.

doc.shortHtml: Answers what $key holds — ?V rather than a throwing read, because these types have no subscript and so no $a[$k] ?? $d to offer instead.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key to look up, matched by identity.

doc.returnHtml: The value stored under $key, or null where the map holds no key identical to it — which a stored null is indistinguishable from, so has is the question that tells the two apart.

doc.shortHtml: Whether the map holds a key identical to $key.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key to look for, matched by identity.

doc.returnHtml: true when the key is present — even where it holds null — and false otherwise.

doc.shortHtml: Drops $key and the value it held.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key to drop, matched by identity.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; a key the map does not hold is left alone rather than reported.

doc.shortHtml: Counts the pairs the map holds.
doc.returnHtml: The number of keys; 0 for an empty map.

doc.shortHtml: Whether the map holds no pairs.
doc.returnHtml: true for a map with no keys, false otherwise.

doc.shortHtml: Every key, as a list in insertion order — the same order a foreach over the map yields.
doc.returnHtml: A fresh array<K> list, empty for an empty map, whose positions pair with values().

doc.shortHtml: Every value, as a list in the order keys() answers its keys.
doc.returnHtml: A fresh array<V> list, empty for an empty map, whose positions pair with keys().

doc.shortHtml: Drops every pair, leaving the map empty.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the map itself is kept and can be filled again.

classes.summaryHtml: array<T> is list, stack, queue and dictionary, so SplStack, SplQueue, SplDoublyLinkedList, SplFixedArray, ArrayObject and ArrayIterator are dropped as restatements of it. These three survive because an insertion-ordered string-keyed hash cannot express them (rule:types/arrays).
classes.surfaceHtml: set, get, has, remove, count, isEmpty, keys, values, clear; Iterable

classes.name: Core\ObjectSet
classes.surface: `add`, `has`, `remove`, `count`, `isEmpty`, `union`, `intersect`, `diff`, `clear`; `Iterable`

doc.shortHtml: Adds $value unless the set already holds something identical to it.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to add, matched by identity.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; adding a value the set already holds changes nothing, and has is the spelling for whether it was there.

doc.shortHtml: Whether the set holds something identical to $value.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to look for, matched by identity.

doc.returnHtml: true when the value is a member, false otherwise.

doc.shortHtml: Drops $value from the set.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to drop, matched by identity.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; a value the set does not hold is left alone rather than reported.

doc.shortHtml: Counts the distinct values the set holds.
doc.returnHtml: The number of members; 0 for an empty set.

doc.shortHtml: Whether the set holds nothing.
doc.returnHtml: true for a set with no members, false otherwise.

doc.shortHtml: Builds a new set with every value that is in this set, in $other, or in both.

params.name: other
params.descHtml: The set to combine with.

doc.returnHtml: A new Core\ObjectSet<T>. The values of this set come first, in their order. Then the values of $other that are not in this set follow. Neither set is changed.

doc.shortHtml: Builds a new set with only the values that are in this set and also in $other.

params.name: other
params.descHtml: The set to intersect with.

doc.returnHtml: A new Core\ObjectSet<T>, in the order of this set. It is empty when the two sets have no value in common. Neither set is changed.

doc.shortHtml: Builds a new set with the values that are in this set and not in $other. The name is diff, the same as Core\Arr::diff.

params.name: other
params.descHtml: The set whose values are left out.

doc.returnHtml: A new Core\ObjectSet<T>, in the order of this set. It is empty when $other has every value of this set. Neither set is changed.

doc.shortHtml: Drops every member, leaving the set empty.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the set itself is kept and can be filled again.

classes.surfaceHtml: add, has, remove, count, isEmpty, union, intersect, diff, clear; Iterable

classes.name: Core\Os
classes.surface: host and process facts (`pid`, `hostname`, `cpuCount`, `residentBytes`, `loadAverage`). Replaces `posix_*` minus fork, `php_uname`, `getrusage`, `sys_getloadavg`. A **request's** memory is `Core\Budget`'s and never here — `residentBytes` is the process's resident set, which is the question `Core\Os` is entitled to answer

doc.shortHtml: Returns the number the operating system gives this process. This replaces PHP's getmypid. The number belongs to the whole process. Two requests served by the same process get the same number.
doc.returnHtml: The process number, which is larger than 0.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the name of the machine this program runs on. This replaces PHP's gethostname. It reads the name the machine has for itself, and it does not use the network.
doc.returnHtml: The machine's name.

errors.descHtml: The operating system did not return a name, or the name is not valid UTF-8.

doc.shortHtml: Returns how many CPU cores this program may use. A server or a container can limit a program to some of its cores. A program in a container with 2 cores on a machine with 96 cores gets 2. The web server starts this same number of workers.
doc.returnHtml: The number of cores. It is always 1 or more.

errors.descHtml: The operating system did not say how many cores this program may use.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the most memory this process has used so far, in bytes. This replaces the ru_maxrss figure of PHP's getrusage. On Windows it is the peak working set. The number covers every request the process has served, so it never gets smaller. For the memory of one request, use Core\Budget.
doc.returnHtml: The most memory the process has used, in bytes.

errors.descHtml: The operating system did not report the memory of this process.

doc.shortHtml: Returns how busy the machine is, as three numbers: the averages over the last 1, 5 and 15 minutes. This replaces PHP's sys_getloadavg. Each number counts the processes that are running or waiting to run. A number larger than cpuCount() means some processes are waiting.
doc.returnHtml: Three floats: the averages over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, in that order.

errors.descHtml: Windows does not keep a load average, so this method throws there. The message names the platform.

classes.surfaceHtml: host and process facts (pid, hostname, cpuCount, residentBytes, loadAverage). Replaces posix_* minus fork, php_uname, getrusage, sys_getloadavg. A request's memory is Core\Budget's and never here — residentBytes is the process's resident set, which is the question Core\Os is entitled to answer

doc.shortHtml: Runs $fn and returns everything it printed with echo. This replaces PHP's ob_start and ob_get_clean. The printed text does not reach the output. You can call capture inside another capture, and each call collects only what its own function printed.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: The function to run. Its return value is not used.

params.name: through
params.descHtml: A function that takes the collected output and returns new output of the same class. capture returns that new value. Without it, capture returns the output as it was printed.

doc.returnHtml: What $fn printed. In a web request it is a Core\Html\Markup. In every other program it is a Core\Cli\Text. It is empty when $fn printed nothing. Use echo to print it again without escaping it twice. Use is to check the class, then its text method to get a string. Output from Core\Debug::dump is not collected.

errors.descHtml: The through function returned a value of a different class than it was given.

classes.name: Core\Password
classes.surface: `hash(secret string): string`, `verify(secret string, string): bool`, `needsRehash(string): bool` — **no algorithm argument**. `verify` and `needsRehash` also read a PHP-stored bcrypt hash (`verify` verifies it, `needsRehash` answers `true`); `hash` writes only Argon2id. Replaces `password_hash`, `password_verify`, `crypt`

doc.shortHtml: Turns $password into a hash you can store, using Argon2id. The library chooses the settings, so there is no algorithm or cost argument. The result contains everything verify needs later: the algorithm, the settings, a random salt and the hash itself.

params.name: password
params.descHtml: The password to hash. It may be a secret string. The result is not secret, because it is made to be stored.

doc.returnHtml: A string such as $argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$<salt>$<hash>. Each call uses a new random salt, so the same password gives a different string every time.

errors.descHtml: The request cannot use the 19 MiB of memory that one hash needs.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $password is the password $hash was made from. It uses the settings stored in $hash, so a hash made with older settings still works. It reads the Argon2id strings hash writes, and bcrypt hashes that PHP wrote with $2y$, $2a$ or $2b$. The check takes the same time for every wrong password.

params.name: password
params.descHtml: The password somebody typed. It may be a secret string.

params.name: hash
params.descHtml: The stored hash: a string from hash, or a bcrypt hash that PHP stored.

doc.returnHtml: true when $password matches $hash, false when it does not.

errors.descHtml: $hash is not a password hash this class can read. It does not parse, it uses another algorithm, or it starts with $2x$. This usually means the stored value is broken, so it is an error and not false.
$hash asks for too much work: more than 1 GiB of memory, too many passes over that memory, or a bcrypt cost above 17. It is also thrown when the request cannot use the memory the hash needs.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $hash is weaker than a hash hash makes today. Call it right after verify returns true. If it returns true, hash the password again and store the new hash.

params.name: hash
params.descHtml: The stored hash to check.

doc.returnHtml: true when $hash uses another algorithm or version, or less memory or fewer passes than hash uses now. Every bcrypt hash returns true. false when $hash is as strong as a new hash, or stronger.

errors.descHtml: $hash is not a password hash at all. A hash that uses another algorithm does not throw: it returns true.

classes.surfaceHtml: hash(secret string): string, verify(secret string, string): bool, needsRehash(string): bool — no algorithm argument. verify and needsRehash also read a PHP-stored bcrypt hash (verify verifies it, needsRehash answers true); hash writes only Argon2id. Replaces password_hash, password_verify, crypt

classes.name: Core\Path
classes.summary:
Pure string algebra over paths. **No member touches the disk**, so none needs a capability, and every member
but `fromCwd` is constant-foldable. Everything that reads or writes is `Core\IO` (§ 14) — that split is the
point. `fromCwd` reads the process's working directory, and throws while a request is being answered
(`rule:programs/relative-paths-resolve-from-their-file`).

constants.name: SEPARATOR
constants.descHtml: The separator this platform's paths are rendered with — \ on Windows and / everywhere else, as DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR is; every member emits it and accepts both.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the last part of $path: the file name, or the name of the last folder. A separator at the end is ignored, so /srv/shop/ gives shop. This replaces PHP's basename.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

params.name: withoutExtension
params.descHtml: When true, the extension is removed, so report.pdf gives report. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The name. For a path that is only a root, such as / or C:\, the result is the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the folder that contains $path. The option levels goes up more than one folder. This replaces PHP's dirname.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

params.name: levels
params.descHtml: How many parts to remove from the end. The default is 1. With 0, the result is the path with its separators cleaned up. A number larger than the path stops at the root.

doc.returnHtml: The folder, written with Path::SEPARATOR. When nothing is left, the result is the root for an absolute path and . for a relative one. dirname('') is ., and PHP returns ''.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the extension of the last part of $path: the text after the last ., without the dot. This replaces PHP's pathinfo($path, PATHINFO_EXTENSION).

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: The extension, or null when there is none. A name that starts with a dot, such as .gitignore, has none. A name that ends with a dot, such as report., has none too. PHP returns gitignore and '' for these two.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $path with the extension of its last part changed to $extension. When $extension is null, the extension is removed. PHP has no function for this.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

params.name: extension
params.descHtml: The new extension, without its dot, the same way Core\Path::extension returns it. It may have a dot inside, such as tar.gz. null removes the extension.

doc.returnHtml: The new path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR.

errors.descHtml: $extension is empty, starts with a ., or contains / or \. Or $path has no file name, such as / or ''.

doc.shortHtml: Adds each of $segments to the end of $base, with one separator between each part. This replaces the $a . "/" . $b that PHP programs write. Only $base decides where the result starts. A segment that starts with / or a drive is added after $base and does not replace it.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The first path. The result starts where this path starts.

params.name: segments
params.descHtml: Any number of paths to add, in order. A leading /, \ or drive in one of them is removed.

doc.returnHtml: The joined path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. With no segments, the result is $base with its extra separators removed. A .. segment stays in the result and still means the parent folder.

doc.shortHtml: Splits $path into its parts: the folders and the file name, in order. This replaces PHP's explode("/", $path). Core\Path::join puts the parts back together into the same path.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: The parts in order. When the path starts at a root, the root is the first part: /, a drive such as C:\, or a share such as \\server\share\. The root is written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. No part is empty, because a repeated separator or one at the end adds nothing. The empty path gives an empty array.

members.name: normalize
members.replaces: the lexical half of `realpath` — resolves `.`/`..` **without** touching the disk

doc.shortHtml: Removes the . and .. parts from $path and writes it with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. The method works on the text only and never looks at the disk. The result can still point outside a folder, so it does not make a path safe. Core\IO::within checks that.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: The same path without . parts, and with each .. removing the folder before it. A .. at the start of a relative path stays. A .. that would go above a root is removed, because a root has no parent. A repeated separator or one at the end is removed. The empty path gives ..

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $path starts at a root. A root is a separator, a drive followed by a separator, or a network share. The check is the same on every platform.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: true for /tmp, \tmp, C:/log and \\server\share. false for a relative path such as logs/app.log, for C:log, and for the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the path that leads from the folder $base to $path. The . and .. parts of both paths are removed first, as Core\Path::normalize does. PHP has no function for this.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The place the result leads to.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The folder the result starts from. The result has one .. for each folder of $base that $path does not share.

doc.returnHtml: A relative path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. It is . when both paths name the same place. It is null when no relative path exists: one path is absolute and the other is not, the paths start at different roots, or $base starts with more .. parts than $path does. Folder names are compared byte for byte. A drive letter and a server name ignore upper and lower case.

doc.shortHtml: Joins $path to the folder the program was started from, and returns the full path. Use it for a path that a user typed on the command line.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. A relative path is joined to the working folder. A full path is returned as it is, with its . and .. parts removed.

doc.returnHtml: A full path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR, with its . and .. parts removed. The method does not check that the file exists. The result is not tainted, so you can pass a path from Core\Cli::arguments to Core\IO::read.

errors.descHtml: The program is answering a web request. A server has no working folder that belongs to the app.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the full path of the source file that contains this call. The compiler writes the path in place of the call, so the call costs nothing when the program runs.
doc.returnHtml: The full path of the file, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. In a bundled program, the folder is the one beside the executable.

errors.descHtml: The source was given to the compiler as text, so there is no file to name.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the full path of the folder that contains this source file. The compiler writes the path in place of the call, so the call costs nothing when the program runs.

params.name: join
params.descHtml: A relative path, written directly in the code as a string such as 'data'. It is added to the folder. A variable or a full path does not compile. Use Core\Path::join(Core\Path::thisDir(), $part) for a part the program builds.

doc.returnHtml: The full path of the folder, with $join added when you give one, and with its . and .. parts removed.

errors.descHtml: The source was given to the compiler as text, so there is no folder to name.

classes.summaryHtml: Pure string algebra over paths. No member touches the disk, so none needs a capability, and every member but fromCwd is constant-foldable. Everything that reads or writes is Core\IO (§ 14) — that split is the point. fromCwd reads the process's working directory, and throws while a request is being answered (rule:programs/relative-paths-resolve-from-their-file).

classes.name: Core\Process
classes.surface: `run`, `spawn` — argv only, never a shell string

members.name: run
members.signature: run(string $path, array<string> $argv, {cwd?: string, env?: array<string>, timeout?: Core\Time\Duration}): Core\Process\Result

doc.shortHtml: Runs the program at $path with the arguments in $argv, and waits until it ends. The program is started directly, never through a shell, so nothing needs escaping. Needs the process.exec capability for the program. This replaces PHP's exec, system, shell_exec, passthru and the backtick operator.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The program to start, as an absolute path. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it. PATH is not searched, so ls means a file named ls in that folder.

params.name: argv
params.descHtml: The arguments, one in each element: ["-n", "1", $host]. An element with a space, a quote or a ; in it is still one argument, on every platform.

params.name: cwd
params.descHtml: The folder the program starts in, as an absolute path. A relative path must be written directly in the code, and is joined to the folder of this file. Without it, the program starts in the same folder as this program.

params.name: env
params.descHtml: The environment variables of the program, as name => value. This replaces all of them, so a variable that is not in the array is not set. Without it, the program gets the same variables as this program. A secret value must be revealed first.

params.name: timeout
params.descHtml: The longest time the program may run, counted from the start. When it passes, the program is stopped and a TimeoutError is thrown.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Process\Result with the exit code and everything the program wrote to its output and to its error output. The program cannot write to this program's own output, so the two never mix.

errors.descHtml: process.exec does not allow this program, or it is a .bat, .cmd or .ps1 file. Those are not allowed on any platform, because Windows starts them through a shell. The error is also thrown when the program writes more than [limits] max_output in total. Then the program is stopped and nothing is returned. It is also thrown when cwd is a relative path, when an env name is empty or has a = in it, or when timeout is zero or shorter.
The program was still running when timeout passed. The program is stopped and nothing is returned.
The program could not be started or waited for. For example, nothing is at the path, the file is not a program, or the cwd folder does not exist.

members.name: spawn
members.signature: spawn(string $path, array<string> $argv, {cwd?: string, env?: array<string>, timeout?: Core\Time\Duration}): Core\Process\Handle

doc.shortHtml: Starts the program at $path with the arguments in $argv, and returns at once while the program runs. The handle it returns reads the program's output and writes to its input. The program is started directly, never through a shell. Needs the process.exec capability for the program. This replaces PHP's proc_open.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The program to start, as an absolute path or a path relative to the working directory. PATH is not searched.

params.name: argv
params.descHtml: The arguments, one in each element. An element with a space, a quote or a ; in it is still one argument, on every platform.

params.name: cwd
params.descHtml: The folder the program starts in, as an absolute path. A relative path must be written directly in the code, and is joined to the folder of this file. Without it, the program starts in the same folder as this program.

params.name: env
params.descHtml: The environment variables of the program, as name => value. This replaces all of them, so a variable that is not in the array is not set. Without it, the program gets the same variables as this program. A secret value must be revealed first.

params.name: timeout
params.descHtml: The longest time the program may run, counted from the start. When it passes, the program is stopped and a TimeoutError is thrown.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Process\Handle for the running program. Other requests keep running while this one waits on the handle. The program is stopped when the request that started it ends.

errors.descHtml: process.exec does not allow this program, or it is a .bat, .cmd or .ps1 file. Those are not allowed on any platform, because Windows starts them through a shell. It is also thrown when cwd is a relative path, when an env name is empty or has a = in it, or when timeout is zero or shorter.
The program could not be started. For example, nothing is at the path, the file is not a program, or the cwd folder does not exist.

classes.surfaceHtml: run, spawn — argv only, never a shell string

classes.name: Core\Process\Handle
classes.summary: A program that `Core\Process::spawn` started and that may still be running. `readStdout` and `readStderr` read its output a part at a time, and `writeStdin` writes to its input. `wait` waits for the end and returns a `Core\Process\Result`, and `kill` stops the program at once. A program that is still running when the request ends is stopped.

doc.shortHtml: Waits until the program writes to its standard output, and returns what it wrote. Call it in a loop to read the output one part at a time while the program runs. Other requests keep running while this one waits.
doc.returnHtml: The next part of the output, as bytes, up to 64 KiB. A part is whatever has arrived: it can be less than one line or several lines. At the end of the output the result is null, and every later call also returns null. Use as string to convert a part to text.

errors.descHtml: The timeout given to spawn has passed. The program is stopped, and every later call except kill throws this error too.
The operating system could not read the output. The output is then closed, so the next call returns null.

doc.shortHtml: Waits until the program writes to its standard error, and returns what it wrote. Programs write their error messages and warnings there. It works like readStdout, and the two outputs are never mixed.
doc.returnHtml: The next part of the error output, as bytes, up to 64 KiB. At the end of the error output the result is null, and every later call also returns null. Use as string to convert a part to text.

errors.descHtml: The timeout given to spawn has passed. The program is stopped, and every later call except kill throws this error too.
The operating system could not read the error output. The error output is then closed, so the next call returns null.
