doc.shortHtml: Sends $data to the program's standard input. The call waits until the program has taken all of it. A tainted value is allowed here, because the program reads it as data and does not run it as a command.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The data to send, as bytes. All of it is sent. Use as bytes to convert a string.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The input stays open, so you can call writeStdin again. wait closes the input, and then the program sees the end of it.

errors.descHtml: The timeout given to spawn has passed. The program is stopped, and every later call except kill throws this error too.
The operating system could not send the data. This happens most often when the program has already ended, or after wait.

doc.shortHtml: Closes the program's standard input, waits until the program ends, and returns its result. While it waits, the server keeps handling other requests.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Process\Result with the exit code, and the output and error output that readStdout and readStderr did not read yet. If you already read all of the output, both are empty. A second call returns the same exit code and empty output.

errors.descHtml: The output that was not read yet is larger than [limits] max_output. The program is then stopped.
The timeout given to spawn has passed. The program is stopped, and every later call except kill throws this error too.
The operating system could not read the output or get the exit code.

doc.shortHtml: Stops the program at once, whatever it is doing. If the program has already ended, kill does nothing and throws no error. A program that nobody stops is stopped when the request that started it ends.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. Call wait afterwards to get the exit code. It is not 0 for a program that was stopped.

errors.descHtml: The operating system could not stop the program.

classes.summaryHtml: A program that Core\Process::spawn started and that may still be running. readStdout and readStderr read its output a part at a time, and writeStdin writes to its input. wait waits for the end and returns a Core\Process\Result, and kill stops the program at once. A program that is still running when the request ends is stopped.

classes.name: Core\Process\Result
classes.summary: The result of a program that has ended. `Core\Process::run` and `Core\Process\Handle::wait` return one. `exitCode` returns the program's exit code, and `stdout` and `stderr` return what it wrote to its output and its error output. The program has already ended, so these methods never throw an error.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the exit code of the program. Most programs return 0 when they succeed, and another number when they fail.
doc.returnHtml: The exit code, as an int. On Linux and macOS, it is -1 when a signal stopped the program before it could return an exit code.

doc.shortHtml: Returns everything the program wrote to its standard output.
doc.returnHtml: The output, as bytes. A program can write data that is not valid text, so the result is not a string. Use as string to convert it to text. That throws an error if the output is not valid UTF-8.

doc.shortHtml: Returns everything the program wrote to its standard error. Programs write their error messages and warnings there. This output is never mixed with stdout.
doc.returnHtml: The error output, as bytes. Use as string to convert it to text.

classes.summaryHtml: The result of a program that has ended. Core\Process::run and Core\Process\Handle::wait return one. exitCode returns the program's exit code, and stdout and stderr return what it wrote to its output and its error output. The program has already ended, so these methods never throw an error.

classes.name: Core\Program
classes.surface: `implementing<T>()`, and `implementingWith<I, T>(string $member = "")` — the same enumeration with one attribute retrieval joined per class, each row holding the instance and its matching payload or null — and `constructors<T, C>()`, the same classes in the same order, each row holding the class name and a `make` callable typed `C` that builds it

doc.shortHtml: Returns a new object of every class that is a T. T is an interface or a class, and you write it between < and >: Core\Program::implementing<Module>(). When T is a class that is not abstract, T itself is in the list. Abstract classes are not included. Each class needs a constructor without arguments, or the program does not compile. Novis finds the classes when it compiles the program, so nothing is searched while it runs.
doc.returnHtml: An array<T> with one new object per class, sorted by class name. Every call creates new objects. The array is empty when no class is a T.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the same objects as implementing<I>(), each with one attribute of its class. You write the interface or class I and the shape T of the attribute between < and >: Core\Program::implementingWith<Page, {path: string}>("render"). Novis reads the attributes when it compiles the program, so nothing is searched while it runs.

params.name: member
params.descHtml: The name of the method, property or constructor parameter that has the attribute. An empty string reads the attributes of the class itself.

doc.returnHtml: An array with one row per class, sorted by class name. Each row is {instance: I, attribute: ?T}. attribute is null when the class has no attribute of the shape T. Two matching attributes on one class do not compile.

members.name: constructors
members.signature: constructors<T, C>(): array<{class: string, make: C}>

doc.shortHtml: Returns a function for every class that implementing<T>() lists, in the same order. You write the interface or class T and a function type C between < and >: Core\Program::constructors<Module, callable(Config): Module>(). Each function creates a new object of its class with the arguments you pass. A class whose constructor does not accept these arguments does not compile.
doc.returnHtml: An array with one row per class, sorted by class name. Each row is {class: string, make: C}. class is the full class name. No object is created until you call make.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a text that identifies this version of the program. It is a BLAKE3 hash of all the compiled code and of the environment it was compiled for. The same code on the same server gives the same value on every run.
doc.returnHtml: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The value changes when the code or the environment changes. It is safe to print, because a hash does not show any source code.

errors.descHtml: The program was started without an identity. nvs run always gives a program one, so this happens only when a program is started some other way.

classes.surfaceHtml: implementing<T>(), and implementingWith<I, T>(string $member = "") — the same enumeration with one attribute retrieval joined per class, each row holding the instance and its matching payload or null — and constructors<T, C>(), the same classes in the same order, each row holding the class name and a make callable typed C that builds it

classes.name: Core\Queue
classes.summary: Runs work in the background. `push` saves a job as a row in the database set by `[queue] connection`, and a worker runs the job later. Inside a transaction on that connection, the job is saved only when the transaction commits. `status`, `cancel` and `delete` work on one job. `stats` and `purge` work on a whole queue.

members.name: push
members.signature: push(string $script, {args?: mixed, queue?: string, runAt?: Core\Time\Instant, maxAttempts?: uint, backoff?: Core\Time\Duration, key?: string, tag?: string, grants?: array<string>, memory?: string, cpuTime?: string, wallTime?: string, maxOutput?: string}): Core\Queue\Id

doc.shortHtml: Adds a job that runs $script in the background. The job is a row in the database set by [queue] connection. Inside a transaction on that connection, the job is saved only when the transaction commits. If the transaction rolls back, the job is not saved.

params.name: script
params.descHtml: The path of the file a worker runs, written the way spawn script writes one. A relative path starts at the folder of the file that calls push. It is a file, not a class or a function, so the job has no captured variables.

params.name: args
params.descHtml: The data the job receives. It is copied into the row and decoded into the types the job declares. It is never passed by reference, because the worker usually runs in another process.

params.name: queue
params.descHtml: The name of the queue the job goes in. Each worker takes jobs from the queues it is configured for, so you can keep slow work and fast work apart.

params.name: runAt
params.descHtml: The earliest time a worker may start the job. The default is now.

params.name: maxAttempts
params.descHtml: How many times the job may run before it moves to the dead-letter table (the table of jobs that failed too often). The default is [queue] max_attempts. The number is always finite, so a job cannot retry forever.

params.name: backoff
params.descHtml: The base wait between two attempts. The wait grows after each failed attempt, and the worker adds a small random amount. The default is one second.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: A key that stops duplicate jobs. While a job with this key is still pending, a second push with the same key adds nothing. It returns the id of the pending job.

params.name: tag
params.descHtml: A group name for the job. Many jobs can have the same tag. Only purge reads it, to delete one group of jobs. You cannot add a tag after the push.

params.name: grants
params.descHtml: The capabilities the job may use, written the way nvs.toml grants them. The list may only contain capabilities this request has. The default is what this request has. [] gives the job no capabilities.

params.name: memory
params.descHtml: The memory limit for the job, written like [limits] memory. [limits.hard] sets the highest value allowed. The default is the limit of this request.

params.name: cpuTime
params.descHtml: The CPU time limit for the job, written like [limits] cpu_time. It follows the same rules as memory.

params.name: wallTime
params.descHtml: The real time limit for the job, written like [limits] wall_time. It follows the same rules as memory.

params.name: maxOutput
params.descHtml: The limit on the output the job may print, written like [limits] max_output. It follows the same rules as memory.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Queue\Id for the new job. You pass it to status, cancel and delete. When key finds a pending job, it is the id of that job.

errors.descHtml: The configuration has no [queue] block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet. It is also thrown when grants contains a capability this request does not have.
maxAttempts is 0, or backoff is negative. It is also thrown when grants contains a name that is not a capability, or a limit is one this request may not set.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the insert. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the table yet.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the current state of one job, as a Core\Queue\State case. Every call reads the state from the database.

params.name: job
params.descHtml: The Core\Queue\Id that push returned. It identifies the job and its queue.

doc.returnHtml: Pending while the job waits, also while its runAt time or its backoff has not passed. Claimed while a worker runs it, Succeeded after it ran, Dead after it used all its attempts, and Cancelled after cancel stopped it.

errors.descHtml: The configuration has no [queue] block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet. It is also thrown when neither table has the job, for example because delete deleted it.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the query. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the tables yet.

doc.shortHtml: Removes one job from the queue if it is still waiting. A job that a worker already started keeps running, because cancel does not stop work in progress.

params.name: job
params.descHtml: The Core\Queue\Id that push returned. It identifies the job and its queue.

doc.returnHtml: true if this call cancelled the job. false if the job was no longer waiting: a worker took it, it already ran, or an earlier cancel removed it. After true, status returns Cancelled.

errors.descHtml: The configuration has no [queue] block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the update. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the table yet.

doc.shortHtml: Counts the jobs of one queue. The result has five numbers: waiting jobs, running jobs, attempts used, jobs in the dead-letter table, and the attempts those jobs used. All five are read at the same moment.

params.name: queue
params.descHtml: The name of the queue, the same name push used in its queue option. Each call counts one queue.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Queue\Stats. Each number is a method, so you write $stats->pending(), not $stats->pending.

errors.descHtml: The configuration has no [queue] block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the query. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the tables yet.

doc.shortHtml: Deletes the row of one job. The row can be in the jobs table or in the dead-letter table. A job that a worker is running is not deleted. You need the queue.purge capability for the queue of the job.

params.name: job
params.descHtml: The Core\Queue\Id that push returned. It still works after the job moves to the dead-letter table.

doc.returnHtml: true if this call deleted the row. false if there was nothing to delete: a worker is running the job, the job is not in this queue, or an earlier delete deleted it. After true, the row is gone, so status throws an error for this job.

errors.descHtml: The configuration grants no queue.purge for the queue of the job. A server has no such grant until the person who runs it adds one. It is also thrown when there is no [queue] block, or the database driver cannot run statements yet.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the delete. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the tables yet.

members.name: purge
members.signature: purge(string $queue, {state?: Core\Queue\State, tag?: string, before?: Core\Time\Instant, limit?: uint}): uint

doc.shortHtml: Deletes the finished jobs of a queue and returns how many rows it deleted. Without state, it deletes the Succeeded and Cancelled jobs. Dead and Pending jobs are deleted only when you pass that state. Claimed jobs are never deleted. One call deletes at most limit rows, so you call it again until it returns 0. You need the queue.purge capability for the queue.

params.name: queue
params.descHtml: The name of the queue. It must match the name push used exactly. The queue.purge capability is checked for this name.

params.name: state
params.descHtml: One Core\Queue\State to delete in place of the default ones. Dead deletes from the dead-letter table. Pending deletes jobs that have not run yet. Claimed throws an error, because a worker is running those jobs.

params.name: tag
params.descHtml: Deletes only the jobs that push gave this tag.

params.name: before
params.descHtml: Deletes only the jobs added before this time. This is the time of the push, not the time of the next attempt.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: The most rows one call deletes, oldest first. The default is 1000. A delete without a limit can lock the table for a long time, and every push waits for it.

doc.returnHtml: The number of rows this call deleted, and 0 when nothing matched. while (Core\Queue::purge('email') > 0) {} deletes all of them, one batch at a time.

errors.descHtml: state is Core\Queue\State::Claimed. A worker is running those jobs, so their rows cannot be deleted.

The configuration grants no queue.purge for this queue. A server has no such grant until the person who runs it adds one. It is also thrown when there is no [queue] block, or the database driver cannot run statements yet.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the delete. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the tables yet.

classes.summaryHtml: Runs work in the background. push saves a job as a row in the database set by [queue] connection, and a worker runs the job later. Inside a transaction on that connection, the job is saved only when the transaction commits. status, cancel and delete work on one job. stats and purge work on a whole queue.

classes.name: Core\Queue\Stats
classes.summary: The numbers that `Core\Queue::stats` returns for one queue. All five are read at the same moment. Each number is a method, so you write `$stats->pending()`, not `$stats->pending`.

doc.shortHtml: The number of jobs that wait for a worker. This includes jobs whose runAt time is still in the future, and jobs that wait between two attempts.
doc.returnHtml: A uint. It is 0 for a new queue and for a queue with no work left.

doc.shortHtml: The number of jobs that a worker is running now. A job whose worker stopped is still counted here. After the [queue] visibility time, another worker can start it again.
doc.returnHtml: A uint. When it equals the number of jobs your workers can run at once, the queue is busy but not stuck.

doc.shortHtml: The total number of attempts the jobs of this queue have used. If this number grows and pending does not, jobs are failing and running again.
doc.returnHtml: A uint for the jobs table only. The jobs in the dead-letter table are counted by deadLettered and deadAttempts.

doc.shortHtml: The number of jobs that used all their attempts and are now in the dead-letter table. These jobs did not finish, so this is a good number to alert on.
doc.returnHtml: A uint. It goes down only when purge or delete deletes a job from the dead-letter table.

doc.shortHtml: The total number of attempts the jobs in the dead-letter table used. Divide it by deadLettered to see how many attempts a job uses before it fails for good.
doc.returnHtml: A uint for the dead-letter table only. Every attempt is counted in this number or in attempts, never in both. Add the two to get the total.

classes.summaryHtml: The numbers that Core\Queue::stats returns for one queue. All five are read at the same moment. Each number is a method, so you write $stats->pending(), not $stats->pending.

classes.name: Core\Random
classes.summary:
`Core\Random` is a CSPRNG, always — PHP's `rand`/`mt_rand`/`shuffle`/`str_shuffle`/`array_rand` and its
newer `Random\Randomizer` OOP twin all collapse into it, and none of the insecure generators survives
under any name.

doc.shortHtml: Draws an integer uniformly from [$min, $max], inclusive at both ends, from the CSPRNG — as random_int does, replacing rand and mt_rand as well.

params.name: min
params.descHtml: The lowest value the draw may answer.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: The highest value the draw may answer.

doc.returnHtml: An int in the range, without bias; $min itself when the two bounds are equal.

errors.descHtml: $min is above $max — the range is empty, and the bounds are not swapped.

doc.shortHtml: Draws a float uniformly from the half-open interval [0, 1), replacing lcg_value and the mt_rand() / mt_getrandmax() idiom.
doc.returnHtml: A float with 53 random bits; 0.0 is drawable and 1.0 is not.

doc.shortHtml: Draws $count bytes from the CSPRNG as a raw buffer — a key, a nonce or an IV — as random_bytes does, replacing openssl_random_pseudo_bytes as well.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: How many bytes to draw; at least one.

doc.returnHtml: A bytes value of exactly $count octets, unrendered — Core\Random::token is the hex spelling.

errors.descHtml: $count is 0, as random_bytes(0) is a ValueError, or is larger than a buffer this process can allocate.

doc.shortHtml: Draws $bytes bytes from the CSPRNG and renders them as lower-case hex — the bin2hex(random_bytes(…)) idiom, for a session identifier or a reset link.

params.name: bytes
params.descHtml: How many bytes of entropy to draw, 32 by default — the answer is twice as many characters.

doc.returnHtml: A string of 2 * $bytes hex digits, 0–9 and a–f.

errors.descHtml: $bytes is 0 — the empty string is a token every other empty token equals — or the draw or its rendering is larger than a buffer this process can allocate.

doc.shortHtml: Draws one entry of $a uniformly and answers its value, replacing array_rand in its one-element spelling — the value, where array_rand answers the key.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to draw from.

doc.returnHtml: One entry's value; null when $a is empty, which over an array<?T> is indistinguishable from drawing a null entry.

doc.shortHtml: Draws $count distinct entries of $a uniformly, replacing array_rand with a count — in random order, where array_rand keeps the subject's order.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to draw from.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: How many distinct entries to draw; at most the array's size.

doc.returnHtml: A fresh list of the drawn values under 0, 1, … keys, in random order; the subject's keys are discarded, and $a is unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $count is above the number of entries $a holds.

doc.shortHtml: Answers every entry of $a in a uniformly random order, replacing shuffle and str_shuffle — a fresh array rather than a reordering in place.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to reorder.

doc.returnHtml: A fresh list of all the values under 0, 1, … keys — the subject's keys are discarded, as shuffle renumbers — and $a is unchanged.

classes.summaryHtml: Core\Random is a CSPRNG, always — PHP's rand/mt_rand/shuffle/str_shuffle/array_rand and its newer Random\Randomizer OOP twin all collapse into it, and none of the insecure generators survives under any name.

classes.name: Core\Random\Seeded
classes.summary: A random generator that starts from a seed you give it, so the same seed gives the same values every time. Use it for tests and simulations. For a key, a code or a token, use `Core\Random`.

doc.shortHtml: Draws an integer uniformly from [$min, $max], inclusive at both ends, from this generator's own sequence — Core\Random::int's answer, reproducibly.

params.name: min
params.descHtml: The lowest value the draw may answer.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: The highest value the draw may answer.

doc.returnHtml: An int in the range, without bias; $min itself when the two bounds are equal.

errors.descHtml: $min is above $max — the range is empty, and the bounds are not swapped.

doc.shortHtml: Draws a float uniformly from the half-open interval [0, 1) from this generator's own sequence — Core\Random::float's answer, reproducibly.
doc.returnHtml: A float with 53 random bits; 0.0 is drawable and 1.0 is not.

doc.shortHtml: Draws $count bytes from this generator's own sequence as a raw buffer — a fixture, never a key, since a reproducible buffer is a secret anyone holding the seed has.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: How many bytes to draw; at least one.

doc.returnHtml: A bytes value of exactly $count octets, unrendered.

errors.descHtml: $count is 0, as Core\Random::bytes's own draw of nothing is, or is larger than a buffer this process can allocate.

doc.shortHtml: Draws $bytes bytes from this generator's own sequence and renders them as lower-case hex — a stable identifier for a fixture, never a session token.

params.name: bytes
params.descHtml: How many bytes of entropy to draw, 32 by default — the answer is twice as many characters.

doc.returnHtml: A string of 2 * $bytes hex digits, 0–9 and a–f.

errors.descHtml: $bytes is 0, or the draw or its rendering is larger than a buffer this process can allocate.

doc.shortHtml: Draws one entry of $a uniformly from this generator's own sequence and answers its value — Core\Random::pick's answer, reproducibly.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to draw from.

doc.returnHtml: One entry's value; null when $a is empty, which over an array<?T> is indistinguishable from drawing a null entry.

doc.shortHtml: Draws $count distinct entries of $a uniformly from this generator's own sequence — Core\Random::sample's answer, reproducibly.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to draw from.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: How many distinct entries to draw; at most the array's size.

doc.returnHtml: A fresh list of the drawn values under 0, 1, … keys, in drawn order; the subject's keys are discarded, and $a is unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $count is above the number of entries $a holds.

doc.shortHtml: Answers every entry of $a in an order drawn from this generator's own sequence — Core\Random::shuffle's answer, reproducibly.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to reorder.

doc.returnHtml: A fresh list of all the values under 0, 1, … keys — the subject's keys are discarded — and $a is unchanged.
