classes.name: Core\RateLimit
classes.surface: `consume(tainted string $key, uint $limit, Duration $per, {burst?, cost?}): RateLimit\Decision` over the shared store, and `shed(…)` per core and approximate. `Decision` is readonly `allowed: bool`, `limit: uint`, `remaining: uint`, `retryAfter: ?Duration`. Both **neutral**; a `secret` key is refused; an unreachable store throws

members.name: consume
members.signature: consume(string $key, uint $limit, Core\Time\Duration $per, {burst?: uint, cost?: uint}): Core\RateLimit\Decision

doc.shortHtml: Charges $cost units against $key's allowance of $limit per $per in the shared store, and answers whether this arrival is inside the limit.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: What the allowance is per — an account, a tenant, an API key id. tainted is admitted, since a key is one opaque value on the wire; a secret is refused, since keying on one writes it into a store, and the fix is to key on Core\Hash::of of it.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: How many units $per admits — the drain rate, not a ceiling on any one instant.

params.name: per
params.descHtml: The period $limit units are admitted over.

params.name: burst
params.descHtml: How much may arrive at once; defaults to $limit, which admits a whole period's worth in one instant.

params.name: cost
params.descHtml: What this one call weighs, so an expensive endpoint may charge five units of the same quota; defaults to 1.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\RateLimit\Decision. Its retryAfter is null exactly when it is allowed, and is the exact wait until the arrival would be admitted otherwise — never an estimate, and never rounded up to the next window.

errors.descHtml: The shared store cannot be reached or refused the command. It is never answered as allowed: whether this limiter fails open or closed is knowledge only the call site has, so the decision is thrown to it.

No [cache.shared] url is configured, or cache.shared is not granted — a deployment mistake rather than the world saying no, and deliberately not the class the fail-open catch around this member holds. Also $limit, $per or $burst at zero, a period too short to divide into $limit units, and a $cost larger than $burst, which no wait could admit.

members.name: shed
members.signature: shed(string $key, uint $limit, Core\Time\Duration $per, {burst?: uint, cost?: uint}): Core\RateLimit\Decision

doc.shortHtml: Charges $cost units against $key's allowance of $limit per $per in this core's own memory, and answers whether this arrival is inside the limit — the approximate tier, for dropping load rather than for enforcing a promise.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: What the allowance is per. tainted is admitted and a secret refused, for consume's reasons.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: How many units $per admits on this core: a limit of 100 across eight cores admits up to 800, which is why a number somebody was promised belongs to consume instead.

params.name: per
params.descHtml: The period $limit units are admitted over.

params.name: burst
params.descHtml: How much may arrive at once; defaults to $limit.

params.name: cost
params.descHtml: What this one call weighs; defaults to 1.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\RateLimit\Decision, answered from this core's memory and so reaching no store: there is nothing to be unreachable, and this member does not throw for one. Its arrivals are held in Core\Cache's local tier, which may forget an entry at any time — a forgotten key admits a burst, which is the approximation the tier is chosen for.

errors.descHtml: $limit, $per or $burst at zero, a period too short to divide into $limit units, and a $cost larger than $burst, which no wait could admit — the same refusals consume makes, since both derive one window.

classes.surfaceHtml: consume(tainted string $key, uint $limit, Duration $per, {burst?, cost?}): RateLimit\Decision over the shared store, and shed(…) per core and approximate. Decision is readonly allowed: bool, limit: uint, remaining: uint, retryAfter: ?Duration. Both neutral; a secret key is refused; an unreachable store throws

classes.name: Core\RateLimit\Decision
classes.summary: The result of one `Core\RateLimit::consume` or `shed` call. `allowed` says whether the call was inside the limit. `limit`, `remaining` and `retryAfter` give the numbers for `RateLimit` and `Retry-After` response headers.

doc.shortHtml: Whether this arrival was inside the limit, and so whether its cost was charged.
doc.returnHtml: true when the units were charged, false when nothing was charged and the arrival was refused.

doc.shortHtml: The $limit the decision was made against, carried back so a RateLimit header can be written from the decision alone.
doc.returnHtml: The limit as it was passed.

doc.shortHtml: How many further units the store would admit at this instant.
doc.returnHtml: The units left in the burst allowance, counted after this arrival was charged; 0 when the next unit would have to wait.

doc.shortHtml: How long until this arrival would be admitted — the exact wait, computed from the store's own clock rather than estimated.
doc.returnHtml: null exactly when the decision is allowed, and otherwise the Core\Time\Duration until the theoretical arrival time; a Retry-After header built from it tells the client when to come back rather than when the window turns over, which is what stops every refused client retrying in the same instant.

classes.summaryHtml: The result of one Core\RateLimit::consume or shed call. allowed says whether the call was inside the limit. limit, remaining and retryAfter give the numbers for RateLimit and Retry-After response headers.

classes.name: Core\Reflect
classes.surface: `forClass`, `forObject`, `typeOf(mixed): TypeKind`, and the visibility-respecting walk. Replaces `ReflectionClass` **and** `get_class`, `get_object_vars`, `get_class_methods`, `method_exists`, `property_exists`, `class_exists`, `is_a`, `is_subclass_of`, `class_implements`, `spl_object_id`

doc.shortHtml: Describes the class $name names, reaching it by name rather than through a value. Replaces ReflectionClass's constructor and class_exists.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The class's name as its declaration writes it, namespace included and with no leading separator — what Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::name answers.

doc.returnHtml: A description of that class, or null where the running program declares no class of that name — the null is class_exists's answer, which is why asking is not a failure.

doc.shortHtml: Describes $object's class — its name, and the properties code outside the class can see. Replaces get_class and get_object_vars.

params.name: object
params.descHtml: The value to describe. Reflection is for the receiver whose class is not known while compiling, so the parameter is mixed.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Reflect\ClassInfo for the object's own class, carrying answers rather than a way back to the object.

errors.descHtml: $object is not an object — a mixed carries no promise that it is one, so the check is made here rather than by the caller.

doc.shortHtml: Which of the language's representations $value currently holds. The single replacement for PHP's fourteen is_* predicates and gettype, which are only meaningful on a mixed at all.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to ask about. On anything but a mixed the checker already knows the answer, so the interesting receiver is the one whose type was erased.

doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\TypeKind case — exactly one, since the cases partition the representations rather than overlapping the way is_scalar and is_int do.

classes.surfaceHtml: forClass, forObject, typeOf(mixed): TypeKind, and the visibility-respecting walk. Replaces ReflectionClass and get_class, get_object_vars, get_class_methods, method_exists, property_exists, class_exists, is_a, is_subclass_of, class_implements, spl_object_id

classes.name: Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo
classes.summary: One `#[...]` attribute written on a class or on one of its members, as `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::attributes` returns it. `target` and `parameter` say where it is written. `fields` lists its payload's field names, and `field` returns one value.

doc.shortHtml: The type alias the named form gave the attribute, as it is written.
doc.returnHtml: The written name, or the empty string for the bare #[{...}] form. The name is not resolved. It is used to check the payload object where it is written, and a caller never uses it to find an attribute.

doc.shortHtml: The member the attribute is written on.
doc.returnHtml: A property's name with no $ sigil, or a method's name — or the empty string for the class or interface declaration itself. A parameter's site names its method here and the parameter in parameter.

doc.shortHtml: The parameter of target the attribute is written on.
doc.returnHtml: The parameter's name with no $ sigil, or the empty string for every attach site that is not a parameter's. The pair is what tells #[X] public function f(...) from public function f(#[X] int $n), which name one declaration each and not the same one.

doc.shortHtml: The payload's field names, in the order the attribute writes them.
doc.returnHtml: One string per field, including a field whose value Novis does not fold here — the name is as much a fact about the attach site as the value is, and field is what reports the difference.

doc.shortHtml: One payload field's value, folded at compile time.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The field's own name, as fields answers it.

doc.returnHtml: The value as a string, int, bool or float. These are the four types a payload field can have here.

errors.descHtml: The attribute's payload has no field of that name, so the ask is a mistake rather than an absence to report — fields is the list that cannot be wrong. Or the field's value is one Novis does not fold into a description: a class constant, an enum case or Foo::class, each of which resolves through the namespace the attribute was written in, plus the values that Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo also cannot read. Core\Attributes::get reads all of those, at compile time and by shape.

classes.summaryHtml: One #[...] attribute written on a class or on one of its members, as Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::attributes returns it. target and parameter say where it is written. fields lists its payload's field names, and field returns one value.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\ClassInfo
classes.summary: One class, as `Core\Reflect::forClass` and `Core\Reflect::forObject` return it. `properties`, `methods`, `constants` and `attributes` list what the class declares. `get`, `set`, `call` and `construct` use a class whose name is only known at run time.

doc.shortHtml: The described class's name, namespace included, spelled as the declaration writes it.
doc.returnHtml: The class name — App\Model\User for a namespaced declaration, and never an alias the naming site happened to use.

doc.shortHtml: The described class's properties — its own and every inherited one — each with its name, its visibility and the type its declaration spells. Replaces ReflectionClass::getProperties.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo per declared property, in slot order: every ancestor's first, then the class's own. A private or protected property is among them, carrying the bit that says so — naming a member is introspection of the program's shape, and reading one is get's question, checked there.

doc.shortHtml: The property names a read written at this call site may make, in slot order. Replaces get_object_vars, whose answer is scope-sensitive in the same way.
doc.returnHtml: One name per property this site may read, $-sigil excluded: every declared property where the call is written inside the described class, and the public ones anywhere else. The complete list is properties, and the difference between the two answers is exactly what get would refuse here.

doc.shortHtml: Whether the described class declares a property called $name. Replaces property_exists.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The property's name, $-sigil excluded, as the declaration writes it.

doc.returnHtml: true for a private or protected property as well as a public one, which is what tells a refused read from a misspelled name. Whether this site may read it is properties' own bit.

doc.shortHtml: The described class's methods — its own and every inherited one — each with its name, its visibility and how many parameters it declares. Replaces get_class_methods.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\MethodInfo per declared method, in name order, and a method the calling site could not call is among them carrying isPublic() === false. Naming a method is not calling it, which is why the roster is complete and Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::call is where the check is made.

doc.shortHtml: The described class's constants — its own and every inherited one — each with its name and its visibility. Replaces ReflectionClass::getReflectionConstants.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo per constant the class answers, its own declarations first. A constant a subclass redeclares appears once, with the declaration that wins. The values are not here: naming a constant is metadata, reading one is acting, and constant is where that check is made.

doc.shortHtml: The value of the class constant $name, under exactly the visibility ordinary code at this call site would face. Replaces ReflectionClassConstant::getValue, and there is no setAccessible to lift the check with.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The constant's name, as the declaration writes it — no class qualifier and no ::.

doc.returnHtml: The folded value: a string, int, bool or float, whichever the declaration's right-hand side is.

errors.descHtml: $name names a constant this call site may not reach — a reflective read has the visibility ordinary code has; or one whose declared type carries secret, which is refused at every site, because the mixed this answers with carries no qualifier and the value would reach the next sink unmarked.

The class declares and inherits no constant of that name. Or the constant's value is not a string, int, bool or float written directly in the code: hasValue checks this before the call. Both are mistakes in the program, not permission problems, and that is how they differ from the errors above.

doc.shortHtml: Reports whether the described class declares or inherits a method named $name. Replaces method_exists.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The method's name, as the declaration writes it and as methods spells it.

doc.returnHtml: true for a method the class answers for at any visibility, false for a name it declares none of — so a refusal to call tells a private method from a misspelling.

doc.shortHtml: Every #[...] written on the class's own declaration or on one of its own members.
doc.returnHtml: One row per attach site, in source order — the declaration's own first, then each member's, and a method's parameters' after that method's. Own-only, where constants is flattened over the ancestors: an attribute is a fact about the declaration it is written on, so a base class's site is never reported as this class's. Asking for a payload by its shape is Core\Attributes::get, which is checked where it is written and costs nothing at run time; this is the reflective question, for a class the caller does not name in source.

doc.shortHtml: Reads $object's $name property, under exactly the visibility ordinary code at this call site would face. Replaces ReflectionProperty::getValue, and there is no setAccessible to lift the check with.

params.name: object
params.descHtml: An instance of the described class — the description is of a class, so the value to read is named here rather than held.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The property's name, $-sigil excluded, as properties spells it.

doc.returnHtml: The property's value, with its own declared type erased to mixed.

errors.descHtml: $object is not an object, or $name names a property that is not public — a reflective read has the visibility ordinary code has, so the refusal is the one an ordinary out-of-class read would meet.

$object is not an instance of the described class, or $name names no property of it at all. Both are mistakes in the program rather than facts about the value, which is what separates them from the refusal above.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $object's $name property, under exactly the visibility ordinary code at this call site would face, and then runs the PropertyObserver an ordinary write runs. Replaces ReflectionProperty::setValue, again with no setAccessible.

params.name: object
params.descHtml: An instance of the described class — get's own argument, for get's reason.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The property's name, $-sigil excluded, as properties spells it.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: What to store. It is checked against what the concrete class declares the property to hold, since the declared type is not knowable here.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. What was stored is what a following get answers, and what the observer was told about.

errors.descHtml: $object is not an object, $name names a property that is not public, or $value is not of the type that property declares — the first two being the refusals an ordinary out-of-class write would meet, and the third the one a write through an erased view meets.
$object is not an instance of the described class, or $name names no property of it at all — get's pair, told apart from the refusals above for get's reason.

Whatever the class's own onPropertySet observer throws. It is told of the write once the value is stored, and a throw out of it still fails the write — a reflective write is not the place that changes.

doc.shortHtml: Calls $object's $name method with $arguments, under exactly the visibility ordinary code at this call site would face. Replaces ReflectionMethod::invoke, and there is no setAccessible to lift the check with.

params.name: object
params.descHtml: An instance of the described class — the description is of a class, so the value to call on is named here rather than held.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The method's name, () excluded, as the declaration writes it.

params.name: arguments
params.descHtml: One entry per declared parameter, in order, keys ignored. Entries after the last parameter are ignored. Required even where the method takes none, which is then [].

doc.returnHtml: Whatever the method returned, with its own declared type erased to mixed.

errors.descHtml: $name is not public, names no method of the class, or names a Core member; or $arguments has fewer entries than the method declares, or an entry whose type the parameter does not accept. Every one of these is the refusal an ordinary call through an erased receiver meets, raised by that same check rather than by a second one written here.
$object is not an object at all. A $object that is an object but not an instance of the described class is the LogicError above.

doc.shortHtml: Builds an instance of the described class, running its constructor with $arguments under exactly the visibility a new written at this call site would face. Replaces ReflectionClass::newInstanceArgs, and there is no setAccessible to lift the check with.

params.name: arguments
params.descHtml: One entry per declared constructor parameter, in order, keys ignored. Entries after the last parameter are ignored. Required even where the class declares no constructor, which is then [].

doc.returnHtml: The new instance, with its own class erased to mixed. A class declaring no constructor answers with the allocation its declared defaults armed.

errors.descHtml: The constructor is not public and this call site is outside the class; or $arguments has fewer entries than it declares, or an entry whose type a parameter does not accept; or the described class is not one this program declares. Each is the refusal the ordinary door meets, raised by that same check.

classes.summaryHtml: One class, as Core\Reflect::forClass and Core\Reflect::forObject return it. properties, methods, constants and attributes list what the class declares. get, set, call and construct use a class whose name is only known at run time.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo
classes.summary: One class constant, as `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constants` returns it. `name` and `isPublic` describe the declaration. `hasValue` says whether `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constant` can return its value.

doc.shortHtml: The constant's name, as the declaring class writes it.
doc.returnHtml: The name with no class qualifier and no :: — what Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constant takes.

doc.shortHtml: Whether code outside the declaring class may name the constant.
doc.returnHtml: false for a private or protected constant, which is still listed, on Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo::isPublic's terms exactly: knowing that a constant exists and may not be read from here is what tells a refusal from a misspelling.

doc.shortHtml: Whether the constant's declared value is one Novis folds at compile time, and so one Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constant can hand back.
doc.returnHtml: true for a string, int, bool or float written directly in the code. false for an array or object constant, and for an integer too large for int. Novis reads a constant only when its value is written directly in the code, and it does not evaluate other expressions. So this is false for exactly the constants that are also not allowed in type position.

classes.summaryHtml: One class constant, as Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constants returns it. name and isPublic describe the declaration. hasValue says whether Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constant can return its value.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\EnumInfo
classes.summary: One enum, as `Core\Reflect\EnumInfo::of` returns it for the enum's name. `cases` lists the names of its cases, `valueOf` returns the value of one case, and `isUnsigned` says whether the values are `uint` or `int`.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a description of the enum with the name $name. An enum has no methods of its own, so this is the way to read the list of its cases.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The full name of the enum, with its namespace and with no \ at the start. Status::class gives this name.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Reflect\EnumInfo for that enum. The result is null if the program has no enum with that name, and also for the name of a class.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the full name of the enum.
doc.returnHtml: The name that was passed to of, with its namespace. You can pass it to of again to get a description of the same enum.

doc.shortHtml: Every case the enum declares, by name.
doc.returnHtml: One string per case, sorted by the value of the case from the smallest to the largest. Two cases with the same value are sorted by name. The order is not the order of the declaration. An enum with no case gives an empty list.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of one case of the enum.

params.name: case
params.descHtml: The name of the case, as cases gives it. The name is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: The value of the case. It is a uint if isUnsigned returns true, and an int otherwise. Use as uint or as int to store it in a variable of that type.

errors.descHtml: The enum has no case with that name. Use cases to get the names that exist.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether the values of the enum's cases are uint or int.
doc.returnHtml: true for an enum declared with : uint. false for an enum declared with : int or with no type, because an enum with no type is an int enum.

classes.summaryHtml: One enum, as Core\Reflect\EnumInfo::of returns it for the enum's name. cases lists the names of its cases, valueOf returns the value of one case, and isUnsigned says whether the values are uint or int.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\MethodInfo
classes.summary: One method of a class, as `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::methods` returns it. `name` and `isPublic` describe the declaration. `parameterCount` and `parameters` describe what the method takes.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the name of the method.
doc.returnHtml: The name as the class declares it, with no class name and no parentheses. A constructor is named constructor. You can pass the name to Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::hasMethod and Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::call.

doc.shortHtml: Tells you whether code outside the class may call the method.
doc.returnHtml: true for a public method, and false for a protected or private method. Those methods are still in the list that Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::methods returns. If isPublic returns false, Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::call from outside the class throws a LogicError.

doc.shortHtml: Returns how many parameters the method declares.
doc.returnHtml: The number of parameters, as a uint. $this is not counted. The number is also correct for a method the compiler adds, where parameters returns an empty array.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the parameters of the method, in the order they are written. It replaces PHP's ReflectionMethod::getParameters.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\ParameterInfo for each parameter. $this is not included. For a method the compiler adds, such as the constructor of LogicError, the array is empty. parameterCount still returns how many arguments that method takes.

classes.summaryHtml: One method of a class, as Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::methods returns it. name and isPublic describe the declaration. parameterCount and parameters describe what the method takes.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\ParameterInfo
classes.summary: One parameter of a method, as `Core\Reflect\MethodInfo::parameters` returns it. `name` returns the name of the parameter, and `type` returns its declared type.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the name of the parameter.
doc.returnHtml: The name as the method declares it, without the $. This is the name you write for a named argument. A promoted constructor parameter has the same name as its property.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the declared type of the parameter, written the way the method writes it.
doc.returnHtml: The type as text, such as int, ?int, array<string> or App\User. A parameter declared in a source file always has a type, so the result is text. The result is null only if no type is known for the parameter. To check the type of a value, use Core\Reflect::typeOf.

classes.summaryHtml: One parameter of a method, as Core\Reflect\MethodInfo::parameters returns it. name returns the name of the parameter, and type returns its declared type.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo
classes.summary: One property of a class, as `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::properties` returns it. `name` and `isPublic` describe the declaration. `type` returns the type the property is declared with.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the name of the property.
doc.returnHtml: The name as the class declares it, with no $ and no class name. You can pass the name to Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::hasProperty, Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::get and Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::set.

doc.shortHtml: Tells you whether code outside the class may read and write the property.
doc.returnHtml: true for a public property, and false for a protected or private property. Those properties are still in the list that Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::properties returns. If isPublic returns false, Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::get from outside the class throws a RuntimeError.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the type the property is declared with, written the way the class writes it.
doc.returnHtml: The type as a string, such as int, ?int, array<string> or Customer. The properties of a built-in error class, such as message on LogicError, have no written type, so the result is null. To find the type of a value, use Core\Reflect::typeOf.

classes.summaryHtml: One property of a class, as Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::properties returns it. name and isPublic describe the declaration. type returns the type the property is declared with.

classes.name: Core\Regex
classes.summary:
Semantics — the two-tier engine, the step budget, why the *pattern* is a sink while the subject is not —
are `rule:core-classes/regex-two-tiers`. `preg_match`'s `$matches` out-parameter is a returned
`?Match` (R3), and there are no `PREG_*` flag constants (R11).

doc.shortHtml: Compiles a regular expression once, with options, and returns a Core\Regex\Pattern. You can pass the Pattern to every Core\Regex method that takes a pattern.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: The regular expression, with no delimiters. A tainted string does not compile here. Use Core\Regex::quote to match a user's text literally.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: true makes letters match in upper and lower case. PHP writes this as i. The default is false.

params.name: multiline
params.descHtml: true makes ^ and $ match at the start and end of every line. PHP writes this as m. The default is false.

params.name: dotAll
params.descHtml: true makes . match a newline too. PHP writes this as s. The default is false.

params.name: ungreedy
params.descHtml: true makes and + match as little as possible, and ? as much as possible. PHP writes this as U. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The compiled Core\Regex\Pattern. The pattern is checked here, so a mistake in it throws at this line and not at its first use.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression. The message contains the pattern.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $pattern matches anywhere in $subject. The match can be at any position. Write ^ and $ in the pattern to match the whole text.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to search.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

doc.returnHtml: true if the text contains at least one match, and false if it does not.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, or matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows.

doc.shortHtml: Finds the first match of $pattern in $subject and returns it as a Core\Regex\Match. The Match has the matched text, each group and the position of the match.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to search.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

params.name: from
params.descHtml: The character position where the search starts. The default is 0. A negative position counts from the end of $subject.

doc.returnHtml: The first Core\Regex\Match at or after from, or null if there is no match.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, or matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows.

doc.shortHtml: Finds every match of $pattern in $subject and returns them as an array of Core\Regex\Match. The matches do not overlap, and they are in the order they appear in the text.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to search.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

doc.returnHtml: One Core\Regex\Match for each match, from left to right. The array is empty if there is no match.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, or matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces every match of $pattern in $subject with $replacement, and returns the new text. In $replacement, $1 is the text of group 1 and $0 is the whole match.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to search.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

params.name: replacement
params.descHtml: The text that replaces each match. $1 to $99 insert a numbered group, and ${name} inserts a named group. Write ${1}0 when a digit follows the group. $$ is one $. A group the pattern does not have inserts nothing. PHP's \1 is not a group here.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: How many matches to replace, counted from the start of the text. The default is every match. 0 replaces nothing.

doc.returnHtml: The text with the matches replaced. It is the same text if there is no match.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, or matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows.

members.name: replaceWith
members.signature: replaceWith(string $subject, Pattern|string $pattern, callable(Match): string $fn, {limit?: uint}): string

doc.shortHtml: Replaces every match of $pattern in $subject with the text your function returns for that match, and returns the new text. The function gets one Core\Regex\Match.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to search.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: A function that gets one Core\Regex\Match and returns a string. It is called once for each match, from left to right. The text it returns is inserted as it is, so $1 in it is two characters.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: How many matches to replace, counted from the start of the text. The default is every match. 0 replaces nothing. The function is not called for a match after the limit.

doc.returnHtml: The text with the matches replaced. It is the same text if there is no match.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows, or the new text is larger than the memory limit.

members.name: split
members.signature: split(string $subject, Pattern|string $pattern, {limit?: int, keepEmpty?: bool}): array<string>

doc.shortHtml: Splits $subject at every match of $pattern, and returns the pieces as an array. The matches are not part of any piece.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to split.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: The largest number of pieces. The last piece contains the rest of the text. A negative number removes that many pieces from the end. 0 returns the whole text as one piece. The default is no limit. PHP's preg_split reads 0 and -1 as no limit.

params.name: keepEmpty
params.descHtml: Whether empty pieces are kept. The default is true. With false, empty pieces are removed after limit is applied.

doc.returnHtml: The pieces, from left to right. If there is no match, the array has one piece: the whole text.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, or matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows.

doc.shortHtml: Puts a \ before every character that has a special meaning in a pattern. The result is a pattern that matches $text exactly. A tainted text is allowed here, and the result can be used as a pattern.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The text to match exactly.

doc.returnHtml: The escaped pattern. A text with no special characters is returned unchanged. The escaped characters are not the same as PHP's preg_quote: & and ~ are escaped here, and !, :, <, =, > and / are not.

classes.summaryHtml: Semantics — the two-tier engine, the step budget, why the pattern is a sink while the subject is not — are rule:core-classes/regex-two-tiers. preg_match's $matches out-parameter is a returned ?Match (R3), and there are no PREG_* flag constants (R11).

members.name: group
members.notes: one group's text; `null` where the pattern declares it and this match did not reach it, and a **throw** for a group the pattern does not declare
members.notesHtml: one group's text; null where the pattern declares it and this match did not reach it, and a throw for a group the pattern does not declare

doc.shortHtml: Returns the text of one group, by its number or by its name. PHP reads this as $matches[$group] after preg_match.

params.name: group
params.descHtml: The number of the group, or its name. Group 0 is the whole match.

doc.returnHtml: The text of the group. The result is null if the pattern has the group but this match did not use it.

errors.descHtml: The pattern has no group with this number or name.

members.name: groups
members.notes: every group at once, in `preg_match`'s own order: a named group under its name, then under its number
members.notesHtml: every group at once, in preg_match's own order: a named group under its name, then under its number

doc.shortHtml: Returns the text of every group in one array. A named group is in the array twice: under its name and under its number.
doc.returnHtml: An array with group 0 first. A group that this match did not use is in the array, and its value is null.

members.name: offset
members.notes: where the whole match starts, in `rule:types/string-is-utf8`'s unit — not `PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE`'s bytes
members.notesHtml: where the whole match starts, in rule:types/string-is-utf8's unit — not PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE's bytes

doc.shortHtml: Returns the position in the text where the whole match starts. The position counts characters, not bytes.
doc.returnHtml: The position of the first character of the match. A match at the start of the text is at 0.

members.name: text
members.notes: the whole match, which is group `0`
members.notesHtml: the whole match, which is group 0

doc.shortHtml: Returns the whole text that the pattern matched. This is the same text as group(0).
doc.returnHtml: The matched text. It is never null, but it can be an empty string.

classes.name: Core\Request
classes.surface: `method`, `path`, `query`, `queryAs`, `post`, `postAs`, `body`, `bytes`, `json`, `jsonAs`, `bodyStream`, `header`, `headers`, `cookie`, `files`, `clientIp`, `scheme`, `host`, `mount`, `route`, `isHead` — replacing `$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_FILES`, `$_COOKIE`, `$_REQUEST`, `filter_input`. `path` is the request path with the matched mount's prefix **removed** and `mount(): Request\Mount` answers what was removed — a `prefix(): string` and that mount's glob `captures(): array<tainted string>` — which is how a host-mounted deployment learns which tenant it serves, and never `null`, because a request that reached a program reached it through some mount; `route(): ?Router\Match` is the match the server made once before the handler, and is what the CSRF check and the `route` metric label read ([0102](../decisions/0102.md)); `method` reports `Get` for a `HEAD` request so a `Get`-only route table still matches, with `isHead` carrying the truth; `clientIp` and `scheme` are resolved from the socket peer unless a peer in `[server] trusted_proxies` asserted otherwise; `files(): Iterable<Part>` is the **only** way to receive an uploaded file and yields parts lazily, each answering `name()`, a `filename()` that is never a path and a `contentType()` — all three `tainted` — and consumed by `readAll({max?}): tainted bytes`, by iterating `content(): Iterable<bytes>`, or by `saveTo(string $path, {max?, overwrite?})` — there is no temp path, no `move_uploaded_file` and no `size` (`rule:http-server/an-upload-is-received-only-through-files`); a multipart form's non-file parts are buffered into `post()` as usual; `post(string $name): mixed` reads one submitted field by name under `query`'s bracket convention, over those buffered parts or over a urlencoded body, and reads to the **end** of the body, which is what makes it answer every field rather than the ones that arrived before the part a `files` walk stopped on, so a handler wanting the uploads too takes `files()` first; and `bodyStream(): Iterable<tainted bytes>` is the raw-body alternative to `body`, carrying the qualifier `body` puts on the same octets. `json({maxDepth?: uint}): mixed` is `Core\Json::decode` over those same octets, carrying that member's bag and its default of 512; it consults no `Content-Type`, on `post`'s reasoning, and a body that is absent or empty is a `ParseError` like a malformed one, because `mixed` cannot tell "no body" from the document `null`. `jsonAs<T>({maxDepth?: uint}): T` is `Core\Json::decodeAs` over those same octets, refusing the same bodies for the same reasons; it keeps nothing of what it built, so every call hydrates a fresh `T` and two callers are never handed one object. `bytes(): tainted bytes` is `body`'s reading for a payload that is not text — named after `Core\Response::bytes`, buffering over the same hold, and answering the octets a `string` cannot hold. A body that is not UTF-8 is a `ParseError` from `body`, naming this member, rather than a repaired string: a lossy decode would silently change a webhook's signed payload (`rule:types/string-is-utf8`). `queryAs<T>({name?: string}): T` and `postAs<T>({name?: string}): T` are `Core\Arr::shapeAs` over what `query` and `post` parse: with no `name` the whole parameter set is the subject — the only way a program reaches it, since neither `$_GET` nor `$_POST` has a public array spelling here — and with one it is the subtree that name reaches under the bracket convention. Each field converts with `as`, so a form's text fits a declared `int`, and a key `T` does not name is left behind. `body`, `bytes`, `post`, `postAs`, `json` and `jsonAs` are **buffering** readers, which keep what they read and so may follow one another; `bodyStream` and `files` are **streaming** readers, each of which consumes the body and may only be the first reader of it, which is why a `post()` reading the fields a walk buffered is ordinary rather than an exception (`rule:http-server/a-mount-table-expands-at-boot`, `rule:http-server/trusted-proxies-is-empty-and-empty-reads-nothing`, `rule:http-server/head-runs-as-get`, `rule:http-server/buffering-readers-share-the-body-and-streaming-readers-consume-it` and `rule:http-server/the-body-is-read-on-demand-under-two-caps`).

doc.shortHtml: Returns the method of the request, such as GET or POST, as a case of Core\Http\Method. A HEAD request returns Get. Use isHead to tell the two apart.
doc.returnHtml: The Core\Http\Method case of the request. It is never Head.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request, such as a command-line program or a test. It is also thrown when the method is not one of the cases of Core\Http\Method. The server answers such a request with 501 before your program runs.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether the request is a HEAD request. method returns Get for a HEAD request, so this is the only way to tell the two apart.
doc.returnHtml: true when the request method is HEAD, and false for every other method. The server sends no body in the response to a HEAD request, so a program can skip the work of building one.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request.

doc.shortHtml: The request path with the matched mount's prefix removed, so an application reads the same paths wherever it is mounted.
doc.returnHtml: The remainder of the path after the mount prefix, percent-encoded as it arrived and tainted. What was removed is mount()'s to report.

errors.descHtml: This program is not answering a request.

doc.shortHtml: One query-string parameter by name, read with PHP's bracket convention — the same parse Core\Uri::parseQuery performs, so a[b]=c is reached as a nested array under a.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The parameter's name, decoded — the key as a form writes it, without brackets for a nested value.

doc.returnHtml: The parameter's value as a string, a nested array<mixed> for a bracketed key, or null where the query carried no such name. Check it out with as, which throws on input the type does not fit rather than quietly yielding zero.

errors.descHtml: This program is not answering a request, or the query string holds percent escapes that decode to octets that are not UTF-8.

doc.shortHtml: The query string read as the type T written at the call site — Core\Arr::shapeAs over what query parses, converting each named field with as; with no name the whole parameter set is the subject, and with one it is the subtree that name reaches.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The parameter whose nested value is read, under query's bracket convention and without brackets. Omitted, the whole query string is read instead.

doc.returnHtml: A new T whose every field is the declared type, or — for an array<T> — one per entry. Nothing of it is kept: every call parses the query string again, so two callers are never handed the same object.

errors.descHtml: This program is not answering a request, the query string holds percent escapes that decode to octets that are not UTF-8, or T is a class carrying no #[Json\Derive] codec to read it against.

A field T requires is absent, or holds a value as refuses for its declared type, or the named subtree is not a set of fields at all. Every field that failed is one issue on the error, at its own dotted path, so a form shows the whole list rather than the first item of it.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of one request header by its name. It replaces the HTTP_ entries of PHP's $_SERVER.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The name of the header. Upper and lower case do not matter, so Content-Type and content-type are the same header.

doc.returnHtml: The value as a tainted string, exactly as it arrived. The result is null when the request has no header of that name. When the header arrived on more than one line, the values are joined with , in the order they arrived. headers() returns each line on its own.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every header of the request, grouped by name. It replaces PHP's getallheaders.
doc.returnHtml: An array<array<tainted string>>. Each key is a header name in lower case. Its value is a list with one entry for each line of that header, in the order the lines arrived. The array is empty when the request has no headers.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of one cookie by its name. It replaces PHP's $_COOKIE.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The name of the cookie, exactly as it was set. Upper and lower case are different, and a.b and a_b are two different cookies.

doc.returnHtml: The value as a tainted string, exactly as it arrived. Nothing is decoded. The result is null when the request has no cookie of that name. When the name starts with __Host- and the cookie arrived twice, the result is null too.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the whole request body as one string. It replaces PHP's file_get_contents('php://input').
doc.returnHtml: Every byte the client sent, in order and unchanged. The string is tainted. It is empty when the request has no body, and every call returns the same string.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request. Or bodyStream or files already read the body, and those two do not keep it.
The body is larger than [limits] request_body (8M). The bytes past that limit are never stored.
The connection failed while the body arrived, or the client sent fewer bytes than its Content-Length said.
The body is not valid UTF-8, so it cannot be a string. bytes returns the same body as bytes.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the whole request body as bytes. Use it for a body that is not text, such as an uploaded file.
doc.returnHtml: Every byte the client sent, in order and unchanged. The value is tainted. It is empty when the request has no body. A body that is not valid UTF-8 is returned too, where body throws an error.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request. Or bodyStream or files already read the body, and those two do not keep it.
The body is larger than [limits] request_body (8M). The bytes past that limit are never stored.
The connection failed while the body arrived, or the client sent fewer bytes than its Content-Length said.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the request body as one JSON document and returns the decoded value. It replaces PHP's json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input'), true).

params.name: maxDepth
params.descHtml: How deep the document may nest. The default is 512, and the value must be from 1 to 1024. A document with no array or object in it has depth 1.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded value, the same as Core\Json::decode returns for the body. A JSON object becomes an array with string keys. Every string in it is tainted. Every call returns the same value.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request. Or bodyStream or files already read the body, and those two do not keep it. Or maxDepth is not from 1 to 1024.
The body is not one whole JSON document, or it nests deeper than maxDepth. An empty body throws this error too. The Content-Type header is not checked.
The body is larger than [limits] request_body (8M). The bytes past that limit are never stored.
The connection failed while the body arrived, or the client sent fewer bytes than its Content-Length said.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the request body as one JSON object and returns a new instance of the class T. The class needs #[Core\Json\Derive]. Write array<T> to read a JSON array with one object for each element.

params.name: maxDepth
params.descHtml: How deep the document may nest. The default is 512, and the value must be from 1 to 1024. A document with no array or object in it has depth 1.

doc.returnHtml: A new T with its fields read from the body, or one T for each element for an array<T>. Every call creates new objects, so two callers never get the same object.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request. Or bodyStream or files already read the body, and those two do not keep it. Or T has no #[Core\Json\Derive] attribute. Or maxDepth is not from 1 to 1024.

The body is not one whole JSON object, or it nests deeper than maxDepth. An empty body throws this error too. It is also thrown when a field is missing or has the wrong type. The issues list has one entry for each wrong field. The Content-Type header is not checked.
The call stack is full before the last object is created. This can happen when a class contains itself and the body nests very deeply.
The body is larger than [limits] request_body (8M). The bytes past that limit are never stored.
The connection failed while the body arrived, or the client sent fewer bytes than its Content-Length said.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the request body in pieces, in the order they arrive. Use it for a large body that you do not want in memory all at once.
doc.returnHtml: A value that a foreach loop reads once. Each piece is a tainted bytes value. How the body is split has no meaning. The loop runs zero times when the request has no body.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request. Or body, bytes, json, files or bodyStream already read the body. After this call, those methods throw this error too.
The connection failed while the loop read the body. The pieces before the failure are still given to the loop.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the files that a form uploaded, one at a time in a foreach loop. It replaces PHP's $_FILES and move_uploaded_file.
doc.returnHtml: An Iterable<Core\Request\Part>. Each loop step gives the next file as it arrives. The text fields are not in the loop, and post reads them after it. The loop runs zero times when the request has no multipart/form-data body.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request. Or body, bodyStream or post already read the body. After this call, body, bytes, bodyStream and json throw this error too. post still works after the loop.
The request says it has a multipart/form-data body, but its boundary is missing, given twice or not valid. Or the body does not have the form that the request declared.
The connection failed while the loop read the body, or the body ended before its last boundary.

doc.shortHtml: One submitted form field by name, read with PHP's bracket convention — the same parse query performs, over a multipart/form-data body's non-file parts or over a urlencoded one, replacing $_POST and filter_input(INPUT_POST, …).

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The field's name, as the form declared it and without brackets for a nested value.

doc.returnHtml: The field's value as a string, a nested array<mixed> for a bracketed key, or null where the form carried no such name. Reading the body to its end is what this member does, so on a multipart/form-data request it is called after the files() walk, never before: the uploads are drained on the way to the last field.

errors.descHtml: This program is not answering a request, or this request's body has already been read by body or bodyStream — those two hand the bytes over uninterpreted and leave no fields behind. A body files is walking is the one case this member joins rather than refuses.

The request declared a multipart/form-data body and then did not say how to read one, or what arrived is not the body it declared, or a urlencoded field holds percent escapes that decode to octets that are not UTF-8.
The connection failed under the body, or the peer stopped short of the length it declared.

doc.shortHtml: The submitted form read as the type T written at the call site — Core\Arr::shapeAs over what post parses, converting each named field with as; with no name the whole form is the subject, and with one it is the subtree that name reaches.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The field whose nested value is read, under post's bracket convention and without brackets. Omitted, the whole form is read instead.

doc.returnHtml: A new T whose every field is the declared type, or — for an array<T> — one per entry. Reading the body to its end is what this member does, exactly as post does, so on a multipart/form-data request it is called after the files() walk. Nothing of it is kept: every call reads the form again, so two callers are never handed the same object.

errors.descHtml: This program is not answering a request, or this request's body has already been read by body or bodyStream, or T is a class carrying no #[Json\Derive] codec to read the form against.

The body is not the form it declared — post's three refusals, unchanged — or a field T requires is absent, or holds a value as refuses for its declared type, or the named subtree is not a set of fields at all. Every field that failed is one issue on the error, at its own dotted path.
The connection failed under the body, or the peer stopped short of the length it declared.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the network address of the client that sent this request. Behind a proxy that is listed in [server] trusted_proxies, the address comes from X-Forwarded-For.
doc.returnHtml: The address as a tainted string, such as 203.0.113.7 or 2001:db8::1. An IPv6 address is always in its short form. The result is null when the request has no address, for example over a Unix socket.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request. For example, it is a command-line program, a job or a test.

doc.shortHtml: The scheme this request effectively arrived over, which only a trusted peer's X-Forwarded-Proto can make https for a connection that was not itself TLS.
doc.returnHtml: "http" or "https", tainted. Never null: every request arrived over one, and a deployment that trusts no proxy always reads the scheme of the connection itself.

errors.descHtml: This program is not answering a request — a CLI program, a scheduled script, a job worker or a test.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the host name the request was sent to, read from its Host header. It replaces PHP's $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'].
doc.returnHtml: The host name as a tainted string in lower case. A port and one dot at the end are removed, so Shop.Example.com.:8443 returns shop.example.com. An IPv6 address keeps its brackets. The result is null when the request has no Host header. header("host") returns the header exactly as it arrived, with the port. Headers such as X-Forwarded-Host are never read.

errors.descHtml: The program is not answering a request.

doc.shortHtml: The route this request matched, which the server took once at the door before any of this program ran — the same match the CSRF check and the route metric label read, so a handler never matches its own path a second time.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Router\Match answering the declared name and the path's captures, or null where nothing in the table claimed this method and path — which is a served request like any other, since matching dispatches nothing. A program declaring no #[Route] builds no table and reads null here for the same reason.

errors.descHtml: This program is not answering a request, as a CLI program, a scheduled script, a job worker and a test are not — refused rather than answered null, because "no request arrived" and "nothing matched" are different facts.
A capture percent-decodes to octets that are not UTF-8, so it has no tainted string to bind to; the throw names the capture and the offset of the first byte a string cannot hold.

doc.shortHtml: Which mount is serving this request: the prefix the server took off the path before path() answered it, and the glob captures of the mount row that took it — the pair a host-mounted deployment learns which tenant it is running for from.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Request\Mount, always — a request that reached this program reached it through some mount, and one that came in by a door with no prefix and no glob answers "" and an empty array rather than null.

errors.descHtml: This program is not answering a request — a CLI program, a scheduled script, a job worker and a test are not, and none of them was mounted anywhere.
