classes.name: Core\Storage
classes.summary: Saves files by name in a folder that `nvs.toml` sets up as a disk. `put` writes a file, `get` reads it back, `delete` removes it and `list` returns the names on the disk. A name is one plain word such as `invoice-1042.pdf`, never a path.

doc.shortHtml: Saves $contents as the file $key on $disk. A file that is already there is replaced, unless overwrite is false.

params.name: disk
params.descHtml: The name of a [storage.<name>] block in nvs.toml. That block sets the folder the files are saved in. A tainted value is not allowed here, because the program chooses the disk and user input never does.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name of the file on the disk. It is 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, ., - and _, and it does not start with a .. A / or a \ throws an error, so a key never points into another folder.

params.name: contents
params.descHtml: The bytes to save. The whole value is written.

params.name: overwrite
params.descHtml: Whether a file that already has this key may be replaced. The default is true. With false, put throws an IOError if the key is already used.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The file is on the disk when put returns.

errors.descHtml: No [storage.<name>] block with this name sets a root. Or $key is not a valid key. Or the fs.read or fs.write capability does not include the file's path.
The file could not be written. This includes overwrite: false for a key that is already used.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the file $key on $disk. If there is no file with that key, the result is null.

params.name: disk
params.descHtml: The name of a [storage.<name>] block in nvs.toml. That block sets the folder the files are saved in. A tainted value is not allowed here, because the program chooses the disk and user input never does.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name of the file on the disk. It is 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, ., - and _, and it does not start with a .. A / or a \ throws an error, so a key never points into another folder.

doc.returnHtml: The file's bytes, or null if nothing was saved under this key.

errors.descHtml: No [storage.<name>] block with this name sets a root. Or $key is not a valid key. Or the fs.read or fs.write capability does not include the file's path.
The file is there, but it could not be read.

doc.shortHtml: Deletes the file $key from $disk.

params.name: disk
params.descHtml: The name of a [storage.<name>] block in nvs.toml. That block sets the folder the files are saved in. A tainted value is not allowed here, because the program chooses the disk and user input never does.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name of the file on the disk. It is 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, ., - and _, and it does not start with a .. A / or a \ throws an error, so a key never points into another folder.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The file is gone when delete returns.

errors.descHtml: No [storage.<name>] block with this name sets a root. Or $key is not a valid key. Or the fs.read or fs.write capability does not include the file's path.
There is no file with this key, or it could not be deleted. Deleting a missing file throws this error, so a typo in a key is reported.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the keys of the files on $disk, sorted by their bytes. get can read every key in the result.

params.name: disk
params.descHtml: The name of a [storage.<name>] block in nvs.toml. That block sets the folder the files are saved in. A tainted value is not allowed here, because the program chooses the disk and user input never does.

params.name: prefix
params.descHtml: Only keys that start with this text are returned. The default is empty, which returns every key. A prefix that is not empty and not a valid key throws an error, because no key can start with it.

doc.returnHtml: The matching keys, sorted. An empty array if no file matches. Only regular files with a valid key are listed. A folder, a symlink and a file with any other name are not in the result.

errors.descHtml: No [storage.<name>] block with this name sets a root. Or prefix is not empty and not a valid key. Or the fs.read capability does not include the disk's folder.
The disk's folder could not be read. It does not exist, or it is not a folder.

classes.summaryHtml: Saves files by name in a folder that nvs.toml sets up as a disk. put writes a file, get reads it back, delete removes it and list returns the names on the disk. A name is one plain word such as invoice-1042.pdf, never a path.

classes.name: Core\Str
classes.summary:
`string` is guaranteed-valid UTF-8 (`rule:types/bytes`), so **no member takes an
encoding argument** (R13) and there is no `mb_` twin of anything. Indexing granularity — what `length`, `at`
and `slice` count in — is `rule:types/string-is-utf8`'s, not this file's: **extended
grapheme clusters**. Every signature below is written granularity-agnostically, so nothing here changes if
that ADR's own *Revisiting* ever re-opens it.

doc.shortHtml: Which of UAX #15's four normal forms Core\Str::normalize rewrites into — composed or decomposed on one axis, canonical or compatibility on the other.

cases.name: Nfc
cases.descHtml: Canonical composition: é is one code point, and only canonical equivalents are unified — the form to store and compare text in.

cases.name: Nfd
cases.descHtml: Canonical decomposition: é is e plus a combining acute, and only canonical equivalents are unified.

cases.name: Nfkc
cases.descHtml: Compatibility composition: Nfc, and a character that merely renders like another — ﬁ, ① — is unified with it too, which does not round-trip.

cases.name: Nfkd
cases.descHtml: Compatibility decomposition: Nfd, plus the same compatibility unification Nfkc applies.

doc.shortHtml: Counts the graphemes in $s — user-perceived characters, the unit every Core\Str member counts in — so a combining sequence counts once and this is never a byte count.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to measure.

doc.returnHtml: The grapheme count; 0 for the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s is the empty string "". A string of spaces is not empty, and neither is "0".

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to check.

doc.returnHtml: true when $s has no characters, otherwise false.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the one character at position $index of $s. A character is what a person sees as one letter, so "é" is one character. Replaces PHP's mb_substr($s, $i, 1).

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to read from.

params.name: index
params.descHtml: The position of the character. The first character is at 0. A negative position counts from the end, so -1 is the last character.

doc.returnHtml: A string with exactly one character in it.

errors.descHtml: There is no character at $index. The position is at or past the length of $s, counting from either end.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $needle appears anywhere in $haystack. Replaces PHP's str_contains.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The text to search for. The search is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: true when $needle is in $haystack, otherwise false. An empty $needle is in every string, so the result is true.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s starts with $prefix. Replaces PHP's str_starts_with.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to check.

params.name: prefix
params.descHtml: The text $s must start with. The check is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: true when $s starts with $prefix, otherwise false. An empty $prefix is at the start of every string, so the result is true.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s ends with $suffix. Replaces PHP's str_ends_with.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to check.

params.name: suffix
params.descHtml: The text $s must end with. The check is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: true when $s ends with $suffix, otherwise false. An empty $suffix is at the end of every string, so the result is true.

doc.shortHtml: Finds the first place where $needle appears in $haystack and returns its position. The first character is position 0. Replaces PHP's strpos, stripos, mb_strpos and mb_stripos.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The string to search for. An empty needle matches where the search starts.

params.name: from
params.descHtml: The position where the search starts. A negative value counts from the end. The default is 0.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: When true, upper-case and lower-case letters match each other. Each character is compared by its lower-case form, so ß does not match SS. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The position of the first match at or after from, counted in characters as Core\Str::length counts them. You can pass it to Core\Str::slice. The result is null when there is no match.

doc.shortHtml: Finds the last place where $needle appears in $haystack and returns its position. The first character is position 0. Replaces PHP's strrpos, strripos and mb_strrpos.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The string to search for.

params.name: before
params.descHtml: Searches only the characters in front of this position, so a match must end here or earlier. A negative position counts back from the end. The default is the whole string.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: When true, upper-case and lower-case letters count as the same. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The position of the last match, or null when there is none. Matches may overlap, so lastIndexOf("aaa", "aa") returns 1.

doc.shortHtml: Counts how many times $needle appears in $haystack. Replaces PHP's substr_count.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The text to count. The search is case-sensitive. It must not be empty.

doc.returnHtml: The number of times $needle appears, or 0 when it does not appear. Matches do not overlap, so countOf("aaa", "aa") is 1.

errors.descHtml: $needle is empty.

members.name: compare
members.signature: compare(string $a, string $b, {caseInsensitive?: bool, natural?: bool}): int

doc.shortHtml: Compares two strings to sort them. Replaces PHP's strcmp, strcasecmp, strnatcmp and strnatcasecmp.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first string.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The second string.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: When true, upper and lower case letters are equal. ß and SS are still different. The default is false.

params.name: natural
params.descHtml: When true, digits inside the strings are compared as numbers, so "img2" comes before "img12". The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: -1 when $a comes first, 0 when the two are equal, and 1 when $b comes first.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the part of $s that starts at $offset and has $length characters. Positions count characters as a person sees them, so "é" is one character. Replaces PHP's substr and mb_substr.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to take the part from.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: Where the part starts. The first character is at 0. A negative offset counts from the end.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many characters to take. A negative length stops that many characters before the end. null takes everything to the end.

doc.returnHtml: The part as a new string. It is "" when the part is empty or the offset is past the end. $s does not change.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the part of $s before the first $needle, without the needle. With {last: true}, it cuts at the last $needle. Replaces PHP's strstr($s, $needle, true).

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to cut.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The separator to cut at. The search is case-sensitive. The needle is not part of the result.

params.name: last
params.descHtml: When true, cuts at the last needle. The default is false, which cuts at the first one.

doc.returnHtml: The text before the needle. If the needle is not in $s, the result is null. If the needle is at the start, the result is an empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the part of $s after the first $needle, without the needle. With {last: true}, it cuts at the last $needle. Replaces PHP's strstr and strrchr.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to cut.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The separator to cut at. The search is case-sensitive. The needle is not part of the result.

params.name: last
params.descHtml: When true, cuts at the last needle. The default is false, which cuts at the first one.

doc.returnHtml: The text after the needle. If the needle is not in $s, the result is null. If the needle is at the end, the result is an empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Splits $s into parts at every place where $separator is found. Replaces PHP's explode.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to split.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The text to split at. Upper and lower case are different. It must not be empty.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: A positive limit gives at most that many parts. The last part contains the rest of the string. A negative limit deletes that many parts from the end. 0 gives the whole string as one part. The default is no limit.

doc.returnHtml: The parts in order, without the separator. The empty string gives [""]. A negative limit that deletes every part gives [].

errors.descHtml: $separator is empty.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $s into pieces of $size characters each. A piece never cuts a character in half. Replaces PHP's str_split, mb_str_split and chunk_split.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to divide.

params.name: size
params.descHtml: How many characters each piece has. It must be at least 1.

doc.returnHtml: The pieces in order. Only the last piece can be shorter than $size. The result is [] for the empty string.

errors.descHtml: $size is 0.

doc.shortHtml: Splits $s into its lines. A line ends at \n, at \r\n or at \r, on every system. Replaces PHP's explode(PHP_EOL, $s).

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to split.

doc.returnHtml: One string for each line, without its line break. A line break at the very end does not add an empty line. An empty line in the middle is kept as "". An empty string gives [].

doc.shortHtml: Divides $s into its characters, the way a person counts them. An accented letter, a flag or an emoji with a skin tone is one character, even when it is several code points. These are the characters Core\Str::length counts. Replaces PHP's grapheme_str_split.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to divide.

doc.returnHtml: One string for each character, in order. An empty string gives [].

doc.shortHtml: Lists the code points of $s. A code point is the number Unicode gives to one symbol. One character a person sees can be several code points. Replaces PHP's mb_str_split followed by mb_ord.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to read.

doc.returnHtml: One uint for each code point, in order. Each number is between 0 and 0x10FFFF and is never a surrogate. The result is [] for the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Joins the strings in $parts into one string, with $separator between each two neighbouring strings. Replaces PHP's implode.

params.name: parts
params.descHtml: The strings to join, in the order of the array.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The text that goes between two neighbouring strings. The default is the empty string "".

doc.returnHtml: The joined string. An empty array gives "".

members.name: replace
members.signature: replace(string $s, string $search, string $replacement, {caseInsensitive?: bool, limit?: uint}): string

doc.shortHtml: Replaces every occurrence of $search in $s with $replacement. Matches are found from left to right and do not overlap. The new text is not searched again. Replaces PHP's str_replace and str_ireplace.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

params.name: search
params.descHtml: The text to find. An empty $search matches nothing.

params.name: replacement
params.descHtml: The text that replaces each match.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: If true, upper-case and lower-case letters match each other, so "A" finds "a". The default is false.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: The most matches to replace, counted from the left. 0 replaces nothing. The default is every match.

doc.returnHtml: The changed string. If nothing matched, the result is $s unchanged.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces several texts in $s in one call. Each key of $pairs is a text to find, and its value is the text that replaces it. The string is read once, from left to right. Where several keys match at the same place, the longest one is used. The new text is not searched again. Replaces PHP's strtr and str_replace with arrays.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

params.name: pairs
params.descHtml: The replacements. Each key is the text to find, and its value is the text that replaces it. An empty key is ignored.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: If true, upper-case and lower-case letters match each other. If two keys then match the same text, the key written first is used. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The changed string. If $pairs is empty or nothing matched, the result is $s unchanged.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces a part of $s with $replacement. The part is the text Core\Str::slice returns for the same $offset and $length. Replaces PHP's substr_replace.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: The character where the part starts. 0 is the first character. A negative offset counts from the end.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many characters the part has. A negative length stops that many characters before the end. null means the part runs to the end.

params.name: replacement
params.descHtml: The text that replaces the part. "" deletes the part.

doc.returnHtml: The changed string. If the part is empty, for example with a $length of 0, $replacement is inserted at $offset.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the given characters from both ends of $s. Replaces PHP's trim.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.descHtml: The characters to remove, in any order. a..z is the three characters a, . and z. The default is space, tab, newline, carriage return, NUL and vertical tab.

doc.returnHtml: $s without those characters at its start and its end. The middle of $s is not changed.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the given characters from the start of $s. Replaces PHP's ltrim.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.descHtml: The characters to remove, in any order. a..z is the three characters a, . and z. The default is space, tab, newline, carriage return, NUL and vertical tab.

doc.returnHtml: $s without those characters at its start. The rest of $s is not changed.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the given characters from the end of $s. Replaces PHP's rtrim and chop.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.descHtml: The characters to remove, in any order. a..z is the three characters a, . and z. The default is space, tab, newline, carriage return, NUL and vertical tab.

doc.returnHtml: $s without those characters at its end. The rest of $s is not changed.

doc.shortHtml: Adds copies of $padding before $s until the result is $length characters long. Replaces PHP's str_pad with STR_PAD_LEFT.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to pad.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: The length to reach, in characters as a person counts them.

params.name: padding
params.descHtml: The text to add. The last copy is cut short when only part of it fits. The default is one space.

doc.returnHtml: The padded string. If $s already has $length characters or more, it is returned unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $padding is empty and $s is shorter than $length. It is also thrown when the result is larger than this process can hold.

doc.shortHtml: Adds copies of $padding after $s until the result is $length characters long. Replaces PHP's str_pad with STR_PAD_RIGHT.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to pad.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: The length to reach, in characters as a person counts them.

params.name: padding
params.descHtml: The text to add. The last copy is cut short when only part of it fits. The default is one space.

doc.returnHtml: The padded string. If $s already has $length characters or more, it is returned unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $padding is empty and $s is shorter than $length. It is also thrown when the result is larger than this process can hold.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $times copies of $s, joined into one string. Replaces PHP's str_repeat.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to repeat.

params.name: times
params.descHtml: How many copies to write.

doc.returnHtml: The repeated string. It is "" when $times is 0 or $s is empty.

errors.descHtml: The result would be larger than this process can hold.

doc.shortHtml: Reverses the order of the characters in $s. A character is what a person sees as one character, so "café" becomes "éfac" and an accent stays on its letter. Replaces PHP's strrev.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to reverse.

doc.returnHtml: The reversed string. It has the same length as $s. The empty string gives "".

members.name: wrap
members.signature: wrap(string $s, uint $width, {breakWith?: string, cutLongWords?: bool}): string

doc.shortHtml: Splits $s into lines of at most $width characters. It breaks a line at a space and writes breakWith in place of that space. A character is what a person sees as one character, so "é" counts as one. Replaces PHP's wordwrap.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to wrap.

params.name: width
params.descHtml: The longest line, in characters. With 0, every space is a line break.

params.name: breakWith
params.descHtml: The text written at each line break. The default is "\n". Where $s already contains this text, a new line starts there.

params.name: cutLongWords
params.descHtml: With true, a word longer than $width is cut into pieces of $width characters. With false, the default, a long word stays whole on a line of its own.

doc.returnHtml: The wrapped text. A text of at most $width characters is returned unchanged. A result over the memory limit stops the request.

errors.descHtml: breakWith is "", or $width is 0 and cutLongWords is true.

doc.shortHtml: Changes every letter of $s to lower case. It uses Unicode's rules, so ÄRGER becomes ärger. Replaces PHP's strtolower and mb_strtolower.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

doc.returnHtml: The string in lower case. Characters that are not letters do not change. The result can have a different length from $s.

doc.shortHtml: Changes every letter of $s to upper case. It uses Unicode's rules, so straße becomes STRASSE. Replaces PHP's strtoupper and mb_strtoupper.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

doc.returnHtml: The string in upper case. Characters that are not letters do not change. The result can be longer than $s.

doc.shortHtml: Changes the first letter of $s to upper case and keeps the rest as it is. It uses Unicode's rules, so ärger becomes Ärger. Replaces PHP's ucfirst.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string whose first character changes.

doc.returnHtml: The string with its first character in upper case. An empty string gives "".

doc.shortHtml: Changes the first letter of $s to lower case and keeps the rest as it is. It uses Unicode's rules, so Ärger becomes ärger. Replaces PHP's lcfirst.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string whose first character changes.

doc.returnHtml: The string with its first character in lower case. An empty string gives "".

doc.shortHtml: Case-folds $s: every letter changes to one fixed form, so text that differs only in upper and lower case gives the same result. Replaces PHP's mb_convert_case($s, MB_CASE_FOLD).

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to fold.

doc.returnHtml: The folded string. It is a key for comparing, not text to show: ß becomes ss and ﬁ becomes fi. fold("STRASSE") == fold("straße") is true.

doc.shortHtml: Changes $s into one of the four Unicode normal forms. Two ways to write the same text then give the same string. Replaces PHP's Normalizer::normalize.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to normalize.

params.name: form
params.descHtml: Which form to use. Nfc and Nfd keep every character's meaning. Nfkc and Nfkd also replace look-alike characters: ﬁ becomes fi.

doc.returnHtml: The normalized string. Nfc is the form to store and compare text in. A string of ASCII characters is returned unchanged.

doc.shortHtml: Builds a string of one code point. A code point is the number Unicode gives to one symbol. Replaces PHP's mb_chr. To build one byte, as PHP's chr does, use Core\Bytes.

params.name: codePoint
params.descHtml: The number of the symbol. It is at most 0x10FFFF and is not in the surrogate range 0xD800 to 0xDFFF.

doc.returnHtml: A string that contains that one code point. 0x20AC gives "€".

errors.descHtml: $codePoint is above 0x10FFFF, or it is in the surrogate range 0xD800 to 0xDFFF. Unicode gives no symbol to these numbers.

doc.shortHtml: Builds a string from a list of code points, in order. It does the opposite of Core\Str::codePoints. Replaces PHP's mb_chr called on each number and joined with implode.

params.name: codePoints
params.descHtml: The numbers of the symbols, in order. Each one is at most 0x10FFFF and is not in the surrogate range 0xD800 to 0xDFFF.

doc.returnHtml: The string. An empty array gives "".

errors.descHtml: An element is above 0x10FFFF, or it is in the surrogate range 0xD800 to 0xDFFF. No part of the string is returned.

doc.shortHtml: Fills the placeholders in $template with $arguments and returns the text. The template syntax is the one PHP's sprintf uses: %s %d %u %f %e %g %x %X %o %b %%, with flags, a width, a precision and positions such as %1$s. The result never depends on the locale.

params.name: template
params.descHtml: The template. It must be trusted text, so a tainted string is not allowed. When the template is written directly in the code, its placeholders are checked when the program compiles.

params.name: arguments
params.descHtml: The values for the placeholders, in order, or by position with %1$s. Every value must be used by at least one placeholder.

doc.returnHtml: The filled-in text. A width or a precision counts characters, as Core\Str::length does. %f always writes . before the decimals.

errors.descHtml: A placeholder is not valid, the template uses more arguments than were passed, an argument is not used, or a value does not fit its placeholder. For example, %d does not accept an array.
A width or a precision is larger than any string this process can hold. A smaller one that is over the memory limit stops the request.

classes.summaryHtml: string is guaranteed-valid UTF-8 (rule:types/bytes), so no member takes an encoding argument (R13) and there is no mb_ twin of anything. Indexing granularity — what length, at and slice count in — is rule:types/string-is-utf8's, not this file's: extended grapheme clusters. Every signature below is written granularity-agnostically, so nothing here changes if that ADR's own Revisiting ever re-opens it.

classes.name: Core\Taint
classes.summary: A `tainted` value came from outside the program, such as a visitor's request. `assertTrusted()` returns it as a plain `string` after your own check. Each call needs a reason, which says what was checked.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a tainted string as a plain string. Use it only after your own check, when no function made for that one place fits, such as Core\Html::escape.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value your program has checked. A plain string is also allowed, and the result is the same text.

params.name: reason
params.descHtml: What was checked, and why the value can be trusted. It is written for the people who read the code. The program never reads it.

doc.returnHtml: The same text as a plain string. Nothing is escaped or removed. A secret value does not compile here, so call Core\Secret::reveal on it first.

classes.summaryHtml: A tainted value came from outside the program, such as a visitor's request. assertTrusted() returns it as a plain string after your own check. Each call needs a reason, which says what was checked.

classes.name: Core\Task
classes.summary:
Semantics are `rule:concurrency/one-scheduler` — what cancellation does and does
not run, why control never leaves a call with work still running, and the `[deferred]` bound. This section
owns the signatures only. Nothing here needs a capability; it needs the M5 scheduler, which is why it sits
in Part II and lands at **M5** rather than M8.
classes.surface: § 19 below — `all`, `map`, `afterResponse`

members.name: all
members.signature: all({name: callable, …} $tasks, {limit?: uint, deadline?: Duration}): {name: T, …}

doc.shortHtml: Runs every function in the $tasks object at the same time, and waits until all of them have finished. The result is an object with the same field names, and each field has the type its function returns.

params.name: tasks
params.descHtml: An object whose fields are anonymous functions with no parameters, such as {a: fn (): int => 1}. Write them directly in the call. A variable of type callable in a field does not compile.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: The most tasks that run at the same time. The other tasks wait until one finishes. Without it, every task starts at once.

params.name: deadline
params.descHtml: The time limit for the whole call, not for each task. Without it, the request's [limits] wall_time setting is the limit.

doc.returnHtml: An object with the value each function returned. No task is still running when the call returns. If a task throws an error, the other tasks are stopped, and the call throws that same error.

errors.descHtml: When limit is 0. No task could start, so the call could never finish.
When deadline runs out before every task has finished. Every task is stopped first, and the call waits until they have stopped.

members.name: map
members.signature: map(array<T> $items, callable(T, string): U $fn, {limit?: uint, deadline?: Duration}): array<U>

doc.shortHtml: Calls $fn once for each element of $items, and runs the calls at the same time. The result has the same keys in the same order as $items, whichever call finishes first.

params.name: items
params.descHtml: The array. Each element is given to $fn in a task of its own.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: The function to call. It gets ($value, $key), and it may declare only $value. The key is always a string. Its return type is the type of each element of the result.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: The most tasks that run at the same time. The other tasks wait until one finishes. Without it, every task starts at once.

params.name: deadline
params.descHtml: The time limit for the whole call, not for each task. Without it, the request's [limits] wall_time setting is the limit.

doc.returnHtml: An array with what $fn returned for each element, under the element's own key. An empty $items gives an empty array. No task is still running when the call returns. If a task throws an error, the other tasks are stopped, and the call throws that same error.

errors.descHtml: When limit is 0. No task could start, so the call could never finish.
When deadline runs out before every task has finished. Every task is stopped first, and the call waits until they have stopped.

doc.shortHtml: Runs $fn after the response is sent, so the client does not wait for it. Use it for receipts, webhooks and audit logs. The work is not saved anywhere: if the process stops, the work is lost and nothing tries it again.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: The function to run. It takes no arguments, and its return value is ignored. An error it throws is written to the log, and no catch in the request sees it.

params.name: deadline
params.descHtml: The longest time $fn may run. Without it, the [deferred] deadline setting is the limit. The request's [limits] wall_time does not apply here, but its other [limits] settings do.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The functions run one at a time, in the order you added them. They do not run if the request ends with an uncaught error, an exit or a fatal error.

errors.descHtml: When the call is made inside a task that Core\Task::all, Core\Task::map or afterResponse started. Only the request itself may call it, so return the work to the request and call afterResponse there.

classes.summaryHtml: Semantics are rule:concurrency/one-scheduler — what cancellation does and does not run, why control never leaves a call with work still running, and the [deferred] bound. This section owns the signatures only. Nothing here needs a capability; it needs the M5 scheduler, which is why it sits in Part II and lands at M5 rather than M8.
classes.surfaceHtml: § 19 below — all, map, afterResponse

classes.name: Core\Task\Channel
classes.summary: A queue with a fixed size that sends values from one task to another. `send` waits while the queue is full, and a `foreach` loop over the channel receives the values.

doc.shortHtml: Queues $value for the consuming task, suspending the calling task for as long as the channel is full.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to hand across.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing, once the value is queued; a send on a closed channel is a fatal error, which no catch sees.

doc.shortHtml: Ends the stream, so that a consumer's foreach finishes once the queued values are drained.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing; values sent before the close are still delivered, and closing twice changes nothing.

classes.summaryHtml: A queue with a fixed size that sends values from one task to another. send waits while the queue is full, and a foreach loop over the channel receives the values.

classes.name: Core\Test
classes.surface: the assertions, each ending in a `{message?: string}` bag: `assertSame<T>(T $actual, T $expected)`, `assertEquals<T>(T $actual, T $expected)`, `assertEqualsDeep<T>(T $actual, T $expected)`, `assertTrue(bool $actual)`, `assertNull(mixed $actual)`, `assertCount<T>(array<T> $actual, uint $expected)`, `assertContains<T>(array<T> $actual, T $expected)`, `assertMatchesInline(mixed $actual, string $expected)`, `assertThrows(callable(): mixed $body, string $expected)`, `assertDoesNotThrow(callable(): mixed $body)` and `assertCompletes(callable(): mixed $body, {within: Time\Duration} $settings)`; `expectFailure(callable(): mixed $body): void`, which passes when `$body` fails an assertion. Doubles: `double<T>(object $answers): T`, `partial<T>(T $real, object $answers): T`, `assertCalled(object $double, method $method, {times?: uint, with?: array<mixed>, message?: string})` and `assertNeverCalled(object $double, method $method, {message?: string})`. The clock and the `Core\Cli` prompts: `advance(Time\Duration $by): void` and `scriptAnswers(array<string> $answers): void`. The program's own routes: `request(Http\Method $method, string $path, {headers?: array<string>, body?: string|bytes, mount?: string, captures?: array<string>}): Core\Test\Response` — one in-process request against the `#[Route]` table — and `serverUrl(): ?string`. Outbound calls: `answerHttp(string $url, uint $status, {json?: mixed, body?: string|bytes, headers?: array<string|array<string>>, tls?: Http\TlsInfo}): void`, `tlsSession({version?, cipher?, verified?, subject?, issuer?, expiry?}): Http\TlsInfo`, `sentHttp(): array<Core\Test\SentRequest>`, `answerSocket(string $url, array<string|bytes> $frames, {protocol?: string}): void` and `sentSocket(): array<Socket\Message>`. Every assertion is subject-first and generic where it compares

doc.shortHtml: Asserts $actual is identical to $expected — two objects are the same object and nothing else is — as PHPUnit's assertSame does, subject first.

params.name: actual
params.descHtml: The value under test.

params.name: expected
params.descHtml: What it must be identical to; T is bound from $actual, so a type mismatch between the two is a compile error.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: A prefix written in front of the failure's own diagnosis; the default is none.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the assertion is recorded as held in the test's ledger.

errors.descHtml: The two are not identical; the failure is recorded in the ledger before it is thrown, so a catch cannot erase it.

doc.shortHtml: Asserts $actual equals $expected — identity everywhere except two objects, which are compared through Comparable::compareTo — as PHPUnit's assertEquals does, subject first.

params.name: actual
params.descHtml: The value under test.

params.name: expected
params.descHtml: What it must equal; T is bound from $actual, so a type mismatch between the two is a compile error.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: A prefix written in front of the failure's own diagnosis; the default is none.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the assertion is recorded as held in the test's ledger.

errors.descHtml: The two are not equal; the failure is recorded in the ledger before it is thrown, so a catch cannot erase it.
Both are objects and $actual's class declares no compareTo.

doc.shortHtml: Asserts $actual and $expected agree structurally — arrays entry by entry, objects property by property, everything else by identity — and reports where they first differ rather than only that they do.

params.name: actual
params.descHtml: The value under test.

params.name: expected
params.descHtml: What it must agree with everywhere; T is bound from $actual, so a type mismatch between the two is a compile error.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: A prefix written in front of the failure's own diagnosis; the default is none.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the assertion is recorded as held in the test's ledger.

errors.descHtml: The two differ somewhere; the diagnosis names the path, written as a program would subscript $actual, and the failure is recorded in the ledger before it is thrown.
The walk passed 64 levels of containment without reaching a scalar.

doc.shortHtml: Checks that $actual is true. The value must be a bool, so a call with a number or a string does not compile.

params.name: actual
params.descHtml: The bool to check.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: Your own text, added at the start of the failure message. The default is no text.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The check is recorded as passed.

errors.descHtml: $actual is false. The failure is recorded before it is thrown, so a catch does not remove it from the test's result.

doc.shortHtml: Asserts $actual is null, as PHPUnit's assertNull does; the subject is mixed, so a value of any type may be asked.

params.name: actual
params.descHtml: The value under test.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: A prefix written in front of the failure's own diagnosis; the default is none.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the assertion is recorded as held in the test's ledger.

errors.descHtml: $actual is not null; the failure is recorded in the ledger before it is thrown, so a catch cannot erase it.

doc.shortHtml: Asserts $actual holds exactly $expected entries — Core\Arr::count's own signature — as PHPUnit's assertCount does, subject first. A string's length is asserted through Core\Str::length, which says which length was meant.

params.name: actual
params.descHtml: The array under test.

params.name: expected
params.descHtml: The number of entries it must hold.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: A prefix written in front of the failure's own diagnosis; the default is none.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the assertion is recorded as held in the test's ledger.

errors.descHtml: The array holds a different number of entries; the failure is recorded in the ledger before it is thrown, so a catch cannot erase it.

doc.shortHtml: Asserts some entry of $actual is $expected under strict identity — the question Core\Arr::contains answers, and the same answer — as PHPUnit's assertContains does, subject first. A substring is asserted through Core\Str::contains, which says which containment was meant.

params.name: actual
params.descHtml: The array under test.

params.name: expected
params.descHtml: The entry it must hold, compared by identity; int, uint, float and decimal are one numeric domain, so 1 finds 1.0.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: A prefix written in front of the failure's own diagnosis; the default is none.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the assertion is recorded as held in the test's ledger.

errors.descHtml: No entry of the array is identical to $expected; the failure is recorded in the ledger before it is thrown, so a catch cannot erase it.

doc.shortHtml: Asserts that $actual, rendered as Core\Debug::render renders it, is exactly $expected. This is an inline snapshot: the expected text is a string written in the test itself, not a file beside it.

params.name: actual
params.descHtml: The value to render; a secret property inside it renders redacted, so a snapshot cannot become where a secret is committed.

params.name: expected
params.descHtml: The rendering this value is expected to have, written inline; nvs test --update writes it here for you. It replaces this string and nothing else in the file.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: A prefix written in front of the failure's own diagnosis; the default is none.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the assertion is recorded as held in the test's ledger.

errors.descHtml: The rendering differs from $expected; the failure quotes both, and is recorded in the ledger before it is thrown, so a catch cannot erase it.

doc.shortHtml: Runs $body and asserts it throws $expected or a subclass of it, as PHPUnit's expectException does; the throw it judged is consumed, so only the assertion's own verdict propagates.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The function to run; a value it returns is released.

params.name: expected
params.descHtml: The fully-qualified class name, as ParseError::class folds to; the thrown class or any ancestor of it matches.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: A prefix written in front of the failure's own diagnosis; the default is none.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the assertion is recorded as held in the test's ledger. A FATAL or an exit from the body is nobody's assertion to judge and propagates unchanged, and a failed assertion inside the body keeps its own ledger entry.

errors.descHtml: $body returned without throwing, or threw a class that is not $expected — reported with the class it did throw and that throw's message; the failure is recorded in the ledger before it is thrown.

doc.shortHtml: Runs $body and asserts it returns without throwing — the way out of the rule that a test asserting nothing fails; the throw it judged is consumed, so only the assertion's own verdict propagates.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The function to run; a value it returns is released.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: A prefix written in front of the failure's own diagnosis; the default is none.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the assertion is recorded as held in the test's ledger. A FATAL or an exit from the body is nobody's assertion to judge and propagates unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $body threw — a failed assertion inside it included, which keeps its own ledger entry — reported with the throw's message; the failure is recorded in the ledger before it is thrown.

doc.shortHtml: Runs $body and checks that a check inside it failed. Those failures then no longer count against the test. Use it to test a check you wrote yourself.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The function to run. A failed check counts even when $body catches the Core\Test\Failure itself.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The failed checks inside $body are removed from the test's result, and the Core\Test\Failure it threw is caught. The checks that passed still count.

errors.descHtml: No check inside $body failed. This failure is recorded before it is thrown, so a catch does not remove it from the test's result.

doc.shortHtml: Moves the clock that #[Test(at: ...)] fixed forward by $by. A test of something that expires can then check the time after it expires, without waiting.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: How far to move the clock. A negative duration moves it back.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The next Core\Time::now() returns the moved time.

errors.descHtml: The running test has no at:, so there is no fixed clock to move. The real clock of the computer is never moved.
The moved time is outside the range a clock can show, about the years -9999 to 9999. The clock does not move.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the address of the test server that a #[Test(server: true)] test starts. The server runs on this computer, on a free port. Use it when a test needs a real network connection.
doc.returnHtml: An address such as http://127.0.0.1:52341, with no / at the end, so you can add a path directly. The result is null everywhere else, which includes a test without server: true and a program started with nvs run.

doc.shortHtml: Gives the answers for the next Core\Cli prompts, so you can test a program that asks questions. Each prompt takes the first answer that is still waiting. It does not read the terminal.

params.name: answers
params.descHtml: One answer per prompt, in the order the program asks. Write what a person would type, without the line ending. A select reads the number of a choice, and a confirm reads y or n.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A second call adds its answers after the ones still waiting. When no answer is left, a prompt returns its default or throws Core\Cli\NotInteractive.

members.name: request
members.signature: request(Core\Http\Method $method, string $path, {headers?: array<string>, body?: string|bytes, mount?: string, captures?: array<string>}): Core\Test\Response

doc.shortHtml: Sends one request to your own program and returns the answer. It opens no network connection. The request goes through the same route table and the same code as a real request.

params.name: method
params.descHtml: The HTTP method of the request, such as Core\Http\Method::Get.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path of the request, such as /orders/7. A ? and the text after it are the query string.

params.name: headers
params.descHtml: The headers of the request, with the header name as the key. If you give no content-type or content-length, the length is set from body.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The body of the request, as a string or as bytes. If you give no body, the request has no body. An empty string is a body of length 0.

params.name: mount
params.descHtml: The prefix the program is served under, such as /shop. Core\Request::mount() returns it, and Core\Router::url adds it in front of each link. The default is "", which means the root.

params.name: captures
params.descHtml: The parts of the prefix that the mount's pattern matched, in order. For the pattern /shops/{1} and mount: "/shops/acme", this is ["acme"]. Core\Request::mount()->captures() returns this list. The default is an empty list. You need mount to give captures.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Test\Response. status() returns the status the program set, or 200 if it set none. body() returns the text the program wrote, and json() and jsonAs() decode it. header(), headers() and cookies() return the headers and cookies the program set. A path that no route matches still gets an answer, because your program decides what to do with it.

errors.descHtml: captures is not empty and mount is "". The root has no pattern, so it has no captures. captures is also an error when it is not a list.
There is no program to answer, because the call is not in nvs test or nvs run. The call is also an error inside a request that request sent, because a request cannot send another request.

members.name: answerHttp
members.signature: answerHttp(string $url, uint $status, {json?: mixed, body?: string|bytes, headers?: array<string|array<string>>, tls?: Core\Http\TlsInfo}): void

doc.shortHtml: Says what one outbound URL answers with, and takes this test off the network — from the first answer registered, every Core\Http\Client call the test makes is served from the table and none of them connects.

params.name: url
params.descHtml: The URL this answer serves: the whole of it, or a prefix ending in *. Nothing is resolved and no host is looked up — this is the text a call's own URL is compared against.

params.name: status
params.descHtml: The status the call answers with, as a wire status line can write it: three digits, 100 to 999.

params.name: json
params.descHtml: A value the answer carries as a JSON document, written exactly as Core\Json::encode would write it. The answer declares application/json for it unless the headers bag names a content type itself.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The body the answer carries, for a reply that is not a JSON document — text, or the octets of a reply that is not text at all, which is what Core\Http\Response::bytes reads back and ::text refuses. An answer may name this or json and not both.

params.name: headers
params.descHtml: The headers the answer carries, keyed by name — the same shape Core\Http\Options writes a request's headers in, plus one arm it has no use for: an array of strings under a name is a reply that carried that field on that many lines, which is what Core\Http\Response::headers reads back. A name is matched case-insensitively, as a header name is.

params.name: tls
params.descHtml: The TLS session the reply reports, from Core\Test::tlsSession. Core\Http\Response::tls returns it for every call this answer serves. Without it, tls() returns null.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. Answers accumulate, so a test registers as many as it has calls; a URL answered exactly wins over one answered by a prefix, and the longest prefix wins among prefixes.

errors.descHtml: The answer names both json and body, which are two spellings of one body; the status is not one a status line can carry; or the answer gives a tls session to an http:// URL, which has none.

members.name: tlsSession
members.signature: tlsSession({version?: string, cipher?: string, verified?: bool, subject?: string, issuer?: string, expiry?: Core\Time\Instant}): Core\Http\TlsInfo

doc.shortHtml: Builds a TLS session for a test, with a real certificate chain, so a test can read a Core\Http\TlsInfo without a network.

params.name: version
params.descHtml: TLSv1.3 or TLSv1.2. The default is TLSv1.3.

params.name: cipher
params.descHtml: A cipher suite this build supports for that version, under its IANA name. The default is TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 for TLS 1.3 and TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 for TLS 1.2.

params.name: verified
params.descHtml: What verified() returns. The default is true.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The leaf certificate's subject, written as subject() returns it: KEY=value pairs such as CN=api.example.com, O=Shop, with the keys CN, O, OU, C, ST and L. The default is CN=example.com.

params.name: issuer
params.descHtml: The subject of the CA certificate that signs the leaf, which is what issuer() returns. Written like subject. The default is CN=Novis Test CA.

params.name: expiry
params.descHtml: When the leaf certificate expires, in whole seconds. The default is 90 days after Core\Time::now(), so a test with a fixed clock gets the same value every run.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Http\TlsInfo. Its peerChain() has two certificates: the leaf, then the CA that signed it. Pass it to Core\Test::answerHttp as tls to make a faked reply report it.

errors.descHtml: The version is not TLSv1.3 or TLSv1.2; the cipher is not one this build supports for that version; a subject or issuer is not written as KEY=value pairs with the keys above; or the expiry is before 1950 or after 9999.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every HTTP request the program sent after the first Core\Test::answerHttp call. The oldest request comes first.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Test\SentRequest for each request, in the order the program sent them. The list is empty when the program sent nothing. Nothing in a request is tainted, because the program wrote all of it.

doc.shortHtml: Scripts the peer one outbound WebSocket URL answers with, and takes this test off the network — a socket opened to a matching URL completes its handshake without connecting, receives these frames in order and then a close.

params.name: url
params.descHtml: The URL this peer answers: the whole of it, or a prefix ending in *. Nothing is resolved and no host is looked up — this is the text Core\Http\Client::openSocket's own URL is compared against, and it is still judged for its scheme, so a https URL scripted here is refused at the row that opens it.

params.name: frames
params.descHtml: What the peer sends, in order: a string is a text message and bytes is a binary one, which is the same pair send and sendBytes write. A socket that has taken the last of them reads null from receive, which is the peer having closed.

params.name: protocol
params.descHtml: The subprotocol this peer's 101 chooses. It has to be one the call offered in protocols, and a peer choosing a name that was never offered makes openSocket throw — which is the refusal a real peer would meet. Left out, the handshake chooses none.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. Peers accumulate, so a test scripts as many as it opens sockets; a URL answered exactly wins over one answered by a prefix, and the longest prefix wins among prefixes. Two sockets opened to one URL each read that peer's frames from their own position.

doc.shortHtml: Every frame the program under test has sent over a scripted socket, oldest first — what it said, rather than what it was told.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Socket\Message per frame, in the order the program sent them, with text filled for a send and bytes for a sendBytes. The frames of two sockets open at once arrive interleaved in the one order they were written in, so a test that needs them apart scripts one peer at a time.

doc.shortHtml: A stand-in for T built from an object of functions, one per method. It is a T and may be passed wherever one is taken.

params.name: answers
params.descHtml: One field per method of T, with the same name as the method. Each field has the function that answers that method. A field for a method that T does not declare does not compile. A method of T that has no field does not compile either.

doc.returnHtml: The double, typed as T. It records every call made to it, which Core\Test::assertCalled reads afterwards, and no class the author never wrote appears in a backtrace.

errors.descHtml: T declares more methods than one double can stand in for, which is a fixed ceiling set well above the interfaces a test doubles.

doc.shortHtml: A stand-in for T that answers the methods $answers names and delegates every other one to $real.

params.name: real
params.descHtml: The implementation the un-overridden methods are forwarded to, receiver and arguments unchanged.

params.name: answers
params.descHtml: One field per method being overridden, named as the method is. A field T declares no method for is refused where the call is written; unlike double, a method left out is not, that being what $real is for.

doc.returnHtml: The partial, typed as T. Every call is recorded, whether the function in $answers or $real answered it.

errors.descHtml: double's ceiling, for the same reason and with the same two counts.

members.name: assertCalled
members.signature: assertCalled(object $double, method $method, {times?: uint, with?: array<mixed>, message?: string}): void

doc.shortHtml: Asserts that $method was called on $double — after the exercise, against the record the double kept, rather than as an expectation declared in advance.

params.name: double
params.descHtml: The double or partial the call is being asserted about.

params.name: method
params.descHtml: The method, written as Mailer::send — a compile-checked reference, so renaming the method updates or breaks the test.

params.name: times
params.descHtml: The exact number of calls expected. Omitted, any number above zero holds.

params.name: with
params.descHtml: The arguments one of the recorded calls must have been made with, compared as Core\Test::assertEquals compares. Omitted, the arguments are not looked at.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: Prefixed to the failure, as on every other assertion.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A call that was not made, or was made a different number of times or with different arguments, throws.

errors.descHtml: The record does not hold the call the options describe. The message names the method, what was expected of it and every call the record does hold.
$double is an ordinary object rather than something Core\Test::double or Core\Test::partial built, so there is no record to read.

doc.shortHtml: Asserts that $method was never called on $double — assertCalled's other half, over the same record.

params.name: double
params.descHtml: The double or partial the absence is being asserted about.

params.name: method
params.descHtml: The method, written as Mailer::purge and checked as assertCalled's is.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: Prefixed to the failure, as on every other assertion.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. One recorded call is enough to throw.

errors.descHtml: The method was called. The message names the first call the record holds and how many it holds in all.
assertCalled's, for the same reason: $double is not a double.

doc.shortHtml: Runs $body with the test's clock advanced by $settings.within, and asserts that it left nothing still running. Wall-clock time is never read, so a budget written in seconds is spent in microseconds and two runs answer identically.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The work to run. It is called once, on the test's own task, and whatever it answers is dropped.

params.name: settings
params.descHtml: The time budget. You must always give it, because no default duration fits every caller.

shape.descHtml: How far the virtual clock moves before $body runs, so a retry, a backoff or a timeout inside it elapses at once. Core\Test::advance moves the same clock, and the move is permanent: the test reads the advanced clock from here on.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: Prefixed to the failure, as on every other assertion.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A $body that returned having left a task of its own still running throws, naming the budget it overran — rule:testing/task-tree-and-virtual-clock, read at the one moment it means anything.

errors.descHtml: $body returned with work of its own still running. The message names how many tasks and the within they were given.
The test declared no at:, so there is no fixed clock to spend the budget against — Core\Test::advance's refusal, for its reason.
The advanced clock lies outside the range an Instant can hold, as on Core\Test::advance.

classes.surface: what `Core\Test::request` returns: `status(): uint`, `body(): string`, `header(string $name): ?string`, `headers(): array<array<string>>`, `cookies(): array<string>`, `json({maxDepth?: uint}): mixed` and `jsonAs<T>({maxDepth?: uint}): T`, the last two reading the body as `Core\Request::json` and `::jsonAs` do

doc.shortHtml: Returns the HTTP status code of the answer to this request.
doc.returnHtml: The code the program set with Core\Response::setStatus. If the program set no code, the result is 200. If the program threw an error it did not catch, the result is 500, the same code the server sends.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the text the program wrote while it answered this request.
doc.returnHtml: Everything the program wrote with echo, in order. If the program wrote nothing, the result is an empty string. If the program threw an error it did not catch, the result is also an empty string, because the server sends no body for a failed request.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of one header of the answer, by its name.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The name of the header. Upper and lower case do not matter, so Content-Type and content-type are the same header.

doc.returnHtml: The value, exactly as the program set it. The result is null when the answer has no header of that name. When the answer has the header on more than one line, the values are joined with , in order. The answer always has a Content-Type header. If the program set none, its value is text/html; charset=utf-8, the same as the server sends. A request that failed has no headers.

errors.descHtml: The name is Set-Cookie. Two cookies joined into one string are not a cookie, so cookies() and headers() read that header.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every header of the answer, grouped by name.
doc.returnHtml: An array<array<string>>. Each key is a header name in lower case. Its value is a list with one entry for each line of that header, in order. Set-Cookie has one line for each cookie. A request that failed returns an empty array.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the cookies the program set in this answer, by name.
doc.returnHtml: An array<string>. Each key is a cookie name and each value is the cookie value, exactly as the program set it. Nothing is decoded. Attributes such as Path and HttpOnly are not in the result, and headers()["set-cookie"] returns the whole lines. When the program set one name twice, the result has the last value. A cookie that the program deleted is in the result with an empty value. The array is empty when the program set no cookie.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the body of the answer as one JSON document and returns the decoded value.

params.name: maxDepth
params.descHtml: How deep the document may nest. The default is 512, and the value must be from 1 to 1024. A document with no array or object in it has depth 1.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded value, the same as Core\Json::decode returns for the body. A JSON object becomes an array with string keys. Every call decodes the body again and returns the same value.

errors.descHtml: maxDepth is not from 1 to 1024.
The body is not one whole JSON document, or it nests deeper than maxDepth. An empty body throws this error too. The Content-Type header is not checked.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the body of the answer as one JSON object and returns a new instance of the class T. The class needs #[Core\Json\Derive]. Write array<T> to read a JSON array with one object for each element.

params.name: maxDepth
params.descHtml: How deep the document may nest. The default is 512, and the value must be from 1 to 1024. A document with no array or object in it has depth 1.

doc.returnHtml: A new T with its fields read from the body, or one T for each element for an array<T>. Every call creates new objects.

errors.descHtml: T has no #[Core\Json\Derive] attribute. Or maxDepth is not from 1 to 1024.

The body is not one whole JSON object, or it nests deeper than maxDepth. An empty body throws this error too. It is also thrown when a field is missing or has the wrong type. The issues list has one entry for each wrong field. The Content-Type header is not checked.
The call stack is full before the last object is created. This can happen when a class contains itself and the body nests very deeply.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the HTTP method of this request.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Http\Method case. A request sent with Core\Http\Client::get returns Core\Http\Method::Get, a request sent with Core\Http\Client::post returns Core\Http\Method::Post, and the other methods work the same way.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the URL of this request, exactly as the program wrote it.
doc.returnHtml: The whole URL, with its path and query string. It is not the pattern you gave to Core\Test::answerHttp, so a test can check the exact path the program used.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The header name. Upper and lower case letters do not matter, so authorization and Authorization find the same header.

doc.returnHtml: The header value. If the request has no header with this name, the result is null.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the body of this request, such as the JSON document or the form the program sent.
doc.returnHtml: The body as bytes. If the request has no body, the result is empty bytes. Use as string to read it as text.

classes.name: Core\Time
classes.summary:
PHP has ~40 `date_*` procedural functions that are aliases of `DateTime` methods, *and* a
`DateTime`/`DateTimeImmutable` mutable/immutable pair. Both duplications are gone (R17, R20): there are
objects only, and every one is immutable. There is **no ambient timezone** — no process default, no
per-request default — so a `Zone` is an explicit argument at every instant↔calendar conversion.

**Two arithmetics, and the type says which one you get.** An `Instant` moves by a `Duration`, which is an
exact count of nanoseconds; a `DateTime` moves by a count of a `Unit`, which is a calendar step that a DST
boundary or a short month can make longer or shorter than its nominal length. `Time::now()->plus(72h)` and
`Time::now()->in($zone)->plus(3, Unit::Day)` are different operations, and PHP's `"+3 days"` is ambiguous
between them. There is no relative-expression string anywhere in this class: everything `strtotime` spells
is a typed call, and `rule:types/duration`'s `72h`/`30d` literal is what keeps them
short.

doc.shortHtml: A day of the week, Monday first as ISO 8601 and date("N") order them — what $d->weekday() answers and next/previous take. The order is theirs and the numbering is not: the cases are zero-based, Monday as int is 0 and Sunday is 6, where date("N") numbers that same order 1 through 7.

enums.name: Unit
enums.raw: Unit { Nanosecond, Microsecond, Millisecond, Second, Minute, Hour, Day, Week, Month, Quarter, Year }

doc.shortHtml: The calendar step a DateTime, Date or TimeOfDay moves by, and the unit startOf, endOf and difference count in — the half of § 4's two arithmetics a DST boundary or a short month can lengthen or shorten, listed smallest first.

cases.name: Nanosecond
cases.descHtml: One nanosecond, the finest step any value here resolves.

cases.name: Microsecond
cases.descHtml: One microsecond — 1000 nanoseconds.

cases.name: Millisecond
cases.descHtml: One millisecond — 1 000 000 nanoseconds.

cases.name: Second
cases.descHtml: One second of the civil clock.

cases.name: Minute
cases.descHtml: One minute of the civil clock.

cases.name: Hour
cases.descHtml: One hour of the civil clock.

cases.name: Day
cases.descHtml: One calendar day — 23 or 25 hours where the zone crosses a DST boundary.

cases.name: Week
cases.descHtml: Seven calendar days; startOf(Unit::Week) is the Monday, ISO 8601's first day.

cases.name: Month
cases.descHtml: One calendar month, with the day-of-month clamped to the target month's length.

cases.name: Quarter
cases.descHtml: Three calendar months, so plus(1, Unit::Quarter) is plus(3, Unit::Month) and startOf lands on January, April, July or October.

cases.name: Year
cases.descHtml: One calendar year, with 29 February clamped to the 28th where the target has none.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the current time from the system clock. It replaces PHP's time, microtime and date_create. Use ->in($zone) to get the date and time of day in a zone.
doc.returnHtml: The current Instant, to the nanosecond.

doc.shortHtml: Reads a clock that only moves forward, for measuring how long something takes. It replaces PHP's hrtime. Subtract two readings to get the time between them.
doc.returnHtml: A Duration since a fixed starting point. A later reading is never smaller than an earlier one.

doc.shortHtml: Waits for $d, replacing sleep, usleep, time_nanosleep and time_sleep_until — parking the task rather than blocking the core, so a neighbour on the same core runs meanwhile; a request cancelled mid-sleep stops here.

params.name: d
params.descHtml: How long to wait; zero or negative returns at once.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

doc.shortHtml: Builds the instant at a Unix timestamp, replacing DateTime::setTimestamp; the nanos option is added after the second, so -1 with {nanos: 1} is one nanosecond after -1, not before it.

params.name: seconds
params.descHtml: Whole seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z; negative before it.

params.name: nanos
params.descHtml: Nanoseconds to add on top of the second, below 1000000000; the default is 0.

doc.returnHtml: The Instant.

errors.descHtml: nanos is not below 1000000000, or $seconds is outside -377705023201..=253402207200. That is the time from -9999-01-02T01:59:59Z to 9999-12-30T22:00:00Z.

doc.shortHtml: Reads an ISO-8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp that carries its own offset — 2024-03-01T12:00:00Z, 2024-03-01T13:00:00+01:00 — which is all of strtotime and DateTime::__construct that survives: a civil time with no offset is Time::parse with a zone, and a relative expression is a typed call.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The timestamp text, with a date, a time and a Z or ±HH:MM offset.

doc.returnHtml: The Instant the text names.

errors.descHtml: $text is not such a timestamp, with the component it stopped at named. It is also thrown for a time outside -9999-01-02T01:59:59Z..=9999-12-30T22:00:00Z.

doc.shortHtml: Reads a civil date and time through a CLDR pattern and places it in $zone, replacing DateTime::createFromFormat and strptime. A $format written directly in the code is checked when the program compiles, and a malformed one is error E0769. A field the pattern does not name is left at the start of its range.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The text to read; it stays data, so nothing of it carries a qualifier into the answer.

params.name: format
params.descHtml: A CLDR pattern of civil fields only — yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm — since the zone is $zone; a grammar, so a tainted one is refused.

params.name: zone
params.descHtml: The zone the civil fields are read in; a time the zone skips resolves forward past the gap.

doc.returnHtml: The DateTime in $zone.

errors.descHtml: $format does not compile — a field letter outside the implemented subset, an unterminated quote — or names a zone or offset field, which $zone already answers. For a $format written directly in the code, only the first half is E0769: a zonal field is a pattern the grammar reads perfectly well and a rule of this member's own, so it throws however $format arrived.

$text does not match $format: fixed text that differs, a field with no digits, trailing text, or fields that together are not a real civil time. It is also thrown for a time outside -9999-01-02T01:59:59Z..=9999-12-30T22:00:00Z.

members.name: at
members.signature: at(int $year, uint $month, uint $day, Zone $zone, {hour?, minute?, second?, nanos?}): DateTime

doc.shortHtml: Builds a civil date and time in $zone from its fields, replacing mktime, gmmktime and DateTime::setDate; the clock fields default to midnight, and a time the zone skips — 02:30 on a spring-forward morning — resolves forward rather than throwing.

params.name: year
params.descHtml: The year, within -9999..=9999. The time as a whole must also lie between -9999-01-02T01:59:59Z and 9999-12-30T22:00:00Z.

params.name: month
params.descHtml: The month, 1 to 12.

params.name: day
params.descHtml: The day of the month, which must exist in that month.

params.name: zone
params.descHtml: The zone the fields are read in.

params.name: hour
params.descHtml: The hour, 0 to 23; the default is 0.

params.name: minute
params.descHtml: The minute, 0 to 59; the default is 0.

params.name: second
params.descHtml: The second, 0 to 59; the default is 0.

params.name: nanos
params.descHtml: The subsecond nanoseconds, below 1000000000; the default is 0.

doc.returnHtml: The DateTime in $zone.

errors.descHtml: A field is outside its range, the fields together are not a date that exists — 30 February — which is what checkdate used to answer, or the time lies past either end of the range $year names.

doc.shortHtml: Builds a zone-free civil date from its three fields — the one place a date that does not exist throws, which is why there is no checkdate.

params.name: y

params.name: m

doc.returnHtml: The Date.

errors.descHtml: A field is outside its range, or the three together are not a date that exists.

doc.shortHtml: Renders the date through a CLDR pattern of date fields — yyyy-MM-dd, EEEE, d MMMM yyyy — the same grammar DateTime::format takes, narrowed to what a date carries.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A CLDR pattern naming only calendar fields; a grammar, so a tainted one is refused.

doc.returnHtml: The rendered text.
